definition: to give up completely; to desert; to yield oneself to an emotion; freedom from restraint or inhibition
chinese: v. 放棄；拋棄；放縱（情感）；n. 放縱；恣意
example: He had such a headache that he was forced to abandon the meeting.

definition: to lower in rank, prestige, or dignity; to degrade or humble
chinese: 貶低；降低（地位或尊嚴）；使卑下
example: You cannot abase someone who has no shame.

definition: to make embarrassed or ashamed; to make self-conscious
chinese: 使羞愧；使尷尬；使侷促不安
example: In this context, “abash” means cause to be embarrassed; cause to feel self-conscious.

definition: to become or make less intense; to reduce in amount or value; (law) to put an end to
chinese: 減弱；緩和；減少；降低；（法律）廢除
example: This action would not have been sufficient to abate the odor nuisance.

definition: to shorten a word or phrase; to make briefer; to cut short
chinese: 縮寫；縮短；刪節
example: In this context, “abbreviate” means shorten.

definition: to formally give up a throne or power; to fail to fulfill a responsibility
chinese: 退位；放棄（權力或責任）；卸責
example: The king was forced to abdicate.

definition: deviating from the normal or usual course; atypical
chinese: 異常的；偏離常規的；反常的
example: Only individuals with an aberrant temperament can in the long run retain their self-esteem in the face of the disesteem of their fellows.

definition: a departure from what is normal or expected; a mental lapse; (optics) distortion of an image
chinese: 偏離常規；異常；失常；（光學）像差
example: Such a sanction is an inconceivable aberration in the application of international law.

definition: to encourage or assist someone, especially in wrongdoing
chinese: 教唆；煽動；協助（犯罪）
example: It's illegal to aid and abet another person in committing a felony.

definition: a state of temporary inactivity or suspension
chinese: 中止；擱置；暫緩
example: I'll hold my judgment in abeyance until there is more information available.

definition: to regard with extreme repugnance; to detest
chinese: 憎惡；痛恨；極度厭惡
example: People with physical disabilities abhor being pitied.

definition: causing hatred or disgust; offensive; contrary or incompatible
chinese: 可憎的；令人厭惡的；與…相牴觸的
example: an abhorrent deed

definition: lasting a long time; enduring; steadfast
chinese: 持久的；永恆的；不變的
example: Only on paper has humanity yet achieved glory, beauty, truth, knowledge, virtue, and abiding love.

definition: (of a bad situation) extreme and hopeless; wretched; lacking pride; servile
chinese: 悲慘的；極度的；卑屈的；卑躬屈膝的
example: With abject horror she realized that he had already started to eat the body.

definition: to solemnly renounce a belief, claim, or cause; to avoid or shun
chinese: 發誓放棄；公開棄絕；避免
example: Those who were banished from the country were required to forever abjure their right to return.

definition: to renounce or give up something such as a right or power; to deny oneself
chinese: 放棄；捨棄；克制
example: Even under a deluge of scandal, the shameless politician would not abnegate their post.

definition: not normal; deviating from what is typical or usual
chinese: 反常的；異常的；變態的；不規則的
example: abnormal powers of concentration

definition: to detest; to abhor
chinese: 憎惡；痛恨；厭惡
example: It's quite right to abominate people who are evil-doers.

definition: free from deceit or duplicity; honest and open; openly
chinese: adj. 光明正大的；坦率的；無欺詐的；adv. 光明正大地
example: The mayor, despite his avuncular visage plastered about the city, was hardly aboveboard – some concluded that it was his ingratiating smile that allowed him to engage in corrupt behavior and get away with it.

definition: to wear away by friction; to scrape; to wear down mentally
chinese: 磨損；擦傷；（精神上）折磨
example: The rough pumice can abrade the skin.

definition: harsh or rough in manner; causing abrasion; a substance used for grinding or polishing
chinese: adj. （言行）粗魯刺耳的；令人不快的；研磨的；n. 研磨料
example: The claim from the employee about wages may be abrasive to the employer.

definition: side by side; up to date with the latest developments; keeping pace with
chinese: 並肩；並列；了解最新情況；跟上
example: Even the periodical pay raise could not keep abreast of higher living costs.

definition: to shorten a text while keeping the substance; to curtail or reduce a right
chinese: 刪節；縮短；削減（權利）
example: The student decided to abridge his paper by taking out unnecessary details.

definition: to repeal or abolish a law or agreement formally
chinese: （正式）廢除；廢止；取消
example: Did the ruling abrogate your right to seek compensation?

definition: to leave secretly, often to avoid arrest or with something stolen
chinese: 潛逃；偷偷離開；捲款潛逃
example: To abscond means to move in a mysterious way, commonly with the property of another.

definition: complete; not limited; having unrestricted power; certain and unquestionable; something absolute
chinese: adj. 絕對的；完全的；專制的；確鑿的；n. 絕對事物
example: An insulated soft-wood room and a good heater are the absolute necessities for a sauna.

definition: to declare free from guilt or blame; to release from an obligation
chinese: 赦免；使無罪；免除（責任）
example: Father, absolve me of my sins.

definition: intensely interesting; engrossing; taking in
chinese: 引人入勝的；非常有趣的；吸收的
example: Absorbing information on the internet is like drinking water from a fire hydrant.

definition: to refrain from something by one's own choice; to choose not to vote
chinese: 戒絕；自制；（投票）棄權
example: True science teaches us to doubt and to abstain from ignorance.

definition: moderate in eating and drinking; sparing
chinese: （飲食）有節制的；節儉的
example: His abstemious habits gave him a skeletal appearance.

definition: characterized by abstinence; self-restraining, especially in food or drink
chinese: 有節制的；禁慾的；克己的
example: The passage describes its subject as abstentious, meaning Characterized by abstinence; self-restraining.

definition: refraining from indulging an appetite, especially for food, drink, or sex
chinese: 有節制的；禁慾的；戒酒的
example: not totally abstinent but abstemious

definition: existing only as an idea; theoretical; abstruse; a summary; to extract or remove; to summarize; to distract
chinese: adj. 抽象的；理論上的；深奧的；n. 摘要；v. 提取；摘要；使分心
example: To him, hunger was an abstract concept; he always had enough to eat.

definition: difficult to understand; recondite; obscure
chinese: 深奧的；難以理解的；晦澀的
example: Professionals in many fields write in a style that is purposefully abstruse and unclear.

definition: wildly unreasonable or illogical; ridiculous
chinese: 荒謬的；不合理的；可笑的
example: It is human nature to think wisely and to act in an absurd fashion.

definition: existing in great plenty; plentiful; well supplied
chinese: 大量的；豐富的；充足的
example: She has an abundant supply of seeds to plant in the spring.

definition: to use wrongly or improperly; to mistreat; to insult or revile; improper use; cruel treatment; insulting language
chinese: v. 濫用；虐待；辱罵；n. 濫用；虐待；辱罵
example: These actions are an abuse of power and fundamentally undermine the rule of law.

definition: extremely bad; immeasurably deep or great
chinese: 極糟的；極差的；深不可測的；極度的
example: Since the weather is abysmal, we're staying home.

definition: to agree to a demand or request; to assume an office or title; to become a party to an agreement
chinese: 同意；應允；就任；繼位；加入（條約）
example: In this context, “accede” means take on duties or office.

definition: to move or make move faster; to cause to happen sooner; to increase in rate
chinese: 加速；促進；增長加快
example: Put it in first and slowly let out the clutch while you gradually accelerate.

definition: to make more noticeable or prominent; to emphasize
chinese: 強調；突顯；使更明顯
example: Carmela's high cheekbones accentuate her facial structure, enhancing her natural beauty.

definition: easy to reach or enter; easily understood; obtainable
chinese: 易接近的；可進入的；易懂的；可取得的
example: Google has played an important role in making information more accessible over the internet.

definition: a supplementary item or ornament; a person who helps in a crime; supplementary; secondary
chinese: n. 配件；附件；從犯；adj. 輔助的；附屬的
example: A crucifix is a vital accessory when fighting a demon.

definition: happening by chance or unexpectedly; incidental; nonessential
chinese: 意外的；偶然的；附帶的；非本質的
example: Grapefruits were created through an accidental cross between a pomelo and a sweet orange.

definition: enthusiastic public praise or approval; to praise enthusiastically and publicly
chinese: n. 讚譽；喝采；v. 稱讚；公開讚揚
example: The artist's reputation and fame soared after his groundbreaking exhibition received critical acclaim.

definition: to become or make accustomed to a new climate or situation
chinese: 適應（新環境或氣候）；使適應
example: In this context, “acclimate” means get used to a certain climate.

definition: an expression of praise or approval; an award or honor; a touch on the shoulder conferring knighthood
chinese: 讚揚；榮譽；獎賞；（受封）騎士禮
example: Although she was merited with many an accolade, we still don’t know what she did to deserve them.

definition: to provide room for; to adapt or adjust to; to oblige or fit in with; to reconcile; to provide lodging
chinese: 容納；適應；遷就；調和；提供住宿
example: His cottage is neat and comfortable; moreover, it can accommodate as many as ten people.

definition: agreement or harmony; a formal agreement; to grant or give; to be consistent with
chinese: n. 一致；協議；v. 給予；授予；相符
example: What he said yesterday was not in accord with what he said last week.

definition: to grow or accumulate gradually by addition
chinese: 逐漸增長；積聚；黏結
example: The tides cause sand to accrete on the shore.

definition: gradual growth by accumulation; something added; (astronomy) accumulation of matter by gravity
chinese: 累積；增長；增加物；（天文）吸積
example: An accretion disk has formed around the star.

definition: to accumulate or increase gradually; to come about as a benefit or result
chinese: （逐漸）累積；增加；產生（利益）
example: Many advantages accrue to society from the freedom of speech.

definition: to gather or pile up gradually; to increase in amount
chinese: 累積；積聚；逐漸增加
example: Don't let food residue accumulate in the oven; it can cause odors and smoke.

definition: to charge someone with a crime or wrongdoing; to blame
chinese: 指控；控告；指責
example: They accuse the government of marginalizing them politically and ignoring their demands.

definition: to make familiar with something through use or experience
chinese: 使習慣；使適應
example: She found it necessary to accustom her child to getting up early.

definition: sharp and forthright in speech or tone; harsh; sour
chinese: （言語或語氣）尖酸刻薄的；辛辣的；酸澀的
example: I'll try to stay on your good side, lest I get cut in two by that acerbic tongue of yours.

definition: sharp or biting in tone; acidic; sour; a chemical acid; (slang) LSD
chinese: adj. 尖刻的；酸性的；酸的；n. 酸；迷幻藥
example: The original acid test used hydrochloric and nitric acid to distinguish gold from base metals.

definition: to admit the truth or existence of; to recognize the authority of; to confirm receipt of; to express thanks for
chinese: 承認；認可；告知收到；答謝
example: Some humans consider their penises as a third leg and biology needs to acknowledge that.

definition: the highest point of achievement or perfection
chinese: 頂點；巔峰；極致
example: When he was at the acme of his career, a scandal brought about his downfall.

definition: familiar with someone or something; having knowledge of
chinese: 熟悉的；認識的；了解的
example: It was not until I entered this university that I got acquainted with her.

definition: to accept or agree reluctantly or without protest
chinese: 默許；勉強同意；默認
example: Mennad cannot acquiesce to this request.

definition: acceptance or agreement without protest
chinese: 默許；默認；順從
example: A lack of response is tantamount to acquiescence.

definition: to get or gain as one's own; to learn or develop a skill or habit; to buy a company
chinese: 獲得；取得；學到（技能或知識）；收購
example: The most valuable skill one can acquire is the ability to think for oneself.

definition: excessively eager to acquire possessions, wealth, or knowledge; greedy
chinese: 貪得的；渴望獲取的；貪婪的
example: He is acquisitive of knowledge.

definition: to declare not guilty of a criminal charge; (acquit oneself) to behave or perform in a certain way
chinese: 宣告無罪；開釋；使（自己）表現
example: In this context, “acquit” means pronounce not guilty of criminal charges.

definition: declared not guilty; legally blameless; past tense of acquit: cleared of a charge; performed or behaved
chinese: adj. 被判無罪的；v. 宣告無罪；表現
example: he stands acquitted on all charges

definition: unpleasantly sharp and pungent in smell or taste; bitter or caustic in manner
chinese: 刺鼻的；辛辣的；（言語）尖刻的
example: Charred wood gives off an acrid smell.

definition: angry and bitter; marked by deep-seated resentment
chinese: 尖酸刻薄的；激烈的；充滿敵意的
example: Divorce can put mutual friends of the divorcing couple in a difficult position, particularly if it's an acrimonious split.

definition: bitterness and ill will in manner or speech
chinese: 尖刻；敵意；怨恨；激烈言辭
example: Acrimony means bitterness and ill will. Don’t forget the adjective form, acrimonious, which describes relationships filled with bitterness and ill will.

definition: to make active or operative; to set in motion; to put into effect; (military) to put a unit on active duty
chinese: 啟動；使活化；使生效；（軍）組建（部隊）
example: Some states could activate their anti-abortion laws immediately, with others following shortly thereafter.

definition: sharpness or keenness of thought, vision, or hearing
chinese: 敏銳；（視覺或聽覺）銳度；（思維）敏捷
example: The hearing acuity of dogs is superior by far to that of humans.

definition: the ability to make good judgments and quick decisions; keen insight
chinese: 敏銳；精明；洞察力；判斷力
example: His wealth was inherited, not a consequence of his own business acumen.

definition: severe or intense; perceptive and keen; (of illness) coming sharply to a crisis; (of an angle) less than 90 degrees
chinese: 嚴重的；劇烈的；敏銳的；（疾病）急性的；（角）銳角的
example: This city will suffer from an acute water shortage unless it rains soon.

definition: created or done for a particular purpose only; improvised; for this specific purpose
chinese: adj. 臨時的；特別的；專案的；adv. 臨時地；特別地
example: Thus, this is an ad hoc solution - good in practice but theoretically weak.

definition: to speak or perform without preparation; improvised or spontaneous
chinese: v. 即興發言；即興表演；adj. 即興的；臨時的
example: He forgot part of his speech and had to ad-lib for a while.

definition: unshakable; refusing to change one's mind; a legendary extremely hard substance
chinese: adj. 堅定不移的；固執的；不讓步的；n. 堅硬物質
example: I tried to talk him out of it, but he was adamant.

definition: to make suitable for a new use or situation; to modify; to rewrite for a different medium; to adjust to new conditions
chinese: 使適應；改編；調整；適應
example: Complaining about something is one way to adapt yourself to a new environment.

definition: able to adjust to new conditions; able to be modified for a new use
chinese: 適應力強的；能適應的；可改編的
example: to succeed one must be adaptable

definition: having a capacity for adaptation; serving to fit an organism to its environment
chinese: 適應的；有適應能力的
example: the adaptive coloring of a chameleon

definition: a person who is addicted to a substance or activity; an enthusiast; to cause to become dependent or devoted
chinese: n. 成癮者；熱衷者；v. 使上癮；使沉溺
example: Just like any addict, we don't care how we get our next fix.

definition: to confuse or muddle; (of an egg) to become rotten; confused; rotten
chinese: v. 使混亂；使糊塗；（蛋）腐壞；adj. 混亂的；腐壞的
example: The fumes of the wine were mounting steadily to addle his indifferent brains.

definition: to cite as evidence or proof in an argument
chinese: 引證；舉出（證據或理由）
example: You can adduce studies and reports all you like, but their sophistry will always win out.

definition: very skilled or proficient; an expert
chinese: adj. 熟練的；擅長的；老練的；n. 專家；能手
example: adept in handicrafts

definition: sufficient for a requirement; satisfactory but not outstanding
chinese: 足夠的；適當的；尚可的
example: she had adequate training

definition: to follow or comply with rules; to believe in and support; to stick firmly
chinese: 遵守；堅持；擁護；黏著
example: Security forces fear that hardliners among the demonstrators may not adhere to such promises.

definition: a supporter or follower of a party, person, or belief; sticking fast; attached
chinese: n. 擁護者；信徒；追隨者；adj. 黏著的；依附的
example: In this context, “adherent” refers to sticking fast.

definition: to suspend a meeting or proceedings until later; to postpone; to move to another place
chinese: 休會；延期；暫停；移往（他處）
example: Let's adjourn to the dining room for dinner.

definition: to make a formal judgment on a disputed matter; to act as a judge
chinese: 裁決；判定；評審
example: The referee had to adjudicate the disputed play.

definition: something added but not essential; an assistant; a part-time instructor; supplementary; holding a temporary position
chinese: n. 附屬物；附加物；助手；（大學）兼任教師；adj. 附屬的；兼任的
example: What on earth is an adjunct?

definition: a solemn and earnest appeal to someone to do something; a solemn command
chinese: 懇求；祈求；嚴令
example: In this context, “adjuration” refers to a solemn and earnest appeal to someone to do something.

definition: to regard with respect or warm approval; to look at with pleasure
chinese: 欽佩；讚賞；欣賞
example: Stupid people can always find someone stupider than themselves who will admire them.

definition: to confess to be true; to allow to enter; to accept as valid; to allow the possibility of
chinese: 承認；准許進入；接納；容許
example: When he was faced with the evidence, he had to admit that he was guilty.

definition: to warn or advise earnestly; to reprove gently but firmly
chinese: 告誡；勸告；（溫和地）責備
example: I therefore admonish you to give the defendant the benefit of every reasonable doubt.

definition: relating to adolescence; immature; a young person in the process of developing into an adult
chinese: adj. 青春期的；不成熟的；n. 青少年
example: adolescent problems

definition: to choose and follow an idea or method; to take legally as one's own child; to approve formally
chinese: 採用；採納；收養；正式通過
example: Mario felt so bad for the abandoned puppy that he decided to adopt it.

definition: to love and respect deeply; to worship; to like very much
chinese: 非常喜愛；崇拜；敬愛
example: I know of no language that I adore as much as this one.

definition: to make more beautiful or attractive by adding ornament
chinese: 裝飾；使生色；點綴
example: I like to adorn my room with flowers.

definition: clever or skillful in using the hands or mind
chinese: 靈巧的；機敏的；熟練的
example: an exceptionally adroit pianist

definition: to praise or admire excessively or servilely
chinese: 諂媚；奉承；過分讚揚
example: In this context, “adulate” means flatter in an obsequious manner.

definition: excessive admiration or servile flattery
chinese: 諂媚；奉承；過度讚揚
example: Pop artists thrive on the adulation of their loyal fans.

definition: to make impure by adding inferior substances; adulterated; impure
chinese: v. 摻雜；摻假；降低品質；adj. 摻假的
example: You should not adulterate wine with water.

definition: to foreshadow; to outline or sketch briefly; to overshadow
chinese: 預示；概述；勾勒輪廓；遮蔽
example: In this context, “adumbrate” means describe roughly or briefly or give the main points or summary of.

definition: happening by chance; coming from outside; not inherent; (botany) growing in an unusual place
chinese: 偶然的；外來的；非固有的；（植物）不定的
example: Adventitious roots are those which do not appear in the usual place on a plant.

definition: an opponent in a contest, conflict, or dispute; an enemy
chinese: 對手；敵手；敵人
example: Chigurh operates outside the boundaries of conventional morality, making him a truly formidable adversary.

definition: difficulties; misfortune; a state of hardship
chinese: 逆境；厄運；困境
example: Adversity and prosperity reveal one's breadth of mind; joy and anger test one's self-restraint.

definition: to refer to or turn attention to (advert to); an advertisement
chinese: v. 提及；注意到；n. 廣告
example: Your advert will appear here.

definition: to publicly support or recommend; a person who supports a cause; a lawyer who pleads a case
chinese: v. 提倡；擁護；主張；n. 擁護者；倡導者；辯護律師
example: More and more environmentalists advocate and use environmentally friendly unleaded petrol in cars.

definition: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty; artistically pleasing; a set of artistic principles
chinese: adj. 美學的；審美的；有美感的；n. 美學觀；審美原則
example: Mathematicians are creative artists, their artworks being sophisticated constructs of ideas and aesthetic proofs.

definition: friendly, good-natured, and easy to talk to
chinese: 和藹可親的；友善的；易於親近的
example: Likeable, easy to talk to: affable is similar to amiable. The differences are subtle, and as far as the GRE is concerned, you can treat them as the same word. Like amiable, this word is great to use to describe people we know. After all, everyone knows an affable person.

definition: to have an effect on; to pretend or put on; to move emotionally; (psychology) observable emotion
chinese: v. 影響；假裝；故作；感動；n. （心理）情感
example: Will the new rules affect me?

definition: behavior or speech that is artificial and meant to impress; a pretense
chinese: 做作；裝模作樣；假裝
example: I don’t see any content in his statements besides clowning, affectation, and pretentiousness.

definition: a feeling of fondness or liking; (medicine) a disease or condition
chinese: 喜愛；感情；愛慕；（醫學）疾病
example: he had trouble expressing the affection he felt

definition: officially attached or closely associated
chinese: 附屬的；有關聯的；隸屬的
example: affiliated clubs

definition: an official association or connection with a group or organization
chinese: 隸屬關係；從屬；聯繫
example: a valuable financial affiliation

definition: a natural liking or attraction; a similarity of characteristics; a close relationship; (chemistry) tendency to combine
chinese: 親和力；喜好；相似；密切關係；（化學）親和性
example: Iron has an affinity for sulphur, and so does hydrogen for oxygen.

definition: to state as true; to confirm; to support or uphold; (law) to uphold a judgment
chinese: 斷言；肯定；確認；支持；（法律）維持（原判）
example: The exploiting classes try to immortalize false worldviews to affirm and strengthen their domination.

definition: to attach or fasten; to add (a signature, stamp); a prefix or suffix
chinese: v. 貼上；附加；n. （語言）詞綴
example: The bones could also have been used to make resin as a glue to affix handles onto tools.

definition: to cause pain or suffering to; to trouble
chinese: 折磨；使苦惱；使痛苦
example: These diseases afflict the poorest and most marginalized communities in the country.

definition: a state of great suffering; a cause of pain or distress
chinese: 痛苦；苦難；折磨；病痛
example: Staring in the smudged mirror, he was not certain if his affliction was loneliness or madness.

definition: having a great deal of money; wealthy; abundant; a tributary stream
chinese: adj. 富裕的；豐富的；n. （河流）支流
example: To be affluent is to be wealthy. This word usually describes countries, neighborhoods, or groups of people.

definition: with the mouth wide open in wonder or surprise; eagerly expectant; (Christianity) selfless love
chinese: adj. 目瞪口呆的；張大嘴的；急切期待的；n. （基督教）神聖之愛
example: He stood agape for a moment in front of the painting, surprised at its realism.

definition: to increase the power, wealth, or status of; to make appear greater than is true
chinese: 擴大（權力或財富）；提高（地位）；誇大
example: His need to aggrandize his accomplishments caused him to obtrude himself into every conversation.

definition: to make a problem or injury worse; to annoy or exasperate
chinese: 加重；使惡化；激怒；使惱火
example: The constant ticking of the clock was starting to seriously aggravate him at night.

definition: a whole formed by combining several elements; formed by combination; total; to gather into a mass or whole
chinese: n. 總計；集合體；adj. 總計的；合計的；v. 聚集；合計
example: In the aggregate, they're a nice enough group, but there are some obnoxious individuals among them.

definition: hostile or violent behavior; an unprovoked attack; readiness to attack
chinese: 侵略；攻擊；挑釁；攻擊性
example: The most visible forms of aggression are often seen between prey and predator.

definition: ready to attack or confront; hostile; forceful and determined; vigorous
chinese: 好鬥的；有攻擊性的；積極進取的；強勢的
example: He continues always being aggressive towards society, rather than repelling society and confining himself.

definition: the quality of being hostile or ready to attack; the quality of being bold and enterprising
chinese: 好鬥；攻擊性；積極進取；魄力
example: He has none of his father's aggressiveness.

definition: to cause distress or a sense of injustice; to infringe on the rights of
chinese: 使苦惱；使委屈；侵害（權利）
example: In this context, “aggrieve” means infringe on the rights of.

definition: filled with horror or shock
chinese: 驚駭的；嚇呆的；驚恐的
example: I'm aghast at the lack of manners, common sense and so on and so forth on the net.

definition: able to move quickly and easily; mentally quick and resourceful
chinese: 敏捷的；靈活的；機敏的
example: sleek and agile as a gymnast

definition: the ability to move quickly and easily; mental quickness
chinese: 敏捷；靈活；機敏
example: Benedito marveled at his billy goat's agility as it leaped from rock to rock.

definition: to campaign to arouse public concern; to make troubled or nervous; to stir or shake
chinese: 煽動；鼓動；使不安；使焦慮；攪動
example: Now is not the time to agitate the hornet's nest.

definition: troubled or nervous; excited; hotly debated; shaken or stirred
chinese: 焦慮不安的；激動的；（被）激烈爭論的；搖動的
example: agitated parents

definition: a state of anxiety or nervous excitement; public campaigning for change; stirring or shaking
chinese: 焦慮不安；激動；煽動；攪動
example: His agitation was so great that he could hardly speak.

definition: very eager or curious to hear or see something; excited
chinese: 極度渴望的；興奮的；急切的
example: They were agog to hear the latest news.

definition: to struggle or worry over a decision; to suffer or cause great pain
chinese: 苦苦思索；焦慮；（使）極度痛苦
example: I hope we didn't agonize over this decision for nothing.

definition: extreme physical or mental suffering; an intense struggle
chinese: 極度痛苦；掙扎；苦惱
example: an agony of doubt

definition: relating to farming or land ownership; a person who advocates land reform
chinese: adj. 農業的；土地的；耕地的；n. 主張土地改革者
example: an agrarian (or agricultural) society

definition: pleasing; pleasant; willing to agree; consistent or in harmony
chinese: 令人愉快的；宜人的；欣然同意的；一致的
example: Holomorphic functions have several agreeable properties, making them easy to work with.

definition: the science or practice of farming; cultivation of soil and raising of animals
chinese: 農業；農學；農耕
example: An arcology is a self-sufficient community, complete with agriculture, contained within a single structure.

definition: having no weak points; unassailable; not allowing air to pass through
chinese: 無懈可擊的；嚴密的；密封的；不透氣的
example: This food will keep for a week in an airtight container.

definition: brisk and cheerful readiness; eagerness
chinese: 欣然；樂意；敏捷；爽快
example: The first three weeks at his new job, Mark worked with such alacrity that upper management knew they would be giving him a promotion.

definition: a claim of being elsewhere when a crime occurred; an excuse; to provide an alibi for
chinese: n. 不在場證明；藉口；託辭；v. 提供不在場證明
example: The problem with the defense attorney's case is that the accused doesn't have an alibi.

definition: unfamiliar; foreign or incompatible with; from another country or world; a foreigner; a being from another planet
chinese: adj. 陌生的；格格不入的；外國的；外星的；n. 外國人；外星人
example: an economic theory alien to the spirit of capitalism

definition: to make someone feel isolated or unfriendly; to estrange; (law) to transfer ownership
chinese: 使疏遠；離間；使不友善；（法律）轉讓
example: If you don't want to alienate people, you must be kind.

definition: the feeling of being isolated or estranged; separation from others; (law) transfer of property
chinese: 疏離感；疏遠；離間；（法律）轉讓
example: Alienation from nature will one day become humanity's demise.

definition: to ally oneself with; to bring into agreement; to place in a straight line; to adjust
chinese: 使結盟；使一致；對齊；校準
example: The map required rectification to align with the new satellite data.

definition: to diminish or put at rest fear, suspicion, or worry; to relieve
chinese: 減輕；緩和；平息（恐懼或疑慮）
example: She tried to allay their fears but only ended up heightening them.

definition: a claim or assertion, often of wrongdoing, made without proof
chinese: （未證實的）指控；說法；斷言
example: an allegation of malpractice

definition: loyalty or commitment to a person, group, or cause
chinese: 忠誠；效忠；擁護
example: Five is too young to pledge allegiance to a flag.

definition: to make suffering or a problem less severe; to relieve
chinese: 減輕；緩和；舒緩
example: In order to alleviate employment pressures, the nation has established a series of relevant policies.

definition: to distribute according to a plan; to set apart for a particular purpose
chinese: 分配；分派；撥出（經費）
example: A committee of experts determines how to allocate the money.

definition: a metal made by combining two or more elements; a mixture; to mix metals; to debase; to spoil or diminish
chinese: n. 合金；混合物；v. 摻雜；降低純度；破壞（樂趣）
example: ODS super alloy is produced by the mechanical alloy method following powder metallurgy.

definition: to refer to indirectly or briefly; to hint at
chinese: 暗指；間接提到；影射
example: In the early part of my study, I allude to work that had already been done on the psychology of crowd-control.

definition: the quality of being powerfully attractive or fascinating; to attract or tempt
chinese: n. 魅力；誘惑力；v. 吸引；誘惑
example: There is an allure and excitement to the power of an old-fashioned steam train.

definition: containing or characterized by indirect references or allusions
chinese: 暗指的；引經據典的；含蓄的
example: allusive speech is characterized by allusions

definition: a person, group, or nation united with another for a common purpose; a supporter; to join in alliance
chinese: n. 盟友；同盟國；支持者；v. 結盟；聯合
example: An enemy of an enemy is not necessarily an ally.

definition: up in or into the air; overhead; (nautical) up the mast; in flight
chinese: adv. 在空中；在高處；（船）在桅頂；adj. 在空中的
example: Until now, opinions differed over the question of whether birds could sleep while aloft.

definition: not friendly or forthcoming; distant; detached
chinese: 冷淡的；疏遠的；超然的
example: Cats are aloof, guinea pigs are nervous, and dogs need constant love and attention.

definition: to change or make different; to adjust clothing to fit; to castrate or spay an animal
chinese: 改變；修改；（衣服）修改尺寸；閹割（動物）
example: If we alter the construction of such sentences, the missing antecedent is often restored.

definition: one of two or more possibilities; available as another choice; unconventional
chinese: n. 替代方案；選擇；adj. 替代的；另類的；非傳統的
example: an alternative plan

definition: height above sea level or the ground; a high place or region
chinese: 高度；海拔；高處；高地
example: the altitude gave her a headache

definition: selfless concern for the well-being of others
chinese: 利他主義；無私
example: There's no explanation for the evolution of altruism that doesn't involve kinship.

definition: a mixture or blend of different elements; (chemistry) an alloy of mercury with another metal
chinese: 混合物；融合體；（化學）汞合金
example: The band’s music was an amalgam of hip-hop and jazz.

definition: to combine or unite to form one organization or structure
chinese: 合併；結合；融合
example: If health departments amalgamate their data, we can better understand the picture for the whole country.

definition: able to use both hands equally well; unusually skillful; double-dealing
chinese: 左右手都靈巧的；多才多藝的；兩面討好的
example: an ambidextrous surgeon

definition: open to more than one interpretation; unclear or uncertain
chinese: 模稜兩可的；含糊不清的；不明確的
example: The coach told his team, “Move towards that side of the field”; because he did not point, his directions were ambiguous, and the team had no idea to which side he was referring.

definition: having mixed or conflicting feelings about something; uncertain
chinese: （情感或態度）矛盾的；搖擺不定的
example: Sam was ambivalent about studying for the GRE because it ate up a lot of her time, yet he learned many words and improved at reading comprehension.

definition: to walk at a slow, relaxed pace; a leisurely walk
chinese: v. 漫步；緩行；閒逛；n. 漫步；緩步
example: You can watch the cows amble through the pasture.

definition: exceptionally pleasing to taste or smell; divine
chinese: （食物）美味的；芳香的；神仙般的
example: The passage describes its subject as ambrosial, meaning extremely pleasing to the taste; sweet and fragrant.

definition: to make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve
chinese: 改善；改進；減輕（問題）
example: Political reforms may ameliorate the living conditions of the poor.

definition: open and responsive to suggestion; easily persuaded; subject to law; capable of being tested
chinese: 順從的；願意接受的；應服從的；可檢驗的
example: Even though she did not like bad weather, Shirley was generally amenable and decided to accompany her brother to the picinc.

definition: to make changes to a text or law; to improve or correct
chinese: 修正；修改（法案）；改善
example: amend the document

definition: a formal change or addition to a law or document; the act of improving or correcting
chinese: 修正案；修訂；改正
example: The amendment is still pending ratification.

definition: a useful or pleasant facility or feature; pleasantness; courtesy
chinese: 便利設施；舒適；融洽；禮節
example: Many of these children were born in refugee camps, and running water is still a new and delightful amenity.

definition: friendly and pleasant in manner; good-natured
chinese: 和藹可親的；友好的；溫和的
example: Amy’s name was very apt: she was so amiable that she was twice voted class president.

definition: characterized by friendliness and absence of discord; peaceable
chinese: 友善的；和睦的；（關係）和平的
example: The judge said he had never seen such an amicable and mutually agreed divorce.

definition: friendship, especially friendly relations between nations or groups
chinese: 友好；和睦；親善關係
example: I yet lingered half-an-hour longer, hoping to see some sign of amity: but she gave none.

definition: without a clearly defined shape or form; unorganized; vague; (chemistry) noncrystalline
chinese: 無固定形狀的；無組織的；模糊的；（化學）非晶質的
example: His study plan for the GRE was at best amorphous; he would do questions from random pages in any one of seven test prep books.

definition: more than enough; plentiful; large and spacious; full in figure
chinese: 充足的；豐富的；寬敞的；豐滿的
example: had ample food for the party

definition: to increase in size, effect, or significance; to make louder; to expand on with details
chinese: 擴大；增強；放大（聲音）；詳述
example: It was a mistake to amplify this debate with thoughtless responses.

definition: in a wildly frenzied and uncontrolled way; frenzied and out of control
chinese: adv. 狂亂地；失控地；adj. 狂亂的；殺氣騰騰的
example: Wherever the bowl-cut teen-idol went, his legions of screaming fans ran through the streets amuck, hoping for a glance of his boyish face.

definition: an error in chronology placing something in the wrong period; a person or thing belonging to an earlier time
chinese: 時代錯誤；年代誤植；過時的人或事物
example: A soldier is an anachronism of which we must get rid.

definition: chronologically misplaced; belonging to an earlier period; old-fashioned
chinese: 時代錯誤的；過時的；不合時宜的
example: English public schools are anachronistic

definition: relieving pain; a pain-relieving drug
chinese: adj. 止痛的；無痛覺的；n. 止痛藥
example: Morphine, an alkaloid found in opium, has powerful analgesic properties.

definition: comparable in certain respects; similar or corresponding
chinese: 類似的；可類比的；相似的
example: In the economic sphere communism is analogous to democracy in the political sphere.

definition: a person who believes in or advocates the abolition of government; a rebel against authority
chinese: 無政府主義者；反抗權威者
example: Every anarchist is a socialist, but every socialist is not necessarily an anarchist.

definition: something or someone vehemently disliked; (church) a formal curse or excommunication
chinese: 深惡痛絕的人或事物；令人厭惡之物；（教會）逐出教會
example: Hundreds of years ago, Galileo was anathema to the church; today the church is anathema to some on the left side of the political spectrum.

definition: relating to bodily structure or to anatomy
chinese: 解剖的；解剖學的；結構上的
example: anatomical features

definition: a person from whom one is descended; an early form from which something developed
chinese: 祖先；祖宗；（事物的）原型；前身
example: A proto-language is the common ancestor of a group of languages or dialects.

definition: one's family or ethnic descent; lineage; the origin or background of something
chinese: 祖先；血統；世系；家世
example: The coccyx is a vestigial feature that shows the common ancestry of mankind and apes.

definition: providing support; supplementary; of secondary importance; a person or thing that supports
chinese: adj. 輔助的；附屬的；次要的；n. 輔助人員；附屬物
example: The professor carefully prepared the materials for the lecture, down to the smallest ancillary page.

definition: a short amusing or interesting story about a real event or person; an unverified account
chinese: 軼事；趣聞；（未經證實的）傳聞
example: Then he told an anecdote which wasn't quite picked up by the microphones.

definition: lacking vigor, energy, or force; weak; suffering from anemia
chinese: 乏力的；缺乏活力的；疲弱的；貧血的
example: The passage describes its subject as anemic, meaning lacking vigor or energy.

definition: a substance that induces insensitivity to pain; causing loss of sensation; insensitive
chinese: n. 麻醉劑；adj. 麻醉的；無感覺的；麻木的
example: He lost consciousness under the influence of the anesthetic.

definition: severe mental or physical pain or suffering; to suffer or cause severe distress
chinese: n. 極度痛苦；苦惱；v. （使）極度痛苦
example: She takes a new lover while he is in anguish.

definition: to pass criticism or censure on; to comment critically
chinese: 批評；譴責；非難
example: In this context, “animadvert” means express blame or censure or make a harshly critical remark.

definition: relating to physical needs or instincts; brutish; of animals; a living organism; a brutish person
chinese: adj. 肉體的；本能的；獸性的；動物的；n. 動物；畜生
example: animal instincts

definition: to bring to life; to inspire or motivate; to give movement to; to make as an animated film; alive; lively
chinese: v. 使有生氣；激勵；推動；製作成動畫；adj. 有生命的；有活力的
example: Whereas the junction is more stiff or rigid, the nexus is more pliable; it is, as it were, animate or articulated.

definition: strong hostility or ill will
chinese: 敵意；仇恨；憎惡
example: The governor’s animosity toward his rival was only inflamed when the latter spread false lies regarding the governor’s first term.

definition: hostility or ill feeling; motivation or intention; (Jungian psychology) the masculine part of a woman's psyche
chinese: 敵意；憎惡；意圖；（心理）阿尼姆斯
example: It was all done out of animus.

definition: to heat and slowly cool metal or glass to toughen it; to strengthen or toughen
chinese: （冶金）使退火；鍛鍊；強化（意志）
example: If you anneal the glass it will be stronger and easier to work with.

definition: to take possession of territory; to add as an extra part; a building added to another; an addition to a document
chinese: v. 併吞；併入（領土）；附加；n. 附屬建築；附錄
example: The annex is on the north of the original building.

definition: the act of incorporating territory into another; addition; something annexed
chinese: 併吞；合併；附加；附加物
example: Any translation is an annexation.

definition: to destroy completely; to defeat utterly
chinese: 消滅；殲滅；徹底擊敗
example: The aliens are trying to annihilate the human race.

definition: to add explanatory notes or comments to a text or diagram
chinese: 註解；評註；加註釋
example: Students should annotate the passage before comparing its competing claims.

definition: to make a public declaration; to state firmly; to be a sign of; to make known the arrival of
chinese: 宣布；聲稱；預示；顯示
example: The mayor declared that he would announce the result of the investigation.

definition: to make slightly angry; to irritate; to harass repeatedly
chinese: 使惱怒；使煩惱；不斷騷擾
example: Go to the exam review and annoy the lecturers there with your questions.

definition: occurring once every year; covering a year; (of plants) living for one year; a yearly publication; an annual plant
chinese: adj. 每年的；年度的；（植物）一年生的；n. 年刊；年鑑；一年生植物
example: a border of annual flowering plants

definition: to declare invalid; to cancel or abolish
chinese: 宣告無效；廢除；取消
example: He wants to annul it.

definition: bland and unlikely to offend; inoffensive; relieving pain; a painkilling medicine; something that soothes
chinese: adj. 平淡無奇的；不得罪人的；無害的；止痛的；n. 止痛藥；慰藉物
example: In this context, “anodyne” refers to a medicine used to relieve pain.

definition: to choose as if by divine intervention; to nominate as successor; to smear with oil in a religious ceremony
chinese: 選定（接班人）；指定；（宗教）塗油；塗抹
example: In this context, “anoint” means choose by or as if by divine intervention.

definition: deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected
chinese: 異常的；反常的；不規則的
example: According to those who do not believe in climate change, the extreme weather over the last five years is simply anomalous—average temps should return to average, they believe.

definition: something that deviates from what is standard or expected; an irregularity
chinese: 異常；反常現象；異常事物
example: We have found an anomaly in the earth's crust.

definition: the condition of being anonymous; lack of distinctive features
chinese: 匿名；不具名；無特色
example: Under the cloak of anonymity, cowards are acting like bigmouths.

definition: not identified by name; of unknown authorship; lacking individuality
chinese: 匿名的；無名的；無特色的
example: An astute reader should be willing to weigh everything they read, including anonymous sources.

definition: active hostility or opposition
chinese: 敵意；對立；對抗
example: On the other hand, nothing more quickly disarms this feeling of antagonism than evidence of delicacy on your part.

definition: showing hostility or opposition; mutually opposed; (biology) acting in opposition
chinese: 敵對的；對抗的；對立的；（藥物）拮抗的
example: The emotional qualities are antagonistic to clear reasoning.

definition: to cause to become hostile; to provoke; to act in opposition to; to counteract
chinese: 激怒；引起敵意；對抗；抵消
example: He didn't want to antagonize her.

definition: existing before a war, especially the American Civil War
chinese: 戰前的；（美國）南北戰爭前的
example: The passage describes its subject as antebellum, meaning belonging to a period before a war especially the American Civil War.

definition: a thing that existed before; a precursor; (grammar) a word to which a pronoun refers; ancestors; preceding in time or order
chinese: n. 前例；前事；（文法）先行詞；祖先；adj. 先前的；在前的
example: If we alter the construction of such sentences, the missing antecedent is often restored.

definition: to come before in time; to precede; to put an earlier date on a document
chinese: 早於；先於；（文件）填早日期
example: These fossils clearly antedate the rise of the dinosaurs.

definition: extremely old; antiquated or out of date; belonging to the time before the biblical Flood
chinese: 極古老的；過時的；（聖經）大洪水以前的
example: The vampire was born in the antediluvian world.

definition: situated at or toward the front; earlier in time
chinese: 前面的；前部的；（時間）較早的
example: The head, expanding from the neck, contracts to a bluntly pointed anterior end.

definition: caused or produced by human activity; relating to the study of human origins and development
chinese: 人為的；人類活動造成的；人類起源學的
example: In this context, “anthropogenic” refers to of or relating to the study of the origins and development of human beings.

definition: the study of human societies, cultures, and their origins and development
chinese: 人類學
example: Every student of biology, anatomy, anthropology, ethnology or psychology is familiar with these facts.

definition: grotesquely or playfully absurd; a ludicrous or grotesque act done for amusement
chinese: adj. 滑稽古怪的；荒誕可笑的；n. 滑稽動作；古怪舉止
example: In this context, “antic” refers to a ludicrous or grotesque act done for fun and amusement.

definition: to expect or predict; to act in advance to prepare for or forestall; to come or act before; to look forward to
chinese: 預期；預料；預先防範；搶先；期待
example: Aid organizations anticipate continued flooding will displace about 200,000 people and affect the lives of 485,000 people.

definition: a remedy that counteracts a poison; something that counteracts an unpleasant situation
chinese: 解毒劑；解藥；矯正方法
example: The lab is trying to synthesize an antidote to treat the poisoning victims.

definition: a strong feeling of aversion or dislike; an object of such dislike
chinese: 反感；厭惡；憎惡的對象
example: That politician attracted the antipathy of the public through their abuse of public office.

definition: old-fashioned or outdated; no longer suitable for modern use
chinese: 過時的；陳舊的；老式的
example: We must do away with the antiquated corporate culture that makes long working hours acceptable.

definition: made in earlier times and valued for its age; old-fashioned; a valuable old object
chinese: adj. 古董的；古老的；過時的；n. 古董；古物
example: the beautiful antique French furniture

definition: the direct opposite; contrast or opposition; (rhetoric) juxtaposition of contrasting ideas
chinese: 正相反的事物；對立面；對照；（修辭）對偶法
example: his theory is the antithesis of mine

definition: directly opposed or contrary; mutually incompatible
chinese: 正相反的；完全對立的；不相容的
example: Your proposal is antithetical to our own.

definition: showing little or no emotion, interest, or concern
chinese: 冷漠的；無動於衷的；缺乏興趣的
example: a woman who became active rather than apathetic as she grew older

definition: lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern
chinese: 冷漠；漠不關心；缺乏興趣
example: Given the amount of apathy in the world, today is the most revolutionary day.

definition: the highest point or tip; the peak or climax of something
chinese: 頂點；巔峰；尖端；最高潮
example: When it comes to ground warfare, tanks remain the apex predators.

definition: a short, pithy statement expressing a general truth
chinese: 格言；警句
example: The aphorism is, how to say it?, the champagne of melancholia; each short statement encapsulates years of disillusionment distilled in a moment of intoxication.

definition: terse and witty like a maxim; containing aphorisms
chinese: 格言式的；警句般的；簡潔精闢的
example: In this context, “aphoristic” refers to terse and witty and like a maxim.

definition: self-confidence and composure, especially in a demanding situation
chinese: 沉著；泰然自若；鎮定
example: The diplomat handled the tense negotiation with calm aplomb.

definition: of or like the end of the world; catastrophic; forecasting disaster; of a revelation; ultimately decisive
chinese: 末日般的；災難性的；預示災禍的；（宗教）啟示的；決定性的
example: Typically busy streets around the world look like scenes from post-apocalyptic movies.

definition: of doubtful authenticity though widely circulated; fictitious; of the Apocrypha
chinese: 真實性可疑的；杜撰的；虛構的；（聖經）偽經的
example: Apocryphal stories are the most fun variety of bullshit.

definition: the highest point or climax; the point in an orbit farthest from the earth
chinese: 頂點；巔峰；極點；（天文）遠地點
example: The apogee of the Viennese style of music, Mozart’s music continues to mesmerize audiences well into the 21st century.

definition: not interested in or involved with politics; politically neutral
chinese: 不關心政治的；與政治無關的；政治中立的
example: If an apolitical language is theoretically possible, it has never existed.

definition: a person who argues in defense or justification of a policy, institution, or doctrine
chinese: 辯護者；擁護者；（宗教）護教者
example: an apologist for capital punishment

definition: overcome with anger; furious; relating to apoplexy
chinese: 極度憤怒的；暴怒的；中風的
example: In this context, “apoplectic” refers to pertaining to or characteristic of apoplexy.

definition: the abandonment of a religious belief, principle, or political party
chinese: 叛教；背棄信仰；變節；脫黨
example: Some believers turn against their faith and renounce it. We call this act apostasy, and those who commit it, apostates. Today the word carries a slightly broader connotation in that it can apply to politics as well.

definition: an ardent early advocate of a cause or reform; one of Christ's twelve disciples
chinese: 倡導者；熱烈擁護者；（基督教）使徒
example: In this context, “apostle” refers to an ardent early supporter of a cause or reform.

definition: the perfect example of something; the highest point of development; elevation to divine status
chinese: 典範；極致；巔峰；神化
example: As difficult as it is to imagine, the apotheosis of Mark Zuckerberg’s career, many believe, is yet to come.

definition: to fill with horror, shock, or dismay
chinese: 使震驚；使驚駭；使憎惡
example: The report's evidence of deliberate neglect will appall many readers.

definition: clothing or attire; to clothe or adorn
chinese: n. 服裝；衣著；v. 使穿衣；裝飾
example: We went up by two floors in order to reach the apparel stalls.

definition: clearly visible or understood; seeming real or true but not necessarily so
chinese: 顯然的；明顯的；表面上的；看似的
example: the effects of the drought are apparent to anyone who sees the parched fields

definition: a ghost or ghostlike figure; a remarkable or unexpected sight; the act of appearing
chinese: 幽靈；鬼魂；突然出現的奇異人物；出現
example: With her perfect figure and elegant dress she was, indeed, a strange apparition upon a lonely moorland path.

definition: a resort to reason or authority; an earnest request; attractiveness; a legal appeal; to make an earnest request; to attract; to apply to a higher court
chinese: n. 訴諸；呼籲；吸引力；上訴；v. 呼籲；懇求；吸引；上訴；訴諸
example: An appeal to common sense is a type of argument from incredulity, a logical fallacy.

definition: attractive or interesting; expressing an earnest request
chinese: 吸引人的；有魅力的；懇求的
example: Appealing mostly to families with small children, the park had a nursery rhyme theme.

definition: to clap the hands in approval; to praise or express approval of
chinese: 鼓掌喝采；稱讚；贊同
example: As soon as the new teacher entered the classroom, the students began to applaud.

definition: approval shown by clapping; praise or approval
chinese: 掌聲；鼓掌；讚許
example: Topping off the performance with a backflip, the dancer preened in the applause.

definition: relevant or appropriate; able to be applied
chinese: 適用的；可應用的；相關的
example: It is not reasonable to suppose that this rule is applicable under any condition.

definition: apt in the circumstances; pertinent or appropriate
chinese: 恰當的；貼切的；中肯的
example: It is, however, apposite to note that this process will continue in the year ahead.

definition: large or important enough to be noticed; perceptible; considerable
chinese: 可察覺的；明顯的；相當大的
example: There was no appreciable quantity of mercury found in the fish.

definition: to understand or perceive; to arrest; to anticipate with anxiety or fear
chinese: 理解；領悟；逮捕；憂慮；預感
example: I sometimes apprehend that there will be some difficulty.

definition: anxiety or fear that something bad will happen; understanding; the act of arresting
chinese: 憂慮；恐懼；理解；逮捕
example: The excitement of starting a new job is sometimes mingled with a certain apprehension.

definition: anxious or fearful about the future; quick to understand
chinese: 憂慮的；擔心的；不安的；善於領悟的
example: They are apprehensive that some further disaster might occur.

definition: to inform or tell someone of something
chinese: 通知；告知；使知曉
example: In this context, “apprise” means inform (somebody) of something.

definition: approval or praise; official sanction
chinese: 讚許；認可；批准
example: The architect secured the mayor's approbation for a new housing project.

definition: to take for one's own use, often without permission; to set aside funds; suitable or proper
chinese: v. 挪用；侵佔；據為己有；撥（款）；adj. 適當的；恰當的
example: Milk isn't good for adult cats, and only cat milk is appropriate for kittens.

definition: close to the actual but not exact; to come close to; to estimate
chinese: adj. 大約的；近似的；接近的；v. 接近；近似；估計
example: the approximate time was 10 o'clock

definition: an accessory or subordinate thing; a right attached to property; equipment used for a task
chinese: 附屬物；（法律）附屬權利；配件；用具
example: An appurtenance to the real estate is access to the pond over there.

definition: relevant or opportune; with reference to; by the way; at an opportune time
chinese: adj. 恰當的；切題的；prep. 關於；就…而言；adv. 順便一提；恰好地
example: Now and then the parrot would utter quite apropos sentences in the most unexpected manner.

definition: suitable or appropriate; having a tendency to; quick to learn
chinese: 恰當的；貼切的；易於…的；傾向於…的；聰穎的
example: It is apt to get either cloudy or windy when the cherry-blossoms are in full bloom.

definition: a natural ability or talent; a natural tendency
chinese: 天資；才能；資質；（自然）傾向
example: Genius is nothing but a great aptitude for patience.

definition: a tank or building for keeping and displaying live fish and water animals
chinese: 水族館；水族箱；魚缸
example: These colourful, lively fish live mainly in the upper part of the aquarium.

definition: of, like, containing, or dissolved in water; formed by water
chinese: 水的；含水的；水溶的；似水的；（地質）水成的
example: aqueous solutions

definition: suitable for growing crops
chinese: 適合耕種的；可耕的
example: Algeria's arable lands are concentrated in the north of the country.

definition: based on whim or chance rather than reason; random; using unrestrained power
chinese: 任意的；武斷的；專斷的；專橫的
example: It's the result of a bunch of arbitrary designs decisions made by one guy.

definition: understood by few; mysterious or secret
chinese: 深奧的；晦澀難懂的；神祕的
example: The warm punch fuming in the icy air called to mind caldrons, witches, and arcane incantations.

definition: playfully mischievous or condescending; chief; a curved structure; to form into an arch
chinese: adj. 調皮的；狡黠的；故作淘氣的；自視高人一等的；主要的；n. 拱；拱門；足弓；v. 使成拱形
example: The baroness was arch, making playful asides to the townspeople; yet because they couldn’t pick up on her dry humor, they thought her supercilious.

definition: very old or old-fashioned; belonging to an earlier period; (of language) no longer in current use
chinese: 過時的；古老的；古代的；（語言）古體的
example: Don't delete items that are unnatural-sounding or archaic without a second opinion by an experienced moderator.

definition: very typical of a certain kind; constituting an original model
chinese: 典型的；原型的；最具代表性的
example: archetypal patterns

definition: a very typical example of something; an original model from which others are copied
chinese: 典型；原型；典範
example: The clarity of the tax code was good enough to become the archetype of perspicuous writing in the lawyer's cohort.

definition: enthusiastic or passionate; characterized by intense emotion; burning
chinese: 熱情的；熱烈的；熱切的；強烈的；（文）燃燒的
example: ardent love

definition: great enthusiasm, passion, or devotion
chinese: 熱情；熱忱；狂熱
example: She still burns with the ardor of youth.

definition: involving great effort; difficult and tiring; steep and hard to climb
chinese: 艱鉅的；費力的；艱辛的；（山路）陡峭的
example: He mastered these words through the arduous consultation of the dictionary.

definition: a reason or set of reasons given to support a conclusion; a line of reasoning; a heated disagreement
chinese: 論點；論證；論據；爭論；爭吵
example: What is significant in this argument is that his theory can identify those phenomena.

definition: an elaborate song for a solo voice, especially in an opera
chinese: 詠嘆調；（歌劇）獨唱曲
example: The third aria is the part in which she makes herself heard the best.

definition: having little or no rain; dull and lacking interest; barren
chinese: 乾燥的；乾旱的；枯燥乏味的；貧瘠的
example: Such projects have turned arid plains into fertile farmland, which has quadrupled agricultural production.

definition: a member of the nobility; a person with the manners or tastes of the upper class
chinese: 貴族；有貴族作風的人
example: The one with the sophisticated beret is actually an aristocrat of ancient lineage.

definition: complete or utter (used of something bad); notorious
chinese: 十足的；徹頭徹尾的；惡名昭彰的
example: an arrant fool

definition: an impressive range or collection; an ordered arrangement; fine clothing; to arrange or display; to deploy; to dress
chinese: n. 一系列；大批；排列；陣列；盛裝；v. 排列；部署（兵力）；打扮
example: Each arm of the eyeglass frame has an array of four tiny directional microphones.

definition: to stop or check; to attract and hold attention; to seize by legal authority; a seizure by legal authority; a stoppage
chinese: v. 阻止；抑制；吸引（注意）；逮捕；n. 逮捕；停止
example: They've offered a reward of three million dollars for information leading to an arrest.

definition: striking or eye-catching; holding the attention
chinese: 引人注目的；醒目的；吸引人的
example: Advertising may be described as the science of arresting the human intelligence long enough to get money from it.

definition: lacking a steady rhythm; irregular; relating to an irregular heartbeat
chinese: 不規律的；無節奏的；（醫）心律不整的
example: The passage describes its subject as arrhythmic, meaning lacking a steady rhythm.

definition: a person who has recently risen in wealth or status but is not socially accepted; an ambitious social climber
chinese: 暴發戶；新貴；不擇手段往上爬的人
example: In this context, “arriviste” refers to a person who has suddenly risen to a higher economic status but has not gained social acceptance of others in that class.

definition: an exaggerated sense of one's own importance; overbearing pride
chinese: 傲慢；自大；狂妄
example: In the shadow of humility, arrogance wilts faster than a rose without a stem.

definition: having or showing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance
chinese: 傲慢的；自大的；狂妄的
example: an arrogant official

definition: human creative expression; works of art collectively; a skill or craft; the humanities; cunning
chinese: 藝術；美術；藝術品；技藝；人文學科；詭計
example: an art exhibition

definition: clever in a crafty or deceitful way; showing skill in achieving an end
chinese: 狡猾的；詭詐的；巧妙的；精巧的
example: The passage describes its subject as artful, meaning marked by skill in achieving a desired end especially with cunning or craft.

definition: a piece of writing in a publication; a particular item; a clause in a document; (grammar) a determiner; to bind by a training contract
chinese: n. 文章；物品；條款；（文法）冠詞；v. 訂約使當學徒
example: This article is critical of the way investigations are being made into the matter.

definition: able to express ideas clearly; jointed; to express clearly; to pronounce distinctly; to connect by joints
chinese: adj. 表達清晰的；口齒伶俐的；有關節的；v. 清楚表達；明確說明；清晰發音；以關節連接
example: He works fast and is very articulate but his insincerity is his biggest defect.

definition: a clever trick or deception; insincere or artificial behavior; skill or ingenuity
chinese: 詭計；計謀；矯飾；技巧
example: The language of truth must be, with no doubt, simple and without artifice.

definition: creative skill or ability; artistic quality
chinese: 藝術才能；藝術技巧；藝術性
example: I had no idea how much artistry could go into a sandwich.

definition: without guile or deception; natural and simple; without skill, clumsy
chinese: 天真無邪的；純樸的；不矯飾的；拙劣的；粗陋的
example: Your artless attempt at a treatise is more like a diatribe.

definition: to go or move up; to climb; to rise to a higher position or the throne; to trace back in time
chinese: 上升；攀登；登上（王位）；晉升；追溯
example: Who of those who have been cast down by sin shall ascend?

definition: a position of dominance or control; the rise to power
chinese: 支配地位；優勢；權勢；崛起
example: The ascendancy of monarchs is what keeps their subjects from rebellion.

definition: a position of dominance or control; (astrology) the rising sign; rising in power or influence
chinese: n. 支配地位；優勢；（占星）上升點；adj. 占優勢的；上升的
example: In this context, “ascendant” refers to position or state of being dominant or in control.

definition: practicing severe self-discipline and abstaining from pleasure; a person who practices such self-denial
chinese: adj. 苦行的；禁慾的；自我克制的；n. 苦行者；禁慾者
example: He is clean-shaven, pale, and ascetic-looking, retaining something of the professor in his features.

definition: to attribute something to a cause or source; to regard a quality as belonging to
chinese: 歸因於；歸功於；歸咎於；認為…具有（特質）
example: Most stereotypes ascribe negative characteristics to a group.

definition: free from germs; preventing infection; lacking vitality or emotion
chinese: 無菌的；消毒的；（喻）缺乏生氣的；冷漠的
example: We're learning about aseptic packaging.

definition: not in a straight or level position; awry; crooked
chinese: adv. 歪斜地；不正地；adj. 歪的；歪斜的
example: There was a phone number placed askew at the bottom of the paper.

definition: a particular part or feature of something; appearance or look; the direction a building faces
chinese: 方面；面向；外觀；神情；（房屋）朝向
example: Addiction is not a personal failing but an aspect of an exploitative system.

definition: harshness of tone or manner; roughness of a surface; a rough projection; severity of conditions
chinese: （語氣）粗暴；嚴厲；粗糙；凹凸不平；（環境）艱苦
example: In materials science, asperity refers to the unevenness, roughness or ruggedness of a material.

definition: a damaging or derogatory remark; an attack on someone's reputation
chinese: 誹謗；中傷；詆毀
example: The unsupported accusation cast an aspersion on the researcher's integrity.

definition: a person who aspires to a position or goal; ambitious or aspiring
chinese: n. 有抱負者；追求者；候選人；adj. 有抱負的；渴望成功的
example: In this context, “aspirant” refers to an ambitious and aspiring young person.

definition: to criticize harshly; to attack violently; to trouble or beset
chinese: 抨擊；猛烈攻擊；（疑慮等）困擾
example: Several reviewers assail the theory for ignoring contrary evidence.

definition: a violent physical or verbal attack; (law) a threat or act of violence; to attack violently
chinese: n. 攻擊；侵犯；（法律）傷害罪；v. 攻擊；襲擊；抨擊
example: Burning the national flag is an assault against the embodiment of the republic.

definition: to gather together; to collect; to fit together the parts of
chinese: 集合；聚集；收集；組裝
example: Stop playing your video game for a minute and help me assemble this desk.

definition: agreement or approval; to express agreement
chinese: n. 同意；贊成；v. 同意；贊成
example: Teenagers grant assent to medical procedures, while parents grant consent.

definition: to state forcefully; to insist on (a right or claim); to behave confidently so as to gain recognition
chinese: 斷言；主張；維護（權利）；表現自己
example: Europe can only assert itself with the very high quality wines which it has.

definition: confident and forceful in expressing views or claims
chinese: 堅定自信的；果斷的；強勢的
example: Algeria needs to take a more assertive posture in the region.

definition: to evaluate the nature, value, or quality of; to estimate the value of; to impose (a tax or fine)
chinese: 評估；評定；估價；課徵（稅款或罰款）
example: Scientists are beginning to assess the toll on wildlife, particularly endangered koala populations.

definition: to declare earnestly or solemnly
chinese: 鄭重宣稱；斷言；堅稱
example: The witness continued to asseverate that the document was authentic.

definition: an earnest, emphatic declaration
chinese: 鄭重宣告；斷言；堅稱
example: In this context, “asseveration” refers to a declaration that is made emphatically (as if no supporting evidence were necessary).

definition: showing great care, attention, and persistent effort
chinese: 勤勉的；刻苦的；專心仔細的；孜孜不倦的
example: The passage describes its subject as assiduous, meaning marked by care and persistent effort.

definition: to take in and understand; to absorb into a culture or the body; to integrate; to make similar; to liken
chinese: 吸收；理解；同化；融入；使相似；比作
example: It can be difficult for newcomers to a country to assimilate.

definition: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense; to calm; to satisfy (an appetite or desire)
chinese: 緩和；減輕；平息；滿足（慾望）
example: This medicine will assuage the pain.

definition: to suppose without proof; to take on (responsibility or office); to take on (a form); to pretend to have
chinese: 假定；以為；承擔（責任）；就任；呈現（樣子）；假裝
example: I assume his train was late

definition: to tell someone positively to remove doubt; to make certain; to secure
chinese: 保證；使確信；使放心；確保
example: The bank's actions seemed to assure investors about the soundness of the governmental bonds.

definition: a small rocky body orbiting the sun; a starfish; shaped like a star
chinese: n. 小行星；（動物）海星；adj. 星狀的
example: The direction the asteroid is orbiting the sun is what clued scientists into its interstellar origins.

definition: so surprising as to cause amazement
chinese: 令人震驚的；驚人的；出乎意料的
example: His arrogance was astounding; he actually believed his uninformed opinion was better than the experts’.

definition: relating to astronomy; (of an amount) extremely large
chinese: 天文學的；天文的；（數量）龐大的；天文數字的
example: The eye-catching posters depict some of the universe's most mysterious astronomical phenomena with artistic flair.

definition: the science of celestial objects and the universe as a whole
chinese: 天文學
example: He was a great authority on astronomy, or the science of the heavenly bodies.

definition: having an ability to assess situations accurately and turn them to advantage; shrewd
chinese: 精明的；機敏的；有洞察力的
example: An astute reader should be willing to weigh everything they read, including anonymous sources.

definition: apart or into pieces; separated by distance
chinese: 成碎片地；分開地；（相距）遙遠地
example: The cabin was torn asunder by the storm.

definition: protection given to refugees; a place of refuge; (dated) a mental hospital; an institution for the needy
chinese: 庇護；政治庇護；避難所；（舊）精神病院；收容所
example: Lukas will probably end up back in the asylum for the things he did.

definition: lacking symmetry or balance; unequal
chinese: 不對稱的；不均衡的；不對等的
example: You claim an inequitable exchange on asymmetrical bases.

definition: in disagreement or conflict; inconsistent
chinese: 不一致；相矛盾；意見不合；不和
example: the figures are at odds with our findings

definition: the smallest unit of a chemical element; a very small particle or amount
chinese: 原子；微粒；極少量
example: Scientists long ago ceased to believe that the atom is the smallest unit of matter.

definition: to make amends or reparation for a wrong
chinese: 贖罪；彌補；補償
example: The salaryman went to live quietly in a remote area in order to atone for his sins.

definition: extremely wicked or cruel; of very poor quality
chinese: 殘暴的；兇殘的；極惡劣的；糟透的
example: He is apt to say atrocious things and to exaggerate his grievances.

definition: an extremely cruel or wicked act; shocking cruelty; something very bad or ugly
chinese: 暴行；殘暴；兇殘；糟透的事物
example: It is hard to believe that humans are capable of such atrocity.

definition: to waste away or decline through disuse; the wasting away of a body part or decline in effectiveness
chinese: v. 萎縮；衰退；n. 萎縮；衰退
example: Astronauts' muscles atrophy when they spend a long time in zero gravity.

definition: to reduce the force, value, or effect of; to make thin or slender; to weaken a signal
chinese: 減弱；削弱；使稀薄；使變細；（訊號）衰減
example: Water will attenuate the signal.

definition: to provide evidence of; to declare to be true; to serve as proof
chinese: 證實；證明；作證；為…的證據
example: The fingerprints on the knife attest to her guilt.

definition: pleasing or appealing to the senses or mind; advantageous
chinese: 吸引人的；有魅力的；誘人的
example: a remarkably attractive young man

definition: to regard as caused by or belonging to; a quality or feature characteristic of someone or something; a symbol
chinese: v. 歸因於；歸功於；認為…屬於；n. 屬性；特質；特徵；象徵物
example: Physical strength is an important attribute as far as search and rescue dogs are concerned.

definition: gradual weakening through sustained pressure; reduction in staff by natural loss; wearing away by friction
chinese: 消耗；（人員）自然減少；削弱；磨損；摩擦
example: Rapid attrition in the number of employees led to an increased workload for those who remained.

definition: to make receptive or aware; to bring into harmony; to tune
chinese: 使協調；使適應；使和諧；（樂器）調音

definition: to express strong disapproval of; to sentence; to declare unfit for use; to doom to an unpleasant fate

definition: to accept or overlook (wrongdoing); to forgive

definition: tending to promote or bring about

definition: feeling or showing self-assurance; certain

chinese: 匯合；匯流處；（因素等）匯聚；人群

definition: to bewilder; to mistake one thing for another; to make unclear or disordered

chinese: adj. 技藝高超的；完美的；道地的；v. 完成；使圓滿；完婚

chinese: v. 收縮；感染（疾病）；染上（習慣）；訂約；n. 合約；契約
