example: The passage describes its subject as distal, meaning situated farthest from point of attachment or origin, as of a limb or bone.

definition: a feeling of dislike or aversion
chinese: 厭惡；反感
example: My apathy for voting comes from my distaste for politics.

definition: to swell or cause to swell from internal pressure
chinese: （使）膨脹；（使）腫脹
example: The gas caused the sealed container to distend visibly.

definition: to extract the essential meaning of; to purify by vaporizing and condensing
chinese: 提煉；萃取精華；蒸餾
example: Now we will distill this water.

definition: characteristic and serving to distinguish; unusual and noticeable
chinese: 獨特的；與眾不同的；有特色的
example: When mosquitoes beat their wings up and down, they produce a distinctive buzzing sound.

definition: to misrepresent or give a false account of; to twist out of shape
chinese: 扭曲；歪曲；曲解；使變形
example: There are many minor mistakes and tiny misunderstandings here that distort the meaning of the original sentence.

definition: misrepresentation; a twisting out of shape; change in a signal's waveform
chinese: 扭曲；曲解；變形；（訊號）失真
example: I don't think color blindness can be cured since it's a distortion in the eye.

definition: to draw attention away; to divert; to trouble or agitate
chinese: 使分心；轉移（注意力）；使心煩意亂
example: When a person can't find a deep sense of meaning, they distract themselves with pleasure.

definition: deeply upset and agitated
chinese: 心煩意亂的；極度不安的；發狂的
example: I was distraught over what to do because everything was going poorly.

definition: to give out shares of; to spread over an area; to supply (goods) to retailers
chinese: 分配；分發；散布；分銷
example: The boiler room contains the heating equipment used to distribute heat throughout the mall.

definition: to interrupt; to interfere with normal functioning; to make anxious; to move from its position
chinese: 打擾；擾亂；使不安；弄亂
example: Emily is studying in her room right now, so please do not disturb her.

definition: active during the daytime; occurring every day
chinese: 日間活動的；白天的；每日的
example: Degus make lovely pets: they are diurnal and hence are awake when you are.

definition: to differ; to deviate from a standard; to move apart in different directions
chinese: 分歧；偏離；岔開；分道揚鑣
example: On the best time to drink this wine, opinions diverge.

definition: differing from each other or from a standard; moving apart
chinese: 有分歧的；相異的；分岔的；（思考）發散的
example: a divergent opinion

definition: the state of being varied; inclusion of people from different backgrounds
chinese: 多樣性；多元化；差異
example: Scientists are studying the genetic diversity of nightshades to evolve more resistant cultivars.

definition: to change the course of; to distract; to reallocate (funds); to amuse
chinese: 使轉向；轉移（注意力）；挪用；使消遣
example: In addition to informing, news can also divert.

definition: to deprive of; to rid oneself of; to sell off (assets or investments)
chinese: 剝奪；使擺脫；撤資；脫去
example: Many farmers had to divest themselves of stock during the drought to save on feeding costs.

definition: the selling off of assets or holdings; the act of depriving
chinese: 撤資；出售資產；剝奪
example: In this context, “divestiture” refers to an order to an offending party to rid itself of property; it has the purpose of depriving the defendant of the gains of wrongful behavior.

definition: the practice of seeking knowledge of the future by supernatural means
chinese: 占卜；預言；預測
example: Augury is divination based on the behavior of birds.

definition: to make known (private or secret information)
chinese: 洩露；透露（祕密）
example: His secret was a shameful one, and he could not bring himself to divulge it.

definition: ready to accept control or instruction; submissive
chinese: 溫順的；馴服的；易於管教的
example: the docile masses of an enslaved nation

definition: to falsify or tamper with; to adulterate; to treat medically; a physician; a holder of a doctorate
chinese: v. 竄改；篡改；摻雜；治療；n. 醫生；博士
example: Rishi wanted to study civil engineering, despite his parents wishing he'd become a doctor.

definition: rigidly applying a theory without regard to practicality; a doctrinaire person
chinese: adj. 教條主義的；死守理論的；n. 教條主義者
example: His doctrinaire approach left no room for evidence that challenged the theory.

definition: to record in detail; to support with evidence; a written or official record
chinese: v. 記錄；以文件證明；n. 文件；文獻
example: The consulate said it notarized his signature, but not the contents of the document.

definition: to move feebly or unsteadily; a leafless parasitic vine
chinese: v. 蹣跚；顫巍巍地走；n. （植物）菟絲子
example: In this context, “dodder” means a leafless annual parasitic vine of the genus Cuscuta having whitish or yellow filamentous stems; obtain nourishment through haustoria.

definition: to avoid by moving quickly; to evade (a duty or question); a sudden evasive move; a trick
chinese: v. 閃避；躲避；規避；n. 閃躲；伎倆
example: Remember to press the dodge button immediately after the dragon opens its mouth.

definition: to take off (clothing, especially a hat); to discard
chinese: 脫下；脫（帽致敬）；拋棄
example: In this context, “doff” means remove.

definition: to trouble persistently; to follow closely; a domesticated canine; a contemptible person
chinese: v. 困擾；纏擾；尾隨；n. 狗；卑鄙的人
example: Better to be the head of a dog than the tail of a lion.

definition: showing persistent, stubborn determination
chinese: 頑強的；堅持不懈的；固執的
example: It is the dogged who wins.

definition: with persistent, stubborn determination
chinese: 頑強地；堅持不懈地；固執地
example: he pursued her doggedly

definition: a set of principles held as unquestionably true by an authority
chinese: 教條；教義；信條
example: Loving, of enemies is another dogma of feigned morality, and has besides no meaning.

definition: asserting opinions as undeniably true
chinese: 武斷的；教條的；自以為是的
example: It's profound ignorance that inspires the dogmatic tone of speaking.

definition: the tendency to assert opinions as undeniably true
chinese: 武斷；教條主義
example: The tone of dogmatism is inspired by profound ignorance.

definition: a state of stagnation or depression; a calm equatorial region of the ocean
chinese: 低迷；停滯；消沉；（航海）赤道無風帶
example: It will be some time before the economy will move out of the current doldrums.

definition: expressing sorrow; mournful
chinese: 悲傷的；憂鬱的；哀戚的
example: the child's doleful expression

definition: feeling or expressing great sorrow
chinese: 憂傷的；悲痛的；哀戚的
example: A dolorous melody accompanied the final scene of the play.

definition: a stupid person
chinese: 笨蛋；傻瓜
example: Only a dolt could fail to understand what was implied by that letter.

definition: a field of knowledge or activity; an area under control; the set of possible inputs of a function; an internet domain
chinese: 領域；範圍；領土；（數學）定義域；（網路）網域
example: For f(x)=2x+1, when the domain of the function is [1,2], the range is [3,5].

definition: a person's home; one's legal place of residence; to settle in a place
chinese: n. 住所；（法律）居住地；v. 使定居
example: He saw her to her home and then hastened to his own humble domicile.

definition: most influential or controlling; most prominent; (of a gene) expressed over another
chinese: 占支配地位的；主導的；顯著的；（遺傳）顯性的
example: Quartzite is a white or pinkish rock, in which the dominant mineral is quartz.

definition: to rule over arrogantly; to act in an overbearing way
chinese: 專橫跋扈；作威作福；壓制
example: He tried unsuccessfully to domineer over his office workers.

definition: a game played with small rectangular tiles; such tiles
chinese: 骨牌遊戲；骨牌
example: In the smoking room, there were always parties of gentlemen playing euchre, draughts and dominoes.

definition: to put on (clothing); a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge; a Spanish title of respect
chinese: v. 穿上；戴上；n. （英國大學）教師；（西班牙）先生
example: His plans always sound great in theory but they don't work in practice.

definition: to give to a charity or good cause; to give (blood or an organ)
chinese: 捐贈；捐獻；捐（血）
example: There is an urgent need for more people to donate their time and money.

definition: a person who gives money or goods; a person who gives blood or an organ
chinese: 捐贈者；捐款人；（器官或血液）捐贈者
example: She needs a bone marrow transplant, but she has not found a donor yet.

definition: to scribble absentmindedly; to pass time aimlessly; an absentminded drawing
chinese: v. 塗鴉；隨手亂畫；閒混；n. 塗鴉
example: Do you ever doodle on a piece of paper when you're bored?

definition: death, ruin, or an inescapable bad fate; to condemn to certain failure
chinese: n. 厄運；毀滅；死亡；v. 註定（失敗）
example: This is one of the signs of weakness and the impending doom of imperialism.

definition: temporarily inactive; in a resting state; latent
chinese: 休眠的；蟄伏的；潛伏的；暫停活動的
example: The scientists say the insects lay dormant, feeding on tree roots and slowly growing underground.

definition: a building providing living quarters for students
chinese: 宿舍；學生宿舍
example: He soon got accustomed to dormitory life and made two or three friends.

definition: gloomy and unfriendly in manner; stern; stubborn
chinese: 陰沉的；冷峻的；嚴厲的；固執的
example: He's always been a dour twat with a face like a cat's arse.

definition: to drench with liquid; to plunge into water; to extinguish (a fire or light)
chinese: 澆濕；潑水；浸入；熄滅
example: You can douse a grease fire by covering the pan with a lid.

definition: favoring peaceful policies; favoring loose monetary policy
chinese: 鴿派的；主張和平的；（金融）傾向寬鬆的
example: He's both a hawkish dove and a dovish hawk.

definition: to make something seem less important than it is; to minimize
chinese: 淡化；輕描淡寫；貶低重要性
example: Laura may be a prodigy, but she is known to downplay her failures.

definition: the most respected or senior member of a group or profession
chinese: （某領域的）元老；資深人士；前輩
example: In this context, “doyen” refers to a man who is the senior member of a group.

definition: to sleep lightly; a short light sleep
chinese: v. 打瞌睡；小睡；n. 瞌睡；小憩
example: The lecture was pretty boring, so I started to doze off.

definition: dull and monotonous; lacking brightness; of a dull light brown color; a dull brownish color
chinese: adj. 單調乏味的；黯淡的；土褐色的；n. 土褐色
example: This morning, the world is grey and drab.

definition: (of laws or measures) excessively harsh and severe
chinese: 嚴苛的；極其嚴厲的
example: The mesmerizing animations further distracted customers from the draconian terms of service.

definition: sudden and striking; very noticeable; relating to drama or the theater
chinese: 顯著的；驚人的；戲劇性的；戲劇的
example: But when the test results are broken down by subgroup, the differences are dramatic.

definition: to speak slowly with prolonged vowels; a slow, drawn-out manner of speaking
chinese: v. 拉長調子慢吞吞地說；n. 慢吞吞的腔調
example: In this context, “drawl” means a slow speech pattern with prolonged vowels.

definition: great fear or apprehension; to fear greatly; causing great fear
chinese: n. 恐懼；畏懼；v. 懼怕；擔憂；adj. 可怕的
example: Dread shapes and forms terrific loomed in sight, / and hostile deities, whose faces frowned / destruction.

definition: dull, bleak, and depressing; lacking cheer
chinese: 沉悶的；單調乏味的；陰鬱的
example: Then, although it was dreary up to the other day, everywhere were flowers, flowers, flowers.

definition: to make thoroughly wet; to soak
chinese: 使溼透；浸透
example: After a while, dressing in the recommended long pants and long sleeved-shirt during a summer hike can really drench your clothes.

definition: silly nonsense; to talk nonsense; to let saliva drip
chinese: n. 胡說八道；廢話；v. 說廢話；流口水
example: Some critics loved the film, while others did not, one calling it sanctimonious drivel.

definition: the quality of being amusing in an odd or wry way
chinese: 滑稽；詼諧；冷幽默
example: The narrator's quiet drollness keeps the serious story from becoming grim.

definition: to speak in a dull monotonous tone; to make a low humming sound; a low hum; an idler; an unmanned aircraft; a male bee
chinese: v. 低沉單調地說；發出嗡嗡聲；n. 嗡嗡聲；遊手好閒者；無人機；雄蜂
example: The drone can recognize which flying insects are beneficial and avoid them.

definition: hard, menial, or dull work
chinese: 苦差事；單調乏味的工作
example: With all its sham, drudgery and broken dreams; it is still a beautiful world.

definition: to obtain or stir up (support, business, interest) by persistent effort
chinese: 竭力爭取；招攬；激起
example: drum up support

definition: open to doubt; questionable; feeling doubt or uncertainty
chinese: 可疑的；靠不住的；半信半疑的；猶豫的
example: I'm dubious about claims to speak more than five languages fluently.

definition: to evade (a duty or question); to lower the head or body quickly to avoid something; a water bird
chinese: v. 迴避；閃避；低頭彎身；n. 鴨子
example: Before he could duck, another stone struck him

definition: (of metal) able to be drawn out into wire; easily molded; easily influenced or led
chinese: （金屬）可延展的；易塑造的；易受影響的；順從的
example: Copper is both ductile and conductive, making it ideal for electrical wiring.

definition: owed or payable; expected at a certain time; proper or appropriate; that which is deserved; fees
chinese: adj. 應付的；到期的；應有的；預定的；n. 應得之物；會費
example: payment is due

definition: (of sound) sweet and pleasing to the ear; soothing
chinese: （聲音）悅耳的；甜美的
example: The passage describes its subject as dulcet, meaning extremely pleasant in a gentle way.

definition: a slow or stupid person
chinese: 笨蛋；遲鈍的人
example: In this context, “dullard” refers to a person who is not very bright.

definition: to deceive or trick; a person who is easily deceived
chinese: v. 欺騙；愚弄；n. 易受騙的人；冤大頭
example: Don't be such a dupe!

definition: an exact copy; to make an exact copy of; to repeat; exactly like something else
chinese: n. 副本；複製品；v. 複製；重複；adj. 完全相同的；複製的
example: It would be wise to get a duplicate key made as soon as you can.

definition: deceitful; marked by double-dealing
chinese: 口是心非的；奸詐的；表裡不一的
example: The audit exposed a duplicitous effort to conceal the missing funds.

definition: deceitfulness; double-dealing
chinese: 口是心非；表裡不一；欺騙
example: In this context, “duplicity” refers to acting in bad faith; deception by pretending to entertain one set of intentions while acting under the influence of another.

definition: to make seem small by comparison; a person or thing much smaller than usual; unusually small
chinese: v. 使相形見絀；使顯得矮小；n. 侏儒；矮子；adj. 矮小的
example: The stunning photos reveal a complex and varied terrain on the icy dwarf planet.

definition: to diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength
chinese: 逐漸減少；縮小；衰退
example: We've made great inroads into solving the problem, but our resources dwindle and the end is not in sight.

definition: irritable and bad-tempered; suffering from indigestion; a person with indigestion
chinese: adj. 脾氣暴躁的；消化不良的；n. 消化不良者
example: The passage describes its subject as dyspeptic, meaning a person suffering from indigestion.

definition: serious and sincere in intention or effort; seriousness (as in 'in earnest'); a deposit given as a pledge
chinese: adj. 認真的；誠摯的；嚴肅的；n. 認真；保證金
example: He began courting her in earnest when he found out that she had another suitor.

definition: extremely loud
chinese: 震耳欲聾的
example: The passage describes its subject as earsplitting, meaning loud enough to cause (temporary) hearing loss.

definition: to listen secretly to a private conversation
chinese: 偷聽；竊聽
example: She put her ear against the door to eavesdrop on a conversation taking place in the neighbouring room.

definition: to decline or diminish gradually; (of the tide) to recede; a state of decline; the receding of the tide
chinese: v. 衰退；減弱；退潮；n. 衰落；低潮；退潮
example: Relations between us seem to be on the ebb.

definition: exuberant enthusiasm and high spirits; the state of boiling
chinese: 熱情洋溢；興高采烈；沸騰
example: She had lost weight; the "puppy fat" and the ebullience had gone.

definition: overflowing with enthusiasm and excitement; boiling
chinese: 熱情洋溢的；興高采烈的；沸騰的
example: Emma is obviously ecstatic with her ebullient expressions after answering something excruciatingly difficult.

definition: unconventional and slightly strange; not having the same center; an odd or unconventional person
chinese: adj. 古怪的；反常的；（圓）不同心的；n. 怪人
example: Do not fear to be eccentric in opinion, for every opinion now accepted was once eccentric.

definition: drawing ideas or style from a wide range of sources; a person who selects from various sources
chinese: adj. 兼容並蓄的；多元的；折衷的；n. 折衷主義者
example: Her eclectic taste was evident from the unusual decor of the room.

definition: to overshadow or surpass; to obscure the light of; the obscuring of one celestial body by another; a loss of significance
chinese: v. 使黯然失色；使相形見絀；遮蔽；n. 日蝕；月蝕；衰落
example: There are too many clouds to be able to gaze at the eclipse properly.

definition: an overwhelming feeling of joy or rapture; a trance-like state
chinese: 狂喜；出神；入迷
example: To burn always with this hard, gem-like flame, to maintain this ecstasy, is success in life.

definition: feeling or expressing overwhelming happiness; in a trance-like state
chinese: 狂喜的；欣喜若狂的；出神的
example: Emma is obviously ecstatic with her ebullient expressions after answering something excruciatingly difficult.

definition: worldwide or general in scope; promoting unity among Christian churches or religions
chinese: 普世的；普遍的；促進基督教各派合一的；跨宗派的
example: When developing an ecumenical service, take care not to offend members of any denomination.

definition: fit to be eaten; something that can be eaten
chinese: adj. 可食用的；n. 食物
example: There are more than twenty thousand known species of edible plants in the world.

definition: a large, imposing building; a complex system of beliefs or ideas
chinese: 大建築物；大廈；（思想等的）體系；架構
example: Thousands of laborers and craftsmen toiled for 22 years to craft the stunning white marble edifice.

definition: to instruct or improve someone morally or intellectually
chinese: 啟迪；教誨；陶冶
example: Good books can edify the mind as well as entertain it.

definition: providing moral or intellectual instruction or improvement
chinese: 有教育意義的；啟發性的；陶冶性情的
example: the paintings in the church served an edifying purpose even for those who could not read

definition: strange and frightening; suggestive of the supernatural
chinese: 怪異的；陰森的；令人毛骨悚然的
example: an eerie feeling of deja vu

definition: to erase or wipe out; to make oneself inconspicuous
chinese: 抹去；消除；使不顯眼
example: I tried to efface the memory of her tears.

definition: the act of erasing or removing; making oneself inconspicuous; thinning of the cervix during labor
chinese: 抹去；消除；（自我）隱沒；（醫學）子宮頸變薄
example: In this context, “effacement” refers to shortening of the uterine cervix and thinning of its walls as it is dilated during labor.

definition: to give off bubbles; to be lively and enthusiastic
chinese: 冒泡；起泡沫；興奮；熱情洋溢
example: In this context, “effervesce” means become bubbly or frothy or foaming.

definition: no longer vigorous or effective; worn out; affected and over-refined
chinese: 衰弱的；頹廢的；精疲力盡的；柔弱做作的
example: The once-mighty empire had grown effete, bloated with luxury and devoid of vigor.

definition: successful in producing the intended result; effective
chinese: 有效的；靈驗的
example: The treatment proved efficacious in reducing the symptoms.

definition: an unpleasant or harmful odor or discharge
chinese: 臭氣；難聞的氣味；（有害的）排出物
example: In this context, “effluvium” refers to a foul-smelling outflow or vapor (especially a gaseous waste).

definition: insolent or impertinent behavior; shameless boldness
chinese: 厚顏無恥；放肆
example: His effrontery has turned everyone in the firm against him.

definition: shining brightly; radiant
chinese: 光輝燦爛的；耀眼的
example: The passage describes its subject as effulgent, meaning radiating or as if radiating light.

definition: expressing feelings in an unrestrained or excessive way
chinese: 熱情洋溢的；感情奔放的；過分熱情的
example: She always gives me such an effusive welcome when I visit her.

definition: believing in or promoting equal rights for all people; a person who holds such beliefs
chinese: adj. 平等主義的；主張人人平等的；n. 平等主義者
example: Bonobos are also different in that they have a more egalitarian and cooperative society than chimpanzees.

definition: thinking only of oneself without regard for others; self-centered
chinese: 自我中心的；只顧自己的
example: Our genetic material is being constantly invaded by small egocentric molecular parasites.

definition: concerned chiefly with one's own interests; selfish
chinese: 利己的；自私的；自我中心的
example: Children are completely egoistic; they feel their needs intensely and strive ruthlessly to satisfy them.

definition: outstandingly bad; shocking; flagrant
chinese: 極其惡劣的；駭人聽聞的；過分的
example: The dictator’s abuse of human rights was so egregious that many world leaders asked that he be tried in an international court for genocide.

definition: to force or throw out; to expel from a place or position
chinese: 逐出；驅逐；噴出；彈出
example: When the lead gets stuck in the pencil sharpener, you can press the back button to eject it.

definition: involving many carefully arranged parts or details; to explain or develop in greater detail
chinese: adj. 精心製作的；複雜的；詳盡的；v. 詳細闡述；精心製作
example: To defend the city, they built an elaborate system of tunnels of their own.

definition: the addition of more detail or explanation; the process of developing something in detail
chinese: 詳細闡述；詳述；精心製作；精巧
example: Further elaboration or ornament would only detract from the perfection of its simplicity.

definition: able to return to its original shape after stretching; flexible or adaptable; able to recover quickly; an elastic band
chinese: adj. 有彈性的；有伸縮性的；靈活的；能迅速恢復的；n. 鬆緊帶
example: A corset, if one is worn, should not extend below the waist-line, and should have elastic side-lacing.

definition: to make very happy or proud; to fill with high spirits
chinese: 使興高采烈；使振奮
example: In this context, “elate” means fill with high spirits; fill with optimism.

definition: very happy and excited; jubilant
chinese: 興高采烈的；歡欣鼓舞的
example: the elated winner

definition: a formal vote to choose a person for office; the fact of being elected; choice
chinese: 選舉；當選；選擇；（神學）揀選
example: the results of the election will be announced tonight

definition: relating to or dependent on charity; charitable
chinese: 慈善的；施捨的；救濟的

definition: to cause someone to become unfriendly or no longer close; to alienate
chinese: 使疏遠；使失和；離間

definition: the state of being alienated or no longer on friendly terms
chinese: 疏遠；失和；隔閡
example: William is working to rebuild his relationship with his son after a period of estrangement.

definition: to impress deeply on the mind; to engrave a design by corroding with acid
chinese: 銘刻；使銘記；蝕刻
example: If you don't wash away the acid quickly, it will etch its way into the metal.

definition: lasting forever; without end; seemingly endless
chinese: 永恆的；永遠的；無休止的
example: There's nothing more fleeting than an eternity, nor something more eternal than a moment.

definition: extremely delicate and light, seemingly not of this world; heavenly or spiritual
chinese: 空靈的；輕盈精緻的；超凡脫俗的；天上的
example: Jamin's perfectly symmetrical features give her an ethereal and timeless beauty.

definition: moral principles governing conduct; the branch of philosophy dealing with morality
chinese: 倫理；道德規範；倫理學
example: At the ethics committee, a temporary halt to cloning experiments was decided.

definition: the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a culture, era, or community
chinese: 風氣；精神特質；氣質；道德觀
example: Settling down and raising a family was against the ethos of the times.

definition: to praise highly in speech or writing, especially in a funeral oration
chinese: 頌揚；稱讚；致悼詞
example: In this context, “eulogize” means praise formally and eloquently.

definition: a speech or piece of writing praising someone, especially one who has just died; high praise
chinese: 悼詞；頌詞；讚美
example: I've been asked to give the eulogy at my grandmother's funeral.

definition: a mild or indirect word substituted for one considered harsh or blunt
chinese: 委婉語；委婉說法
example: It's a euphemism to say that you have to have your dog "put to sleep."

definition: pleasing to the ear; harmonious
chinese: 悅耳的；聲音和諧的
example: In the evening quiet, we enjoy the song of the euphonious nightingale.

definition: a feeling of intense excitement and happiness
chinese: 極度興奮；狂喜；欣快感
example: The euphoria of victory does not blind us to the realities of the moment.

definition: to remove people from a dangerous place; to leave a place; to empty; to discharge waste from the body
chinese: 撤離；疏散；排空；排泄
example: The highway was clogged with traffic as people tried to evacuate the area.

definition: to escape or avoid, especially by cleverness or trickery; to avoid answering or performing
chinese: 逃避；規避；迴避（問題）；躲避
example: The dense vegetation of the mangrove swamp provided excellent cover for small animals trying to evade predators.

definition: soon passing out of sight or existence; fleeting
chinese: 轉瞬即逝的；短暫的；逐漸消失的
example: The passage describes its subject as evanescent, meaning tending to vanish like vapor.

definition: to turn from liquid into vapor; to disappear gradually; to remove water from
chinese: 蒸發；（逐漸）消失；使脫水
example: evaporate milk

definition: tending to avoid commitment or direct answers; directed toward avoidance or escape
chinese: 閃爍其詞的；迴避的；逃避的
example: his answers were brief, constrained and evasive

definition: to occur as a result; to happen in the end
chinese: 最終導致；結果是；發生
example: The rain forecast for yesterday didn't eventuate.

definition: lasting forever or for a very long time; tiresomely prolonged; eternity; a flower that keeps its color when dried
chinese: adj. 永恆的；持久的；沒完沒了的；n. 永恆；（植物）蠟菊
example: Our experiences left us with everlasting scars in our souls.

definition: to expel someone from a property, especially by legal process
chinese: 驅逐；逐出（房客）
example: If you don't pay rent, the landlord will evict you.

definition: proof or grounds for belief; a sign or indication; to show or prove clearly
chinese: n. 證據；跡象；根據；v. 證明；顯示
example: The foundation of scientific theory is based on empirical data and hard evidence.

definition: clearly seen or understood; obvious
chinese: 明顯的；顯然的
example: As is evident from the data, smoking is not decreasing among the young.

definition: to show clearly; to reveal (a feeling or quality)
chinese: 表明；顯示；證明
example: The early sketches evince the artist's careful attention to proportion.

definition: bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind; vividly suggestive
chinese: 引起聯想的；喚起回憶的；生動傳神的
example: The gentle purr of the turtle dove is an evocative sound of summer.

definition: to bring a feeling, memory, or image to mind; to produce a response
chinese: 喚起；引起；使想起
example: In interpersonal relations, nothing is more important than the ability to evoke sympathy.

definition: gradual development; (biology) the process by which species change over generations
chinese: 演變；逐步發展；（生物）演化；進化
example: The study of biology has helped us better understand the evolution of life on earth.

definition: to make a problem, situation, or feeling worse
chinese: 使惡化；使加劇
example: Hot and blustery conditions will exacerbate the risk of fire tomorrow.

definition: making great demands; rigorous; requiring much effort or skill; (participle of exact) demanding or inflicting
chinese: adj. 要求嚴格的；苛求的；費力的；v. 強索；施加（報復）
example: Ziri is even more hellbent on exacting revenge.

definition: the quality of being exact; precision; rigor
chinese: 精確；嚴謹；準確性
example: In this context, “exactitude” refers to the quality of being exact.

definition: to praise highly; to raise in rank or power; to elate
chinese: 讚揚；頌揚；提升（地位）；使得意
example: The party will continue to exalt their hero.

definition: to irritate intensely; to infuriate; to make (a bad feeling or situation) worse
chinese: 激怒；使惱火；使（情況）加劇
example: No coaxing could induce them to advance, and the application of the whip only seemed to exasperate their obstinacy.

definition: to dig out or dig up; to uncover (an archaeological site) by digging; to hollow out
chinese: 挖掘；發掘（遺址）；挖空
example: Archaeologists plan to excavate the site without disturbing the lower layers.

definition: unusually good; outstanding; unusual; forming an exception
chinese: 傑出的；非凡的；例外的；特殊的
example: Their articles are exceptional, even considering that they have already been very successful.

definition: to cry out suddenly, especially in surprise, anger, or joy
chinese: 驚呼；呼喊；大聲說出
example: In this context, “exclaim” means utter aloud; often with surprise, horror, or joy.

definition: to criticize severely; to denounce; to strip or abrade the skin
chinese: 嚴厲批評；痛斥；擦傷（皮膚）
example: In this context, “excoriate” means express strong disapproval of.

definition: severe criticism or censure; an area where the skin is abraded
chinese: 嚴厲譴責；痛斥；（皮膚）擦傷；表皮脫落
example: In this context, “excoriation” refers to severe censure.

definition: to discharge waste matter from the body
chinese: 排泄；排出
example: When someone is diabetic, they excrete sugar in their urine.

definition: to inflict intense pain on; to torment mentally or physically
chinese: 使極度痛苦；折磨
example: In this context, “excruciate” means torment emotionally or mentally.

definition: intensely painful; agonizing; unbearable; (of detail) excessively thorough
chinese: 極度痛苦的；折磨人的；難以忍受的；（細節）極其詳盡的
example: Listening to the orator's incoherent ramblings was excruciating.

definition: to clear from blame or guilt; to show to be innocent
chinese: 開脫罪責；使無罪；證明無辜
example: The witness's testimony helped exculpate the driver after the accident.

definition: the act of clearing from guilt or blame; a justification or excuse
chinese: 開脫罪責；免罪；辯解
example: In this context, “exculpation” refers to the act of freeing from guilt or blame.

definition: tending to digress from the main point; rambling; wide-ranging
chinese: 離題的；散漫的；東拉西扯的
example: The passage describes its subject as excursive, meaning (of e.g. speech and writing) tending to depart from the main point or cover a wide range of subjects.

definition: to forgive; to justify or try to justify; to release from an obligation; a reason given to justify a fault; a pretext
chinese: v. 原諒；為…辯解；免除；n. 藉口；理由
example: Please excuse my dirty hands

definition: to detest; to loathe; to curse; to denounce
chinese: 痛恨；憎惡；咒罵；痛斥
example: Interestingly, the adjective form of execrate is the relatively common GRE word execrable. If something is execrable, it is so awful that it is worthy of our hissing.

definition: critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially scripture
chinese: （經文）詮釋；註釋；評註
example: The Bible is fertile ground for exegesis—over the past five centuries there have been as many interpretations as there are pages in a Gideon.

definition: serving as a model; worthy of imitation; typical; (of punishment) serving as a warning
chinese: 模範的；值得效法的；典型的；懲戒性的
example: The child's behaviour and attitude towards his fellow students was exemplary.

definition: to be a typical example of; to illustrate by example
chinese: 作為…的典型；例示；舉例說明
example: I heard your idea on how to solve the problem, but I would have to ask you to exemplify what you mean.

definition: to free from an obligation or liability; free from an obligation or liability imposed on others
chinese: v. 使免除；豁免；adj. 被免除的；豁免的
example: None can exempt himself from loving; for none can live without a heart, nor the heart without love.

definition: to apply or bring to bear (force, influence); to make use of; to make a strenuous effort
chinese: 施加；運用；發揮；盡力
example: exert one's power or influence

definition: to use up completely; to tire out; to treat a subject thoroughly; waste gases from an engine; an exhaust pipe
chinese: v. 耗盡；使筋疲力竭；徹底探討；n. 廢氣；排氣管
example: There are many things that harm young saplings, such as insects, car exhaust, and typhoons.

definition: to make very happy or lively; to elate; to invigorate
chinese: 使興高采烈；使振奮；使興奮
example: In this context, “exhilarate” means fill with sublime emotion.

definition: to urge strongly; to encourage earnestly
chinese: 力勸；敦促；激勵
example: In this context, “exhort” means spur on or encourage especially by cheers and shouts.

definition: requiring immediate action; urgent; demanding
chinese: 緊急的；迫切的；苛求的
example: The hospital reserved its limited supplies for the most exigent cases.

definition: extremely scanty; meager
chinese: 稀少的；微薄的；極少的
example: an exiguous budget

definition: the state of being banished from one's country; a person who lives in exile; to banish; to expel from one's country
chinese: n. 流亡；放逐；流亡者；v. 放逐；流放
example: A large number of them have been forced into exile or have passed away.

definition: a mass departure of people; an emigration
chinese: 大批離去；（人口）大量外移；出走
example: Spain's countryside is suffering a slow demise after the long exodus of its rural population.

definition: to clear from blame or guilt; to free from an obligation
chinese: 證明無罪；開脫；免除（責任）
example: New laboratory evidence may exonerate the wrongly accused technician.

definition: (of price or demand) unreasonably high; excessive
chinese: （價格）過高的；過度的；離譜的
example: Some generous souls made exorbitant donations that helped save the orphanage.

definition: to get rid of (a troubling memory or feeling); to drive out (an evil spirit) by prayer or ritual
chinese: 擺脫；消除；驅邪；驅魔
example: We exorcise you, every unclean spirit, every satanic power, every incursion of the infernal adversary, every legion, every congregation and diabolical sect.

definition: originating in a foreign country; strikingly unusual or strange
chinese: 外來的；異國情調的；奇特的；不尋常的
example: Kepler has found a diverse array of planets, including exotic, multi-planet solar systems.

definition: talkative and open; genial; covering a wide area; wide-ranging; tending to expand
chinese: 健談的；開朗的；廣闊的；廣泛的；擴張性的
example: After a few sips of cognac, the octogenarian shed his irascible demeanor and became expansive, speaking fondly of the “good old days”.

definition: the quality of being convenient and practical though perhaps improper; self-interest; advantageousness
chinese: 權宜之計；私利考量；方便；得當
example: In this context, “expediency” refers to the quality of being suited to the end in view.

definition: convenient and practical, though possibly improper; advantageous; a means to an end; a makeshift measure
chinese: adj. 權宜的；有利的；方便的；n. 權宜之計；應急手段
example: was merciful only when mercy was expedient

definition: to speed up the progress of; to accomplish quickly
chinese: 加速；促進；迅速處理
example: I created this automatic program to expedite the banal task of sorting these images.

definition: money spent; cost; something sacrificed to gain something else; loss
chinese: 費用；開支；代價；損失
example: Such an economic program will help the rich at the expense of the poor.

definition: to atone for (guilt or sin); to make amends for
chinese: 贖（罪）；補償；彌補

definition: to come to an end; to cease to be valid; to die; to breathe out
chinese: 到期；屆滿；終止；死亡；呼氣
example: This insurance contract will expire at the end of the month.

definition: able to be explained or accounted for
chinese: 可解釋的；可說明的；可理解的
example: explicable behavior

definition: to explain in detail; to analyze and develop (an idea or text)
chinese: 詳細解釋；闡明；剖析
example: The scientists will carefully explicate each step of the experiment for transparency.

definition: stated clearly and in detail; leaving nothing implied; outspoken; (of content) graphically or sexually frank
chinese: 明確的；清楚表達的；直言的；露骨的
example: It's very jarring to hear uncensored songs with explicit lyrics playing in stores.

definition: to make full use of; to take unfair advantage of; to develop (resources); a bold or daring feat
chinese: v. 利用；剝削；開發（資源）；n. 功績；英勇事蹟
example: Narcissists exploit others' weaknesses and vulnerabilities, using them as leverage to control and manipulate.

definition: to investigate or study; to examine; to travel through (an area) to learn about it
chinese: 探究；探討；探索；探險
example: His innate understanding of pleasure allows him to explore and fulfill fantasies with finesse.

definition: an advocate or supporter; one who explains or interprets; a representative example; (math) a power
chinese: 倡導者；擁護者；闡述者；典型代表；（數學）指數

definition: to reason earnestly with someone in protest or dissuasion; to remonstrate
chinese: 勸諫；規勸；抗議；爭辯
example: Whatever they directed, it was in vain to expostulate; fetters, and bread and water, were the sure consequences of resistance.

definition: to explain in detail; to set forth; to interpret
chinese: 詳細闡述；解釋；說明
example: Would you care to expound?

definition: to remove objectionable parts from (a text); to censor; to purify
chinese: 刪改；刪去不雅內容；淨化（書籍）
example: In this context, “expurgate” means edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate.

definition: extremely beautiful and delicate; refined; keen (of sensibility); intense (of pain or pleasure)
chinese: 精緻的；精美的；細膩的；敏銳的；（痛苦）劇烈的

definition: still in existence; surviving
chinese: 現存的；尚存的

definition: to improvise; to speak or perform without preparation; to make do
chinese: 即興表演；即席演說；臨時湊合
example: When the projector failed, the lecturer had to extemporize.

definition: to stretch out or lengthen; to expand in scope; to prolong; to offer or grant (help, credit)
chinese: 延伸；擴大；延長；給予（援助）；提供
example: Select the graft point after imagining how the branches will extend and fruit grow.

definition: covering a large area; large in amount or scope; wide-ranging
chinese: 廣泛的；大量的；廣大的；全面的

definition: to lessen the seriousness of (an offense) by offering excuses; to partially excuse
chinese: 使情有可原；減輕（罪責）；為…開脫

definition: partially excusing or justifying; lessening the seriousness of an offense
chinese: 情有可原的；可減輕罪責的

definition: to destroy completely; to kill off
chinese: 消滅；根除；滅絕
example: Genocide is the systematic effort to exterminate an entire people.

definition: no longer existing; (of a species) having died out; obsolete; (of a volcano) no longer active
chinese: 滅絕的；絕種的；已消亡的；（火山）不再活動的
example: As likely as not, whales will be extinct by the end of this century.

definition: to put out (a fire or light); to bring to an end; to destroy; to cancel (a debt or right)
chinese: 熄滅；撲滅；使破滅；消除
example: Artificial intelligence threatens to extinguish the jobs of both low-educated and highly-educated people.

definition: to destroy completely; to root out; to pull up by the roots
chinese: 根除；滅絕；連根拔起
example: This thing is necessary to extirpate the evil of the world.

definition: to praise enthusiastically
chinese: 讚揚；頌揚；吹捧
example: I plan to extol your virtues to all who will listen.

definition: to obtain (money, a confession) by force, threats, or intimidation
chinese: 勒索；敲詐；強取

definition: to pull out; to obtain (a substance, information) from something; to excerpt; to obtain by force; a concentrated preparation; an excerpt
chinese: v. 拔出；提取；摘錄；榨取；n. 萃取物；精華；摘錄

definition: irrelevant; not pertinent; coming from outside; unnecessary
chinese: 無關的；不相干的；外來的；不必要的
example: Love is what matters; everything else is extraneous.

definition: to infer or estimate from known facts; to extend (data or a trend) beyond the known range
chinese: 推斷；推論；（統計）外推
example: Most of the words are faded, but it's still possible to extrapolate the meaning from these sentences.

definition: excessive spending; lavishness; the quality of exceeding reasonable limits; exaggeration
chinese: 奢侈；揮霍；過度；誇張
example: we were surprised by the extravagance of his description

definition: exceeding reasonable limits; exaggerated; spending too much; lavish
chinese: 過度的；誇張的；揮霍的；奢侈的
example: With her extravagant tastes, she was incapable of making ends meet.

definition: to free from a difficulty or entanglement; to release
chinese: 使脫身；使擺脫；解救
example: Elias wanted to successfully extricate himself out of the system.

definition: full of energy, enthusiasm, and cheerfulness; (of growth) luxuriant; abundant
chinese: 熱情洋溢的；充滿活力的；興高采烈的；（植物）茂盛的；豐富的
example: He's always been so exuberant, he doesn't really seem like a lone wolf.

definition: to display (a quality or feeling) strongly and openly; to give off; to discharge slowly (liquid or smell)
chinese: 流露；散發；滲出；分泌
example: Some people have a calm temperament or exude courtesy.

definition: to rejoice greatly; to be jubilant, especially over a success
chinese: 歡欣鼓舞；狂喜；得意洋洋
example: How long shall the wicked exult?

definition: a short moral story, often with animals; a myth or legend; a fabrication or falsehood
chinese: 寓言；神話；傳說；虛構的故事；謊言
example: He combines fact and fable to make a more interesting story.

definition: to invent (a story) in order to deceive; to forge; to construct or manufacture
chinese: 捏造；虛構；製造；組裝
example: That she could fabricate writings is certain, because she could write.

definition: extremely good; astonishing; existing in fable or legend; mythical
chinese: 極好的；驚人的；傳說中的；虛構的
example: Rima used to be a fabulous wife but she destroyed everything when she started drinking.

definition: the front of a building; a deceptive outward appearance
chinese: （建築物）正面；外表；假象；門面
example: Yanni was more interested in maintaining a facade than being the person behind that facade.

definition: treating serious issues with inappropriate humor; joking; flippant
chinese: 愛開玩笑的；不正經的；滑稽的；輕浮的
example: Are you accusing me of being facetious?

definition: inappropriate or flippant humor; playful jocularity
chinese: 不合時宜的玩笑；滑稽；輕浮
example: In this context, “facetiousness” refers to playful humor.

definition: superficial; overly simplistic; achieved without effort; fluent or effortless
chinese: 膚淺的；過於簡單化的；輕而易舉的；流暢的
example: The hunger for facile wisdom is the root of all false philosophy.

definition: to make easier; to help bring about
chinese: 促進；使便利；使容易
example: The determining factor in question is whether this social welfare plan can facilitate the influx of immigrants.

definition: ease or aptitude in doing something; skill; absence of difficulty; a building or equipment for a particular purpose
chinese: 熟練；才能；容易；設施；設備

definition: a small dissenting group within a larger one; conflict or dissension within a group
chinese: 派系；小團體；派系鬥爭；內訌
example: The chief said that this faction cannot be considered dismantled.

definition: relating to or causing dissension; inclined to form factions; contentious
chinese: 派系的；搞分裂的；製造紛爭的；黨派之爭的

definition: artificially created; not genuine; contrived; sham
chinese: 人為的；虛假的；不自然的；捏造的

definition: a servant or employee who does all kinds of work
chinese: 雜務總管；萬能助手；雜役
example: As the director's factotum, she handled schedules, correspondence, and travel.

definition: concerned with or based on facts; actual
chinese: 事實的；真實的；根據事實的

definition: a short-lived craze or fashion
chinese: 一時的流行；風尚；熱潮

definition: intensely fashionable for a short time; inclined to follow fads
chinese: 一時流行的；趕時髦的；短暫風行的
example: The passage describes its subject as faddish, meaning intensely fashionable for a short time.

definition: a mechanism or measure that prevents disaster in case of failure; designed to remain safe even if something fails; foolproof
chinese: n. 安全裝置；保險措施；adj. 萬無一失的；故障安全的

definition: lacking courage or conviction; timid
chinese: 膽小的；懦弱的；缺乏勇氣的
example: The elephant was alone and fainthearted.

definition: based on a mistaken belief or unsound reasoning; misleading
chinese: 謬誤的；不合邏輯的；騙人的
example: Her line of reasoning is attractive, but ultimately fallacious.

definition: a mistaken belief; an argument based on unsound reasoning
chinese: 謬誤；謬論；謬見；（邏輯）錯誤推理

chinese: 密封的；與世隔絕的；深奧難解的

definition: not conforming to accepted or orthodox standards or beliefs
chinese: 非正統的；異端的

definition: causing horror; shocking

chinese: adj. 假設的；假定的；推測的；n. 假設情況

definition: irritable and surly; in a bad mood
