definition: impossible to avoid or escape; inevitable
chinese: 無法逃避的；必然的
example: The two of us have parted, and we must forget each other; ineluctable fate forbids our ever meeting again.

definition: lacking skill or competence; clumsy; inappropriate; absurd
chinese: 無能的；笨拙的；不得當的；荒謬的
example: This cloth has the special ability to be invisible to the stupid and the inept.

definition: sluggish; lacking vigor; unable to move; chemically inactive
chinese: 遲鈍的；無活力的；不活動的；（化學）惰性的
example: Nitrous oxide is inert at room temperature.

definition: impossible to avoid or escape
chinese: 無法逃避的；不可避免的
example: inescapable conclusion

definition: certain to happen; unavoidable
chinese: 不可避免的；必然的
example: An accident is an inevitable occurrence due to the action of immutable natural laws.

definition: unforgivable; without excuse or justification
chinese: 不可原諒的；無法辯解的
example: When anyone tries to explain the inexplicable, he is getting ready to excuse the inexcusable.

definition: impossible to stop or prevent; relentless; not moved by persuasion or pleading
chinese: 無法阻擋的；不可動搖的；無情的；不為所動的
example: Holmes sat in a great, old-fashioned chair, his inexorable eyes gleaming out of his haggard face.

definition: not advisable or wise in the circumstances; unsuitable; impolitic
chinese: 不明智的；不適當的；失策的
example: an inexpedient tactic

definition: impossible to explain or account for; puzzling
chinese: 無法解釋的；費解的
example: inexplicable errors

definition: incapable of making mistakes; never failing; certain to work
chinese: 絕無錯誤的；絕對可靠的；必定有效的
example: an infallible antidote

definition: well known for something bad; notorious; shameful
chinese: 惡名昭彰的；聲名狼藉的；可恥的
example: I glare resentfully at the crimson letter, is this the infamous red-paper draft notice?

definition: to inspire with foolish or unreasoning love or passion
chinese: 使迷戀；使衝昏頭
example: In this context, “infatuate” means arouse unreasoning love or passion in and cause to behave in an irrational way.

definition: not appropriate or well-chosen; unfortunate
chinese: 不恰當的；不合時宜的；不幸的
example: The passage describes its subject as infelicitous, meaning not appropriate in application; defective.

definition: an inappropriate or unpleasing expression or style; inappropriateness; misfortune
chinese: 不恰當之處；措辭不當；不幸
example: In this context, “infelicity” refers to inappropriate and unpleasing manner or style (especially manner or style of expression).

definition: to deduce or conclude from evidence and reasoning
chinese: 推斷；推論；得出結論
example: I can infer that something went wrong here, even if I don't know what.

definition: to enter or join secretly, esp. to gain information; to permeate; (of liquid) to pass gradually into
chinese: 滲透；潛入；（液體）滲入
example: The roots also help aerate the soil to allow more water to infiltrate the ground.

definition: without limits; endless; very great in amount or degree
chinese: 無限的；無窮的；極大的
example: Languages can form an infinite number of sentences with a finite set of elements.

definition: extremely or immeasurably small
chinese: 極微小的；無限小的
example: We were only given infinitesimal doses.

definition: physically weak, esp. from age or illness; lacking firmness of will
chinese: 體弱的；衰弱的；（意志）不堅定的
example: BMI categories (underweight, overweight or obese) from general reading table are inappropriate for athletes, children, the elderly, and the infirm.

definition: to provoke or intensify strong feeling; to make worse; to anger; to cause inflammation in
chinese: 激起；使加劇；激怒；使發炎
example: In this context, “inflame” means cause inflammation in.

definition: easily set on fire; easily excited or angered; provocative
chinese: 易燃的；易激動的；具煽動性的
example: It only takes one person to leave an inflammable comment on an Internet thread for that thread to blow up into pages upon pages of reader indignation.

definition: arousing anger or strong feeling; provocative; relating to or causing inflammation
chinese: 煽動性的；激起情緒的；發炎的
example: an inflammatory process

definition: to exaggerate; to increase (prices) artificially; to fill with air or gas; to swell; to make conceited
chinese: 誇大；抬高（物價）；使充氣；使膨脹；使自負
example: Ziri struggled to inflate the balloon.

definition: to cause something unpleasant to be suffered by someone; to impose
chinese: 施加（痛苦）；使遭受；強加
example: Sociopaths never feel remorse and they rationalize the pain they inflict on others.

definition: an arrival or entry of large numbers of people or things
chinese: 湧入；大量流入
example: The influx of foreign workers has caused a serious housing problem in this area.

definition: to give information to; to tell; to influence or shape; to pervade; to give incriminating information (on)
chinese: 通知；告知；影響；貫穿；告發
example: The medic knew that it was a carcinogenic substance but didn't inform the authorities.

definition: a violation of a rule or law; a minor offense
chinese: 違反；違規；輕罪
example: In this context, “infraction” refers to a crime less serious than a felony.

definition: to make extremely angry
chinese: 激怒；使大怒
example: In a packed bus, it would infuriate me to miss my stop on account of other passengers.

definition: to fill or pervade; to instill (a quality); to soak (tea or herbs) to extract flavor
chinese: 注入；灌輸；使充滿；浸泡（茶葉）
example: The director used humor to infuse the somber drama with moments of warmth.

definition: clever, original, and inventive; cleverly designed
chinese: 巧妙的；精巧的；有創意的；機靈的
example: This species of moth has evolved an ingenious camouflage for blending into its surroundings.

definition: innocent and unsuspecting; naive; candid; lacking cunning
chinese: 天真的；純樸的；坦率的；無心機的
example: Two-years in college in Manhattan had changed Jenna from an ingenuous girl from the suburbs to a jaded urbanite, unlikely to fall for any ruse, regardless of how elaborate.

definition: to take (food or drink) into the body; to absorb (information)
chinese: 攝取；嚥下；吸收（資訊）
example: For external use only, do not ingest.

definition: to fix (a habit or belief) firmly; to work in thoroughly; to dye in the fiber
chinese: 使根深蒂固；使深植；（紡織）原紗染色
example: In this context, “ingrain” means thoroughly work in.

definition: firmly fixed or established; deeply embedded
chinese: 根深蒂固的；深植的；（汙垢）積久的
example: Miroslav's cursing has become so ingrained in his speech that it often happens subconsciously, without him even realizing it.

definition: an ungrateful person; ungrateful
chinese: n. 忘恩負義者；adj. 忘恩負義的
example: He seemed an ingrate when he dismissed years of generous assistance.

definition: to bring (oneself) into favor with someone by deliberate efforts; to curry favor
chinese: 討好；逢迎；巴結
example: He was a sycophant, always trying to ingratiate himself with the wealthy.

definition: intended to gain favor; flattering; pleasing or winning
chinese: 討好的；逢迎的；討人喜歡的
example: Ingratiating behaviour can be really annoying.

definition: the act of deliberately gaining someone's favor, esp. by flattery
chinese: 逢迎；討好；巴結
example: In this context, “ingratiation” refers to the act of gaining acceptance or affection for yourself by persuasive and subtle blandishments.

definition: existing as a permanent, essential part of something; intrinsic; innate
chinese: 固有的；內在的；本質的；與生俱來的
example: The supernatural is that which transcends the experience and knowledge inherent in human nature.

definition: by its very nature; intrinsically
chinese: 本質上；固有地；天生地
example: the subject matter is sexual activity of any overt kind, which is depicted as inherently desirable and exciting

definition: to receive (property or a title) from someone after their death; to derive (a trait) genetically; to take over (a situation) from a predecessor
chinese: 繼承；遺傳；接手（問題）
example: His relatives took it for granted that they would inherit the bulk of his wealth.

definition: unable to act or express oneself freely; self-conscious; held back or restrained
chinese: 拘謹的；壓抑的；受抑制的
example: in certain conditions previously inhibited conditioned reactions can reappear

definition: cruel; lacking pity or compassion
chinese: 不人道的；殘忍的；無同情心的
example: humans are innately inhumane; this explains much of the misery and suffering in the world

definition: tending to harm or obstruct; unfavorable; hostile
chinese: 有害的；不利的；敵意的
example: He doesn't understand that his actions are inimical to his own interests.

definition: impossible to imitate; unique; matchless
chinese: 無法模仿的；獨特的；無與倫比的
example: His photographs are unsparingly critical, and his inimitable eye unmasks the banal as well as the grotesque.

definition: grossly unfair; wicked; sinful
chinese: 極不公正的；邪惡的
example: iniquitous deeds

definition: gross injustice; immoral behavior; a wicked act
chinese: 極不公正；邪惡；罪行
example: We have taken part in the iniquity that will happen.

definition: to cause (a process) to begin; to introduce to a subject; to admit into a group with rites; a newly admitted member
chinese: v. 發起；開始；使入門；使入會；n. 新加入者；入門者
example: To initiate the quest, first go to the tavern and talk to the quest-giver.

definition: causing or likely to cause harm; damaging; (of words) slanderous
chinese: 有害的；傷害的；誹謗的
example: The report contends the current system is injurious to mental well-being and violates the human rights of patients.

definition: a slight knowledge or vague notion; a hint
chinese: 模糊的概念；略知；暗示
example: I had an inkling this project might turn out difficult.

definition: inborn; natural rather than learned; inherent
chinese: 天生的；先天的；固有的
example: His innate understanding of pleasure allows him to explore and fulfill fantasies with finesse.

definition: by birth or nature; inherently
chinese: 天生地；先天地
example: the child is said to be innately disposed to learn language

definition: the state of being not guilty; purity; naivety; lack of knowledge
chinese: 無罪；清白；天真；無知
example: These dirty clothes could be a new piece of evidence to prove his innocence.

definition: not harmful; not likely to offend or provoke; bland and inoffensive
chinese: 無害的；無冒犯性的；平淡無奇的
example: Everyone found Nancy’s banter innocuous—except for Mike, who felt like she was intentionally picking on him.

definition: introducing or using new ideas or methods; original and creative
chinese: 創新的；有創意的；革新的
example: Campana creates innovative prosthetics for pets without limbs, and even for wild animals.

definition: an indirect, usually disparaging, remark or hint; insinuation
chinese: 影射；暗諷；含沙射影
example: And then she let slip a not-so-subtle innuendo about my drinking habits.

definition: occurring at an inconvenient or inappropriate time
chinese: 不合時宜的；時機不當的；不巧的
example: arrived at a most inopportune hour

definition: unusually or disproportionately large; excessive; unrestrained
chinese: 過度的；過分的；無節制的
example: His so-called apology involved an inordinate amount of explanation and complaining.

definition: eager to learn; curious; unduly curious about others' affairs
chinese: 好奇的；好問的；愛打聽的
example: From within her wrinkle furrowed face two alert and inquisitive eyes looked at me.

definition: impossible to satisfy; greedy
chinese: 無法滿足的；貪得無厭的
example: Yanni had an insatiable lust for life.

definition: words inscribed, engraved, or carved on something; a dedication written in a book
chinese: 題字；碑文；銘文；（書的）題詞
example: According to the inscription, it used to belong to a famous navigator.

definition: impossible to understand or interpret; enigmatic; mysterious
chinese: 難以理解的；不可測的；高深莫測的
example: She looked at him with an inscrutable expression.

definition: unaware (of); lacking sensation; unconscious; indifferent; too slight to be perceived
chinese: 未察覺的；無知覺的；不省人事的；麻木的；難以察覺的
example: Lucy lay senseless on the ground, insensible of the wonderful deliverance which she had experienced.

definition: lacking feeling, perception, or consciousness; inanimate
chinese: 無感覺的；無知覺的；無生命的
example: The passage describes its subject as insentient, meaning devoid of feeling and consciousness and animation.

definition: a person within an organization, esp. one with access to private information; one who knows the inside facts
chinese: 內部人士；知情者；局內人
example: The disputants know instinctively that an outsider can see the difficulty better than an insider.

definition: proceeding gradually and subtly but with harmful effect; treacherous; crafty
chinese: 暗中為害的；潛伏的；陰險的；狡詐的
example: insidious pleasures

definition: not expressing genuine feelings; hypocritical
chinese: 不真誠的；虛偽的；無誠意的
example: a charming but thoroughly insincere woman

definition: lacking interest or vigor; dull; bland; lacking flavor
chinese: 乏味的；無趣的；平淡的；淡而無味的
example: Some people have to stop saying words that add pain, what is called insipid chatter.

definition: rude and disrespectful; arrogant
chinese: 無禮的；傲慢的；粗魯的
example: Her insolent remarks to her boss cost her her job.

definition: unable to pay debts; bankrupt; a person who is insolvent
chinese: adj. 無力償債的；破產的；n. 破產者
example: If you are insolvent you can’t pay your bills. Oftentimes people use the term bankrupt. If you are solvent, on the other hand, you have paid off all your debts.

definition: habitual inability to sleep; chronic sleeplessness
chinese: 失眠；失眠症
example: Grumpy suffered from insomnia, that's why he was always in a bad mood.

definition: casual lack of concern; nonchalance; carefree cheerfulness
chinese: 漫不經心；不在乎；無憂無慮
example: The cicada has represented insouciance since antiquity.

definition: showing a casual lack of concern; nonchalant; carefree
chinese: 漫不經心的；不在乎的；無憂無慮的
example: She gave an insouciant look.

definition: outstandingly brilliant or creative, as if divinely guided; stimulated by something; prompted by an outside source
chinese: 絕妙的；有靈感的；受啟發的；（受人）授意的
example: Sometimes the most inspired ideas seem to just come from out of the blue.

definition: to install or establish in a rank or office
chinese: 任命；使就職；安置
example: In this context, “instate” means t. To set, place, or establish, as in a rank, office, or.

definition: to provoke or incite (someone) to act; to bring about or initiate (an action)
chinese: 煽動；教唆；發起
example: They used every means in their power to instigate the people against him.

definition: to gradually establish (an idea or attitude) in someone's mind; to impart; to put in drop by drop
chinese: 灌輸；逐漸培養；滴注
example: Parents work hard to develop, or instill, positive beliefs and values in their children.

definition: by instinct; without conscious thought
chinese: 本能地；直覺地
example: he instinctively grabbed the knife

definition: to set up or establish; to introduce (a rule or procedure); to begin (legal proceedings); an organization for research, education, or a profession
chinese: v. 創立；制定；實施；開始（訴訟）；n. 研究所；機構；學會
example: Germany’s national public health institute is urging the public to stay disciplined.

definition: useful and informative; enlightening
chinese: 有教育意義的；有啟發性的；增長知識的
example: This book is not only more instructive but more interesting than that book.

definition: defiant of authority; disobedient to orders
chinese: 不服從的；違抗命令的
example: Why are you so insubordinate to your boss?

definition: too extreme to bear; intolerable; unbearably arrogant or conceited
chinese: 難以忍受的；傲慢得令人受不了的
example: Chester always tried to find some area in which he excelled above others; unsurprisingly, his co- workers found him insufferable and chose to exclude him from daily luncheons out.

definition: narrow-minded; interested only in one's own group; isolated; of or relating to an island
chinese: 狹隘的；偏狹的；孤立的；島嶼的
example: The fact that no one ever moves in makes the community more and more insular.

definition: to protect from unpleasant influences; to isolate; to cover with material to prevent the passage of heat, sound, or electricity
chinese: 使隔離；保護（使不受影響）；使絕緣；隔熱
example: You'll end up getting an electric shock if you don't insulate that wire.

definition: a rebel against established authority; rising in revolt; rebellious
chinese: n. 叛亂分子；反抗者；adj. 叛亂的；造反的
example: Ukraine is losing more territory to insurgent forces.

definition: impossible to touch; difficult to define or grasp; an intangible thing or asset
chinese: adj. 無形的；難以捉摸的；觸摸不到的；n. 無形資產
example: There could be an invisible, inaudible, intangible dragon next to you right now.

definition: necessary to make a whole complete; essential; complete; (mathematics) a function representing the area under a curve
chinese: adj. 不可或缺的；構成整體所必需的；完整的；n. （數學）積分
example: The integral is a mathematical operator used to calculate the area under a curve.

definition: adherence to moral principles; honesty; the state of being whole and undivided; soundness
chinese: 正直；誠實；完整；完好
example: Fearing neither obstacles, nor ridicule, she acts with integrity according to the ideas she considers correct.

definition: able to be understood; comprehensible; clear
chinese: 可理解的；易懂的；清楚的
example: If you look at the individual letters of a word long enough, it stops becoming intelligible.

definition: lack of moderation or self-control; excessive indulgence, esp. in alcohol
chinese: 放縱；無節制；酗酒
example: Idleness, vice, and intemperance had done their miserable work, and the dead mother lay cold and still amid her wretched children.

definition: lacking self-control; excessive; immoderate; (of climate) severe; given to excessive drinking
chinese: 無節制的；過度的；放縱的；（氣候）嚴酷的；嗜酒的
example: The passage describes its subject as intemperate, meaning (of weather or climate) not mild; subject to extremes.

definition: to become or make more intense; to strengthen
chinese: 加強；加劇；強化
example: As anger and frustration among the flood victims intensify, reports that international aid has slackened raises concerns.

definition: to place (a dead body) in a grave or tomb; to bury
chinese: 埋葬；安葬
example: They have signed an inter-agency code of conduct on this matter and have completed a mandatory training.

definition: a person who intervenes on behalf of another; a mediator; one who prays for others
chinese: 調停者；說情者；代禱者
example: In this context, “intercessor” refers to a negotiator who acts as a link between parties.

definition: able to be exchanged or used in place of each other
chinese: 可互換的；可交替使用的
example: the arguments of the symmetric relation, ‘is a sister of,’ are interchangeable

definition: to prohibit or forbid; to intercept or cut off (supply lines); an authoritative prohibition
chinese: v. 禁止；阻斷；攔截；n. 禁令
example: The army sought to interdict enemy supply lines before the attack.

definition: provisional; temporary; the intervening time between two events
chinese: adj. 臨時的；暫時的；過渡的；n. 過渡期間；其間
example: A peace accord in 2006 led to the promulgation of an interim constitution in 2007.

definition: to engage or lock together; to fit tightly into each other; a device that prevents an action until conditions are met
chinese: v. 連結；互鎖；緊密相扣；n. 聯鎖裝置
example: This car is fully equipped with an ignition interlock device.

definition: a person who acts as a link or mediator between others; a go-between; acting between; intermediate
chinese: n. 中間人；調解人；媒介；adj. 中間的；調解的
example: In this paper I address the question, what is difficult about the intermediary's position in a negotiation?

definition: endless, or seeming endless because tedious
chinese: 無止盡的；冗長乏味的
example: I listened to the boring lecture for what seemed an interminable fifty minutes.

definition: occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous
chinese: 斷斷續續的；間歇的
example: Intermittent flashes of lightning illuminated the dark gloom of the forest.

definition: the way two or more things affect each other; reciprocal action and reaction
chinese: 相互作用；相互影響
example: My locality is a nexus for occidental and oriental interplay, which is abundant in emotional undulations.

definition: a period between two reigns or governments; any pause or interval
chinese: 過渡期；空位期；間歇
example: In this context, “interregnum” refers to the time between two reigns, governments, etc.

definition: to question formally and closely; to examine critically
chinese: 審問；訊問；質詢；仔細探究
example: He knows how to interrogate people.

definition: a place where roads meet; a point where lines cross; (mathematics) the set of shared elements; the meeting of two things
chinese: 十字路口；交叉點；（數學）交集；交會
example: Since the traffic lights weren't working, there were policemen directing traffic at every intersection.

definition: closely acquainted; private and personal; (of knowledge) detailed; to hint or imply; a close friend
chinese: adj. 親密的；私密的；精通的；v. 暗示；透露；n. 密友
example: The individual soul should seek for an intimate union with the soul of the universe.

definition: to frighten, esp. in order to make someone do something; to overawe
chinese: 威嚇；恐嚇；使膽怯
example: Rodrigo's online bullies sought to isolate and intimidate him on the website.

definition: a substance, such as alcohol or a drug, that produces intoxication
chinese: 致醉物；酒類；麻醉品
example: In this context, “intoxicant” refers to a drug that can produce a state of intoxication.

definition: to excite or exhilarate; to make drunk; to poison
chinese: 使陶醉；使興奮；使喝醉；使中毒
example: Can water intoxicate a person?

definition: hard to solve or manage; stubborn; difficult to control or mold
chinese: 棘手的；難以處理的；倔強的；難駕馭的
example: an intractable disposition

definition: unwilling to change one's views or to compromise; uncompromising
chinese: 不妥協的；固執的；不讓步的
example: He is a stubborn and intransigent demagogue.

definition: fearless; adventurous; resolutely bold
chinese: 無畏的；勇敢的；大膽的
example: Many tried to carry out the deed of the intrepid mountaineer.

definition: very complicated or detailed; elaborate; hard to understand
chinese: 錯綜複雜的；精細的；難懂的
example: intricate lacework

definition: a secret scheme; plotting; to arouse the curiosity or interest of; to plot secretly
chinese: n. 陰謀；密謀；v. 激起好奇心；使感興趣；策劃陰謀
example: This is a story full of intrigue, love, betrayal and secrets.

definition: belonging naturally; essential; inherent
chinese: 固有的；內在的；本質的
example: This celebration is an intrinsic part of the culture of our country.

definition: the act of bringing something into use for the first time; the presenting of one person to another; an opening section of a book; a basic guide
chinese: 引進；採用；介紹；導論；入門
example: The introduction of the new tax is expected to affect the entire economy.

definition: inclined to examine one's own thoughts and feelings
chinese: 內省的；自省的
example: People talk about interesting and introspective subjects when hiking.

definition: to enter without invitation or welcome; to encroach; to disturb; to force in
chinese: 闖入；侵擾；打擾；強加
example: By and large, reporters don't hesitate to intrude on one's privacy.

definition: based on instinctive feeling rather than reasoning; easy to understand or use
chinese: 直覺的；憑直覺的；易懂易用的
example: Yet she had that intuitive feeling of disaster that portends great and overwhelming events.

definition: by intuition; without conscious reasoning
chinese: 直覺地；憑直覺
example: inventors seem to have chosen intuitively a combination of explosive and aggressive sounds as warning signals to be used on automobiles

definition: to overwhelm with things to deal with; to flood; to cover with water
chinese: 使應接不暇；（大量事物）湧至；淹沒；氾濫
example: In this context, “inundate” means fill or cover completely, usually with water.

definition: to accustom (someone) to something unpleasant; to harden; to habituate
chinese: 使習慣（不好的事物）；使麻木；使堅強
example: In this context, “inure” means cause to accept or become hardened to; habituate.

definition: to enter (a country) by military force to conquer it; to encroach on; to enter in large numbers; to spread into harmfully
chinese: 侵略；入侵；侵犯；湧入；侵襲
example: It should be forbidden to invade countries whose names one can't pronounce correctly.

definition: insulting, abusive, or highly critical language; denunciatory
chinese: n. 謾罵；痛斥；惡言；adj. 謾罵的
example: Anyone who has no more ideas to convey may be tempted to resort to invective.

definition: to speak or write about something with great hostility; to protest vehemently (against)
chinese: 痛斥；猛烈抨擊；強烈抗議
example: In this context, “inveigh” means complain bitterly.

definition: to persuade by cunning or flattery; to entice; to win over by coaxing
chinese: 誘騙；哄騙；以甜言蜜語誘使
example: Larsen tried to inveigle me into discussion.

definition: creative and original in thought; able to invent; showing creativity
chinese: 有創造力的；善於發明的；新穎的
example: Butterflies are just flowers that took flight on a feast day when nature was particularly inventive and fruitful.

definition: a complete list of items such as goods or property; the stock of goods; a stocktaking; to make a list of; to take stock of
chinese: n. 存貨；庫存；詳細清單；盤點；v. 盤點；編製清單
example: If your character is overburdened, consider dropping or selling some items from your inventory.

definition: to turn upside down or inside out; to reverse the position, order, or relation of
chinese: 顛倒；倒置；反轉
example: It might help if you invert the colours.

definition: to examine systematically to discover facts; to study; to inquire into
chinese: 調查；研究；審查
example: Let's investigate the syntax of Chinese

definition: having a habit or feeling that is long-established and unlikely to change; deep-rooted; habitual
chinese: 根深蒂固的；積習難改的；成癮的
example: They overcame many inveterate superstitions.

definition: likely to cause resentment or envy; unpleasant; (of a comparison) unfairly discriminating
chinese: 招人嫉恨的；惹人反感的；不公平的
example: She does have a favourite among her children, but she thinks it would be invidious to say which.

definition: to give strength or energy to; to animate; to stimulate
chinese: 使充滿活力；鼓舞；使強健
example: A vigorous public debate can invigorate a stagnant institution.

definition: giving strength and energy; refreshing; stimulating
chinese: 令人振奮的；使人精神煥發的；清新的
example: the invigorating mountain air

definition: too powerful to be defeated; unconquerable; unshakable
chinese: 無敵的；不可戰勝的；不可動搖的
example: A lot of young people think they're invincible, but the truth is young people are knuckleheads.

definition: to cite (a law or authority) in support; to appeal to; to call on (a deity) in prayer; to evoke; (computing) to call (a program)
chinese: 援引（法律或權威）；訴諸；祈求；喚起；調用（程式）
example: In pots I try in vain to invoke the scents of childhood.

definition: complicated; intricate; taking part; connected or concerned; romantically associated
chinese: 複雜的；錯綜的；參與的；牽涉在內的；有（感情）瓜葛的
example: The physics lecture became so involved that the undergraduate’s eyes glazed over.

definition: easily angered; hot-tempered
chinese: 易怒的；暴躁的
example: Ziri has always been an irascible and difficult husband.

definition: extremely angry; furious
chinese: 極憤怒的；暴怒的
example: How would you deal with an angry or irate customer?

definition: anger; wrath
chinese: 憤怒；怒火
example: Máire was injured in an accident.

definition: aiming to promote peace or reconciliation; conciliatory
chinese: 促進和平的；調和的；和解的
example: irenic without being namby-pamby

definition: showing shimmering colors that change with the angle of view; lustrous and colorful
chinese: 彩虹色的；（隨角度）閃爍變色的；絢麗的
example: The skull in the narrow niche cast iridescent reflections.

definition: to irritate or annoy
chinese: 使厭煩；使惱怒
example: In this context, “irk” means irritate or vex.

definition: impossible to break or weaken; rigid and binding; covered with iron armor; a 19th-century warship plated with iron
chinese: adj. 堅不可摧的；不可違背的；鐵甲的；n. 鐵甲艦
example: The passage describes its subject as ironclad, meaning a wooden warship of the 19th century that is plated with iron or steel armor.

definition: using irony; sarcastic; happening in the opposite way to what is expected; mocking
chinese: 諷刺的；反諷的；事與願違的；挖苦的
example: I'm not sure if this is ironic or not.

definition: impossible to eradicate or destroy; deep-rooted
chinese: 無法根除的；根深蒂固的
example: The passage describes its subject as irradicable, meaning impossible destroy.

definition: impossible to reconcile; incompatible; mutually opposed
chinese: 無法調和的；不能和解的；矛盾的
example: irreconcilable differences

definition: a person advocating the recovery of territory once belonging to their nation; relating to irredentism
chinese: n. 收復失土主義者；民族統一主義者；adj. 收復失土主義的
example: In this context, “irredentist” refers to an advocate of irredentism.

definition: not able to be changed, reversed, or retracted; final
chinese: 不可撤銷的；不可改變的；無法挽回的
example: firm and irrevocable is my doom

definition: to supply (land or crops) with water; to flush (a wound or body part) with liquid
chinese: 灌溉；（醫）沖洗
example: They said the farmers complained of not receiving enough water to irrigate their crops.

definition: to make annoyed or angry; to cause discomfort or inflammation in (a body part)
chinese: 激怒；使惱火；刺激（皮膚等）；使發炎
example: The chemicals are designed to irritate the mucous membranes of the eyes, nose and throat.

definition: a piece of land surrounded by water; an isolated area or group; a traffic island
chinese: 島；島嶼；孤立的地方；安全島
example: He was kind enough to take us over to the island in his boat.

definition: to set apart from others; to quarantine; to identify and separate out (a substance or factor); to insulate
chinese: 使孤立；隔離；分離出；使絕緣
example: In order to isolate him from bacteria, and such, he is not allowed visitors.

definition: an important topic or problem for debate; the act of supplying or distributing; one edition of a periodical; offspring; to publish or supply officially; to come or flow out
chinese: n. 議題；爭議；發行；（期刊）期號；後代；v. 發布；發行；發出；流出
example: The proceeds from the bond issue will be used to finance the budget deficit.

definition: traveling from place to place; wandering; a person who travels from place to place
chinese: adj. 巡迴的；流動的；四處奔波的；n. 流動工作者
example: Over time, itinerant groups often develop their own language and culture distinct from their settled counterparts.

definition: to talk rapidly and unintelligibly; to chatter; rapid, meaningless talk
chinese: v. 急促含糊地說；喋喋不休；n. 急促含糊的話
example: Don't give me that jibber jabber.

definition: bored or lacking enthusiasm after having too much of something; cynical; worn out
chinese: 厭倦的；麻木的；膩煩的；疲憊的
example: I look and walk around the streets outside, and I see people look jaded.

definition: a practical joke or prank; to joke or jest; to mock
chinese: n. 玩笑；惡作劇；v. 開玩笑；嘲弄
example: Her jape was not appreciated.

definition: special words or expressions used by a profession or group that are hard for others to understand; unintelligible talk
chinese: 行話；術語；難懂的話
example: Lawyers like to use professional jargon that's difficult for laymen to understand.

definition: harsh and discordant; clashing; shocking or unsettling
chinese: 刺耳的；不協調的；令人震驚的；令人不安的
example: It's very jarring to hear uncensored songs with explicit lyrics playing in stores.

definition: bitterness or prejudice; a medical condition causing yellowing of the skin; to affect with bitterness or prejudice
chinese: n. 偏見；成見；黃疸；v. 使抱偏見
example: I have been suffering from jaundice for some time.

definition: lively and self-confident; sprightly; stylish and smart in dress
chinese: 輕快的；活潑的；自信的；時髦的
example: The passage describes its subject as jaunty, meaning marked by up-to-dateness in dress and manners.

definition: to make rude, mocking remarks; to taunt; a mocking remark
chinese: v. 嘲笑；譏諷；起鬨；n. 嘲弄
example: The crowd continued to jeer.

definition: dull and uninteresting; naive and simplistic; immature; lacking substance
chinese: 枯燥乏味的；幼稚的；不成熟的；空洞的
example: Now that I’m done lamenting jejune’s debased status, I’m going to have a jejune fit.

definition: to put at risk of harm, loss, or failure; to endanger
chinese: 危及；危害；使陷入險境
example: Flavio can’t let anyone jeopardize the mission.

definition: danger of loss, harm, or failure; (law) the risk of conviction faced by a defendant
chinese: 危險；危難；（法律）被判罪的風險
example: He found himself in a state of jeopardy that he couldn't get out of.

definition: a joke or playful remark; a mood of fun; to speak in a joking way
chinese: n. 玩笑；戲謔；v. 開玩笑
example: We've talked about this before, although it was more in jest than anything.

definition: to abandon or discard (a plan or idea); to throw (cargo) overboard or from an aircraft
chinese: 拋棄；放棄（計畫或想法）；（從船或飛機上）投棄
example: To save the lives of the people onboard, the crew had to jettison the cargo.

definition: to be in agreement; to match; to make insulting remarks; (sailing) to shift the sail across; a taunt
chinese: v. 相符；一致；嘲弄；（帆船）換舷；n. 嘲諷
example: In this context, “jibe” means shift from one side of the ship to the other.

definition: a person who supports extreme, aggressive patriotism; a bellicose nationalist
chinese: 好戰的愛國主義者；極端民族主義者
example: In this context, “jingoist” refers to an extreme bellicose nationalist.

definition: a feeling of extreme nervousness; anxiety; (of markets) instability
chinese: 緊張不安；神經過敏；（市場）動盪
example: In this context, “jitters” refers to extreme nervousness.

definition: fond of or characterized by joking; humorous; playful
chinese: 詼諧的；愛開玩笑的；滑稽的
example: She sounded as if she were in a jocular mood.

definition: cheerful and lighthearted; merry; high-spirited
chinese: 歡樂的；快活的；興高采烈的
example: The passage describes its subject as jocund, meaning full of or showing high-spirited merriment.

definition: to stimulate (the memory); to nudge; to run at a slow, steady pace; a slow run; a slight push
chinese: v. 喚起（記憶）；輕推；慢跑；n. 慢跑；輕推
example: Lacing tightly a pair of worn sneakers, the athlete started off with a light jog.

definition: to shock or startle; to push or shake abruptly; to move jerkily; a sudden shock; an abrupt jarring movement
chinese: v. 使震驚；使顛簸；搖晃；n. 震驚；顛簸；震動
example: Yanni's car started to jolt slightly.

definition: to write down quickly and briefly; a very small amount
chinese: v. 草草記下；n. 一點點；少量
example: She carries a notebook so that she can jot down any ideas.

definition: cheerful and friendly; full of good humor and conviviality
chinese: 快活的；和藹愉快的；友善的
example: But these jovial sounds fell sadly on the ear of the ruined nobleman.

definition: feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph
chinese: 歡欣鼓舞的；喜氣洋洋的
example: I got a thesaurus as a present and I feel very happy, glad, cheerful, jovial, jubilant and merry.

definition: a feeling of great happiness and triumph; celebration
chinese: 歡騰；喜悅；慶祝
example: His moods shift rapidly between depressed gloom and frenzied jubilation.

definition: a public officer who decides cases in a court; a person who decides a contest; one able to give an authoritative opinion; to form an opinion about; to try (a case); to decide (a competition)
chinese: n. 法官；裁判；鑑定者；v. 判斷；評斷；審判；評判
example: The scholars quarrel, and the case lies still unsolved in the hands of the judge.

definition: having or showing good judgment; prudent; sensible
chinese: 明智的；審慎的；有見識的
example: We are going to run the country until such time as we can do a safe, proper and judicious transition.

definition: a huge, powerful, overwhelming force or institution; a very large heavy truck
chinese: 無法阻擋的強大力量；龐然大物；重型卡車
example: Napoleon was considered a juggernaut, until he decided to invade Russia in winter; within weeks his once seemingly indomitable army was decimated by cold and famine.

definition: a military group ruling a country after seizing power; a political faction or cabal
chinese: 軍政府；（政變後的）執政團；陰謀集團
example: As dangerous of a threat as North Korea is, some analysts believe that were a junta suddenly to gain power, it could be even more unpredictable and bellicose than the current leadership.

definition: a body of citizens sworn to give a verdict in a court of law; a panel judging a competition
chinese: 陪審團；評審團
example: Before they even began deliberations, many of the jury members had reached a verdict.

definition: just behavior or treatment; fairness; the administration of law; a judge, esp. of a supreme court
chinese: 正義；公正；司法；法官
example: Their goal and activating main idea was indeed brotherhood and justice among the peoples.

definition: able to be shown to be right or reasonable; defensible
chinese: 有正當理由的；合理的；可辯護的
example: Different jurisdictions often have distinct definitions of justifiable homicide.

definition: to show to be right or reasonable; to defend; to be a good reason for; to adjust (text) so lines are even
chinese: 證明合理；為其辯護；作為正當理由；（排版）使對齊
example: Leon is using nonsense in order to justify a point that isn't there.

definition: relating to young people; childish; immature; a young person; a young animal or plant
chinese: adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；未成熟的；n. 青少年；（動植物）幼體
example: juvenile diabetes

definition: to place side by side, esp. for contrast or comparison
chinese: 並置；並列（以作對比）
example: Good essays juxtapose two different arguments.

definition: in the manner of Franz Kafka's writings; nightmarishly complex, bizarre, or illogical, esp. of bureaucracy
chinese: 卡夫卡式的；荒誕離奇的；（官僚體制）令人困惑壓抑的；夢魘般的
example: The process of applying for a passport was so Kafkaesque that Charles ultimately decided not to take a vacation.

definition: quick and penetrating intelligence; eagerness; enthusiasm; sharpness
chinese: 敏銳；熱切；渴望；銳利
example: In this context, “keenness” refers to a quick and penetrating intelligence.

definition: the range of one's knowledge or understanding; the range of sight
chinese: 知識範圍；理解範圍；視野
example: In this context, “ken” refers to range of what one can know or understand.

definition: of crucial importance; essential; a device for opening a lock; a means of understanding; an answer list; (music) a system of notes; a button on a keyboard
chinese: adj. 關鍵的；主要的；n. 鑰匙；關鍵；答案；（音樂）調；鍵
example: One of the key components of empathy is what scientists call facial mimicry.

definition: to take away by force and hold captive, usually for ransom; an instance of kidnapping
chinese: v. 綁架；劫持；n. 綁架
example: You thought you were going to kidnap the kid, didn't you?

definition: good working order or balance (usually in "out of kilter")
chinese: 正常狀態；平衡；協調
example: The lamp on the desk had an out-of-kilter lampshade.

definition: to set on fire; to ignite; to arouse or inspire (an emotion or interest)
chinese: 點燃；激起；引起（興趣或情感）
example: She added twigs to kindle the flames and keep them burning.

definition: similar in kind; like-minded; related; one's family and relations; kinship
chinese: adj. 相似的；志趣相投的；同源的；n. 親屬；血緣關係
example: I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.

definition: an acquired or natural skill; a clever way of doing something; a tendency
chinese: 訣竅；本領；竅門；習性
example: She has a real knack for getting people to do what she wants.

definition: to make (a garment) by looping yarn with needles; to unite closely; (of bones) to heal; to knot (the brow); a knitted garment
chinese: v. 編織；使緊密結合；（骨頭）癒合；皺（眉）；n. 針織品
example: Matthew's grandmother used to knit woolen sweaters for him when he was a child.

definition: full of difficulties or complications; (of wood) having many knots; tangled
chinese: 棘手的；複雜的；（木材）多節的；多結的
example: The tree had a knotty trunk.

definition: to act in an excessively subservient way; to kneel and touch the forehead to the ground; the act of kowtowing
chinese: v. 卑躬屈膝；奉承；叩頭；n. 叩頭
example: In this context, “kowtow” refers to a former Chinese custom of touching the ground with the forehead as a sign of respect or submission.

definition: praise and honor for an achievement; prestige; fame
chinese: 讚揚；榮譽；名望
example: Kudos for your outstanding achievement!

definition: liable to change; unstable; (of emotions) easily altered; (chemistry) readily breaking down
chinese: 不穩定的；易變的；（情緒）起伏不定的
example: The passage describes its subject as labile, meaning (chemistry, physics, biology) readily undergoing change or breakdown.

definition: requiring much time and effort; arduous; showing obvious effort; industrious
chinese: 費力的；艱苦的；（文體）不流暢的；勤勞的
example: He said the provision would also involve a laborious and complicated legal process, including amending constitutional provisions and other electoral laws.

definition: extremely complicated or tortuous; like a labyrinth
chinese: 錯綜複雜的；迷宮般的
example: It seems as if dishonorable, labyrinthine, deliberately confusing economic policies have earned more support from the president than every physical and mental disability combined.

definition: to tear or deeply cut (flesh or skin); to wound the feelings of; to criticize harshly
chinese: 撕裂；割傷；使痛苦；嚴厲抨擊
example: If you don't wear protective clothing, the sharp leaves will lacerate your skin.

definition: tearful or given to weeping; inducing tears; mournful
chinese: 愛哭的；含淚的；催人淚下的；悲傷的
example: She was so lachrymose, she cried at commercials for long-distance phone companies.

definition: lacking enthusiasm and determination; carelessly lazy; listless
chinese: 無精打采的；懶散的；不熱心的
example: a lackadaisical attempt

definition: lacking energy or distinction; mediocre; dull and lacking brightness
chinese: 平淡無奇的；乏味的；黯淡無光的
example: The electorate is largely uninterested in the lackluster candidates.

definition: using very few words; concise to the point of seeming rude or mysterious; terse
chinese: 言簡意賅的；簡潔的；寡言的
example: While Martha always swooned over the hunky, laconic types in romantic comedies, her boyfriends inevitably were very talkative—and not very hunky.

definition: to fall behind; to move slowly; to weaken or slacken; a delay; a period of time between events
chinese: v. 落後；延遲；減弱；n. 延遲；落後；時間差
example: We should read the newspaper so as not to lag behind the times.

definition: a person who falls behind or is slow; slow; sluggish
chinese: n. 落後者；拖延者；adj. 遲緩的；落後的
example: In this context, “laggard” refers to someone who takes more time than necessary; someone who lags behind.

definition: a small gift given to a customer with a purchase; an unexpected bonus
chinese: 小贈品；額外贈送；意外之喜
example: The islanders thought that the seafarers had brought them a lagniappe when the latter presented them with gold coins; little did the islanders know that their days of bartering were numbered.

definition: lay people as distinct from the clergy; people without professional knowledge
chinese: 平信徒；俗人；外行人
example: Tensions grew when the laity questioned the primacy of the clergy in moral decision-making.

definition: to criticize harshly; to scold severely; to beat soundly
chinese: 嚴厲斥責；猛烈抨擊；痛打
example: Editorials continued to lambaste officials for ignoring the warnings.

definition: softly bright or radiant; flickering lightly over a surface; (of wit) light and brilliant
chinese: 柔和光亮的；（火焰）搖曳的；（機智）輕妙的
example: The passage describes its subject as lambent, meaning softly bright or radiant.

definition: to mourn; to express grief or regret about; a passionate expression of grief; an elegy
chinese: v. 哀悼；悲嘆；痛惜；n. 哀悼；輓歌
example: There has never been an age that did not applaud the past and lament the present.

definition: to publicly ridicule by satire; a satirical attack on a person or idea
chinese: v. 諷刺；嘲諷；n. 諷刺文章
example: It's easy to lampoon their ideas now, but they seemed quite reasonable at the time.

definition: a long spear used by a mounted soldier; a soldier armed with one; to pierce; to cut open (a boil) surgically
chinese: n. 長矛；槍騎兵；v. 刺破；（醫）切開
example: The knight had a blue pennon hanging from the end of his lance.

definition: lacking energy or vitality; relaxed and slow; weak
chinese: 無精打采的；懶洋洋的；倦怠的；虛弱的
example: It's the village of languid people, who face down, who stomach up: what could it be?

definition: to suffer from being kept in an unpleasant place or situation; to be neglected; to fail to make progress; to grow weak; to pine
chinese: （在惡劣處境中）受苦；被冷落；停滯不前；衰弱；憔悴
example: He left his best friend to languish behind bars.

definition: tiredness or lack of energy; a pleasantly lazy, dreamy feeling; oppressive stillness
chinese: 倦怠；無精打采；慵懶舒適；（空氣）沉悶
example: In this context, “languor” refers to a relaxed comfortable feeling.

definition: (of hair) straight and limp; long and thin; lean; limp
chinese: （頭髮）平直無光澤的；細長瘦弱的；柔軟下垂的
example: The passage describes its subject as lank, meaning long and thin and often limp.

definition: a brief failure of concentration or judgment; a minor error; an interval of time; a temporary decline; to expire; to pass gradually into (a state); to elapse
chinese: n. 小過失；疏忽；（時間）流逝；中斷；v. 失效；陷入；（時間）消逝
example: Schwartzberg is known for his dazzling time-lapse nature photography.

definition: generosity in giving money or gifts; gifts so given; liberality
chinese: 慷慨贈與；賞賜；慷慨大方
example: Thou shalt be generous, and give largesse to everyone.

definition: feeling or showing open sexual desire; lustful; lewd
chinese: 好色的；淫蕩的；挑逗的
example: Jerry’s coworkers were confused as to why Jerry thought that the word mango carried lascivious connotations; when he tried to explain, they only became more perplexed.

definition: to strike with force; to beat against; to whip; to criticize harshly; to tie tightly; a whip; a stroke with a whip; an eyelash
chinese: v. 猛擊；拍打；鞭打；嚴厲抨擊；捆綁；n. 鞭子；鞭打；睫毛
example: The sea waves lash incessantly against the cliffs.

definition: a state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy; listlessness
chinese: 倦怠；疲乏；無精打采
example: We can't abandon our principles out of moral lassitude.

definition: existing but not yet developed or visible; dormant; concealed
chinese: 潛在的；潛伏的；隱藏的
example: You have a latent problem here that will cause trouble in the future.

definition: scope for freedom of action or thought; tolerance; the angular distance north or south of the equator; a region

example: Persecution mania plagues him, causing persistent feelings of being targeted and unjustly treated.

definition: to show or display; to become apparent; clear or obvious; evident; a list of cargo or passengers
chinese: v. 顯現；表明；adj. 明顯的；顯而易見的；n. 艙單
example: Though the seasons manifest themselves in all sorts of ways, they remain, nonetheless, abstract constructs.

definition: to control or influence cleverly or unfairly; to handle skillfully; to alter (data) deceptively; to operate by hand
chinese: 操縱；擺布；巧妙處理；竄改（數據）；操作
example: Narcissists exploit others' weaknesses and vulnerabilities, using them as leverage to control and manipulate.

definition: artificial or affected in style; having manners of a specified kind
chinese: 矯揉造作的；不自然的；有…禮貌的
example: Children aren't naturally obedient any more than they're naturally well mannered.

definition: of or done with the hands; physical; operated by hand; a handbook
chinese: adj. 手的；手工的；體力的；手動的；n. 手冊；指南
example: manual dexterity

definition: to release from slavery or servitude
chinese: 解放（奴隸）；使擺脫奴役
example: In this context, “manumit” means free from slavery or servitude.

definition: a text submitted for publication; a handwritten document; an ancient handwritten book; written by hand
chinese: n. 原稿；手稿；手抄本；adj. 手寫的
example: Here is the rough draft of the manuscript, but the errors still have to be corrected.

definition: a large number of; a large number of people or things; the majority
chinese: adj. 許多的；n. 許多人；多數
example: many temptations

definition: to impair the quality or appearance of; to spoil; to disfigure
chinese: 損傷；破壞；玷汙；削弱
example: The chief maréchal des logis performs supervisory duties in territorial or mobile brigades.

definition: small and not important; minor; at the edge; barely adequate; written in a margin
chinese: 微小的；次要的；邊緣的；勉強及格的；頁邊的
example: There is only a marginal difference between the two.

definition: to arrange or assemble (facts, troops) in order; to guide ceremoniously; a high-ranking military officer; a federal law officer; an official organizing an event
chinese: v. 整理；集結；調度；引導；n. 元帥；（美國）法警；典禮官
example: marshal the troops

definition: a strict disciplinarian, esp. in the military
chinese: 嚴格執行紀律的人；嚴厲監督者
example: The job seemed perfect to Rebecca, until she found out that her boss was a total martinet; after each project the boss would come by to scrutinize—and inevitably criticize—every little detail of the work Rebecca had done.

definition: a wonderful or astonishing thing or person; to be filled with wonder
chinese: n. 奇蹟；奇人；奇事；v. 驚嘆；感到驚奇
example: Extracts from the sample we took earlier have revealed a great marvel.

definition: to crush into a soft mass; a soft pulpy mass; malt mixed with hot water; mashed potatoes
chinese: v. 搗碎；壓爛；n. 糊狀物；麥芽漿；馬鈴薯泥
example: Mash this sprout with a little salt and rub it on the swollen part.

definition: a false show or pretense; a masked ball; to pretend to be someone one is not; to disguise oneself
chinese: n. 偽裝；假象；化裝舞會；v. 偽裝；冒充
example: The princess held a masquerade ball in the grand ballroom.

definition: comprehensive knowledge or skill; control; superiority
chinese: 精通；熟練；掌握；控制；優勢
example: Many people say that learning a foreign language requires mastery of vocabulary and grammar.

definition: relevance or significance, esp. in law or accounting; the quality of being physical; physical substance
chinese: 重要性；實質性；物質性；實體
example: In this context, “materiality” refers to relevance requiring careful consideration.

definition: to come into being; to become reality; to appear suddenly; to give material form to
chinese: 實現；成為事實；出現；具體化；使物質化
example: Fears of hypotheticals that never materialize don't trump the urgent need to fix a real, concrete problem.

definition: to be enrolled at a college or university; to admit as a student; a person who has matriculated
chinese: v. 入學；註冊入學；准許入學；n. 已註冊入學者
example: In this context, “matriculate” means someone who has been admitted to a college or university.

definition: self-pityingly or tearfully sentimental, often from drunkenness
chinese: 過度感傷的；（酒後）傷感的；愛哭的
example: Just as those who were alive during the 70’s are mortified that they once cavorted about in bell- bottoms, many who lived during the 80’s are now aghast at the maudlin pop songs they used to enjoy— really, just what exactly is a total eclipse of the heart?

definition: an expert or connoisseur
chinese: 專家；行家；內行
example: She is a fashion maven with a lot of influence.

definition: an independent-minded person who does not conform; an unbranded calf; unorthodox; independent
chinese: n. 特立獨行者；標新立異者；未烙印的小牛；adj. 特立獨行的；不合常規的
example: His maverick attitude toward generally-accepted best practices didn't endear him to his superiors.

definition: excessively and feebly sentimental; sickly or insipid in taste
chinese: 過度傷感的；故作多情的；淡而無味的
example: The film's mawkish ending undermined its earlier restraint.

definition: lacking in quantity or quality; scanty; thin
chinese: 貧乏的；不足的；少量的；瘦弱的
example: The beggar rattled a few meager coins in his tin can.

definition: unkind or spiteful; ignoble; stingy; of low birth or status; inferior; to signify; to intend; an average; a middle course
chinese: adj. 刻薄的；卑鄙的；吝嗇的；卑賤的；低劣的；v. 意指；意圖；n. 平均值；中庸
example: I'm pretty sure that that mean teacher will give us a hard test today.

definition: to wander aimlessly; (of a river) to follow a winding course; (of speech) to digress; a winding curve or bend
chinese: v. 漫步；閒逛；（河流）蜿蜒；（談話）離題；n. 河曲；蜿蜒
example: Explorers looked for shortcuts in space-time to meander serendipitously through the universe.

definition: contemptibly small or few; having measles
chinese: 少得可憐的；微不足道的；患麻疹的
example: I was only paid a measly two dollars.

definition: a degree or extent; an action taken to achieve a purpose; moderation or limit; a standard or unit of measurement; a measuring instrument; to find the size of; to assess
chinese: n. 程度；措施；分寸；尺度；量具；v. 測量；衡量；評估
example: Measure the length of the wall

definition: carefully considered; restrained; slow and regular in rhythm
chinese: 慎重的；深思熟慮的；有節制的；（步伐）穩重有節奏的
example: The value of a good education cannot be measured in terms of money.

definition: to interfere in something not one's concern; to tamper
chinese: 干涉；管閒事；干預；亂動
example: He does not pass up any opportunity to meddle in other people's business.

definition: given to interfering in others' affairs
chinese: 愛管閒事的；好干涉的
example: She's a meddlesome old gossip.

definition: to intervene to resolve a dispute; to bring about (an agreement); to act as an intermediary or channel for
chinese: 調解；調停；促成；作為媒介
example: An independent advisor has been brought in to mediate between the unions and the employers.

definition: the science of treating disease; a drug; nonsurgical treatment; a remedy; to treat with medicine
chinese: n. 醫學；藥；內科；療法；v. 用藥治療
example: Those who have never thought about the value of life should not study medicine.

definition: of only average quality; ordinary; not very good
chinese: 平庸的；平凡的；普通的；品質不佳的
example: He could have become a wonderful surgeon, but became a mediocre psychologist.

definition: the quality of being average or undistinguished; a person of mediocre ability
chinese: 平庸；平凡；庸才
example: She always plays big, never settling for mediocrity in her endeavors.

definition: to think deeply about; to focus the mind in contemplation; to plan or intend
chinese: 沉思；深思；冥想；策劃
example: Someone who works a lot doesn't have time to meditate on philosophical matters.

definition: a means of communication or expression; an intervening substance; an artist's material; a middle state; a person claiming to contact spirits; of middle size or degree
chinese: n. 媒介；手段；媒材；中間；靈媒；adj. 中等的；中號的
example: The sun is a medium-sized star, but some stars are much larger or smaller.

definition: a varied mixture; songs or tunes played as one piece; (swimming) a race using several strokes
chinese: 混合物；大雜燴；（音樂）組曲；（游泳）混合式
example: This vegetable medley is really good.

definition: quiet, gentle, and submissive; humble; easily imposed on
chinese: 溫順的；順從的；謙和的；懦弱的
example: Ziri told his daughter that being meek would make people take advantage of her.

definition: patient, submissive humbleness; gentleness
chinese: 溫順；順從；謙和
example: In this context, “meekness” refers to the feeling of patient, submissive humbleness.

definition: (formal) suitable; proper; to encounter; to satisfy (a need or demand); to fulfill; a sports competition
chinese: adj. 合適的；恰當的；v. 遇見；滿足（需求）；符合；n. 運動會
example: She is always ready to meet him halfway when she has an argument with him.

definition: sad and pensive; causing sadness; a deep, long-lasting sadness
chinese: adj. 憂鬱的；悲傷的；令人傷感的；n. 憂鬱；愁思
example: growing more melancholy every hour

definition: a confused fight; a noisy, confused struggle or argument; a confused crowd
chinese: 混戰；亂鬥；激烈論戰；混亂人群
example: A melee ensued after a crunching tackle on the edge of the penalty area.

definition: sweetly or smoothly flowing; pleasant to hear
chinese: （聲音）甜美流暢的；悅耳的
example: Chelsea’s grandmother thought Franz Schubert’s music to be the most mellifluous ever written; Chelsea demurred, and to her grandmother’s chagrin, would blast Rihanna on the home stereo speakers.

definition: exaggeratedly emotional; overdramatic; relating to melodrama
chinese: 誇張做作的；感情誇張的；通俗劇的
example: Don't you think you're being a bit melodramatic?

definition: a threat or danger; a dangerous or annoying person; to threaten; to endanger
chinese: n. 威脅；危險人物；討厭鬼；v. 威脅；危及
example: Her face was distorted and malignant with menace.

definition: threatening; suggesting danger or harm
chinese: 威脅的；險惡的；不祥的
example: He stood for an instant, and then he crept forward, crouching, menacing, into the room.

definition: lying; untruthful; dishonest
chinese: 說謊的；虛假的；不誠實的
example: Tell the truth in a hypocritical, mendacious world, and you'll be taken for insane.

definition: the tendency to be untruthful; dishonesty; a lie
chinese: 說謊；虛假；不誠實；謊言
example: Repeated contradictions eventually revealed the witness's mendacity.

definition: (of work) lowly and requiring little skill; servile; a domestic servant
chinese: adj. 卑微的；低下的；（工作）粗活的；卑躬屈膝的；n. 僕役
example: The job was boring and menial.

definition: relating to the mind; intellectual; relating to mental illness
chinese: 心理的；精神的；心智的；智力的；精神病的
example: mental images of happy times

definition: an experienced and trusted adviser; to advise or train
chinese: n. 良師；導師；顧問；v. 指導；輔導
example: Adriano's star potential was recognized by his mentor, who offered to train him further.

definition: motivated chiefly by money or gain; hired for service; a soldier hired to fight; a person motivated by gain
chinese: adj. 唯利是圖的；貪財的；受僱的；n. 傭兵；唯利是圖者
example: He was a mercenary, but preferred to call himself a soldier of fortune.

definition: subject to sudden mood changes; volatile; lively and quick-witted; containing mercury
chinese: 善變的；反覆無常的；機靈的；水銀的
example: The fact that Ella’s moods were as mercurial as the weather was problematic for her relationships—it didn’t help that she lived in Chicago.

definition: apparently attractive but having no real value; superficially plausible; gaudy; relating to prostitutes
chinese: 華而不實的；虛有其表的；似是而非的；俗豔的；娼妓的
example: Pervasive and pernicious deviations from both fact and logical validity lurked behind a meretricious plausibility.

definition: to combine into one; to blend gradually; to join a stream of traffic
chinese: 合併；融合；漸漸融入；（車道）匯入
example: He was given a tip three weeks ago that two companies would merge.

definition: deserved; justified
chinese: 應得的；理所當然的；值得的
example: Although she was merited with many an accolade, we still don’t know what she did to deserve them.

definition: deserving reward or praise; praiseworthy
chinese: 值得稱讚的；有功勞的；有價值的
example: a lifetime of meritorious service

definition: to fit together harmoniously; (of gears) to engage; to entangle; an opening in a net; netlike material; a trap
chinese: v. 契合；相配；（齒輪）嚙合；網住；n. 網眼；網狀物；圈套
example: The metal mesh is assembled on huge automated machines that weld many joints at once.

definition: holding attention as if by a spell; hypnotic
chinese: 令人著迷的；懾人心魄的；催眠的
example: The passage describes its subject as mesmeric, meaning attracting and holding interest as if by a spell.

definition: to captivate completely; to hypnotize
chinese: 迷住；使著迷；施催眠術
example: Snakes are said to mesmerize small animals and birds.

definition: to change completely in form or nature; to transform
chinese: （使）變形；（使）蛻變；徹底改變
example: Over several decades, the industrial district began to metamorphose into a residential area.

definition: a figure of speech applying a word to something it does not literally denote; a symbol
chinese: 隱喻；暗喻；象徵
example: It's apparently a metaphor for something uncatchable, light of body and fleet of foot.

definition: relating to metaphysics; highly abstract or theoretical; transcending physical reality; relating to the 17th-century Metaphysical poets
chinese: 形上學的；抽象的；超自然的；（詩）玄學派的
example: Mathematics has not a foot to stand upon which is not purely metaphysical.

definition: very rapid; sudden and brilliant; relating to meteors
chinese: 迅速的；快速崛起的；短暫輝煌的；流星的
example: Tebboune has recently seen a meteoric rise in popularity.

definition: done according to a systematic order; orderly; careful and thorough
chinese: 有條理的；井然有序的；有系統的；一絲不苟的
example: Andrés is very methodical in his work.

definition: showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise; overly scrupulous
chinese: 一絲不苟的；極為細心的；謹小慎微的
example: He's meticulous when it comes to his outfit.

definition: courage and spirit; resilience in difficulty; stamina
chinese: 勇氣；毅力；氣魄；耐力
example: She proved her mettle to her comrades with each challenge they faced together.

definition: full of spirit and courage; lively; (of a horse) high-spirited
chinese: 精神飽滿的；勇敢的；有活力的；（馬）烈性的
example: The passage describes its subject as mettlesome, meaning having a proud and unbroken spirit.

definition: to annoy or offend slightly; a fit of irritation; a petty quarrel
chinese: v. 使惱怒；使生氣；n. 惱怒；小爭吵
example: In this context, “miff” refers to cause to be annoyed.

definition: possessing great power or strength; very large or forceful; (informal) extremely
chinese: adj. 強大的；有力的；巨大的；adv. （口）非常
example: struck a mighty blow

definition: migrating seasonally; moving from one region to another
chinese: 遷徙的；遷移的；流動的
example: Many migratory birds rely on wetlands as a crucial stopover point during their journeys.

definition: the physical or social setting in which something occurs
chinese: 環境；氛圍；背景；社會環境
example: Maybe in another universe, beings are like clouds or shadows in a cloudy or shadowy milieu...

definition: to exploit or extract maximum gain from; to take advantage of; to draw milk from; the white fluid produced by mammals
chinese: v. 榨取；剝削；充分利用；擠奶；n. 牛奶；乳汁
example: A whale is a mammal; in other words it feeds milk to its young.

definition: the art of acting through gestures without words; a mime artist; to act out with gestures; to imitate; to lip-sync
chinese: n. 默劇；默劇演員；v. 以動作表演；模仿；對嘴
example: The mime-artist doesn't speak, only mimes.

definition: to imitate, often to mock; to simulate; (biology) to resemble another organism; a person skilled at imitation; imitative; simulated
chinese: v. 模仿；模擬；（生物）擬態；n. 善於模仿者；adj. 模仿的；模擬的
example: Vaccines mimic an infection, which causes the body's immune system to mount a defense.

definition: expressing a threat; menacing; ominous
chinese: 威脅的；恐嚇的；有凶兆的
example: The letter's minatory language warned of severe consequences.

definition: to mix or combine; to move around and socialize at a gathering
chinese: 混合；交際；相混；（與人）往來
example: I don't like to mingle with people who can't share my life interests.

definition: to reduce to the smallest possible amount; to represent as less important; to underestimate
chinese: 降至最低；減到最少；輕視；低估
example: When dusting the shelves, use a microfiber cloth to minimize particles in the air.

definition: the provision of help or care; assistance; the performance of religious duties
chinese: 照料；幫助；援助；（宗教）主持儀式
example: In this context, “ministration” refers to assistance in time of difficulty.

definition: to make (coins); to coin (a word or phrase); a vast sum of money; a place where coins are made; an aromatic plant; in pristine condition
chinese: v. 鑄造（硬幣）；創造（新詞）；n. 鉅款；造幣廠；薄荷；adj. 完好如新的
example: It costs more to mint a penny than the penny itself is worth.

definition: extremely small; tiny; (of letters) lowercase
chinese: 極小的；微不足道的；（字母）小寫的
example: The amount of arsenic in the water is minuscule but significant.

definition: extremely small; trivial; precise and detailed; careful; a sixtieth of an hour; a moment
chinese: adj. 微小的；細微的；詳盡的；仔細的；n. 分鐘；片刻
example: The best argument against democracy is a five-minute conversation with the average voter.

definition: a written record of what happened at a meeting; plural of minute (sixtieths of an hour)
chinese: 會議紀錄；分鐘
example: The fire brigade was on the scene within five minutes of receiving the call.

definition: small, precise, or trivial details
chinese: 細枝末節；瑣事；細節
example: "You have an extraordinary genius for minutiae," I remarked.

definition: an optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions; something illusory or unattainable
chinese: 海市蜃樓；幻象；妄想
example: Being convinced of your own unassailable rationality is like being convinced of the solidity of a mirage.

definition: a difficult situation; a stretch of swampy ground; deep mud; to involve in difficulties; to stick in mud; to hold back; to soil
chinese: n. 困境；泥沼；泥潭；v. 使陷入困境；使陷入泥沼；拖累；弄髒
example: This is what the vox populi reports: he who stirs up the mire brings the mud to the surface.

definition: entangled or hindered in difficulty; stuck as if in mud
chinese: 陷入困境的；深陷其中的；陷入泥沼的
example: The very manner in which the greedy miser carried himself was mired in foul wretchedness.

definition: amusement expressed in laughter; gladness
chinese: 歡笑；歡樂；高興
example: This joke is a source of mirth for the audience.

definition: full of or showing high-spirited merriment
chinese: 歡樂的；愉快的；歡笑的
example: The passage describes its subject as mirthful, meaning full of or showing high-spirited merriment.

definition: a person who dislikes and avoids people in general
chinese: 厭世者；厭惡人類者；不合群的人
example: Hamilton had been deceived so many times in his life that he hid behind the gruff exterior of a misanthrope, lambasting perfect strangers for no apparent reason.

definition: disliking and distrusting humankind
chinese: 厭世的；厭惡人類的；不信任人的
example: Someone who is misanthropic dislikes people and avoids social situations.

definition: a mistaken belief or failure to understand
chinese: 誤解；誤會；錯誤認知
example: The dispute arose from a misapprehension about the study's purpose.

definition: behaving badly (present participle of misbehave); badly behaved; naughty
chinese: v. 行為不端；調皮搗蛋；adj. 行為不端的
example: They both got sent to the principal's office for misbehaving in class.

definition: playfully troublesome; naughty; causing harm or trouble
chinese: 淘氣的；調皮的；惡作劇的；有害的
example: You're sniggering like a mischievous little brat who's just cooked up a dirty trick.

definition: to interpret wrongly; to misunderstand
chinese: 誤解；曲解
example: You've somehow managed to misconstrue what I have said.

definition: a person who behaves badly or unlawfully; villainous; (archaic) heretical
chinese: n. 惡棍；歹徒；罪犯；adj. 邪惡的；（古）異端的
example: The story's miscreant secretly altered the records for personal gain.

definition: (British spelling) a criminal offense less serious than a felony; a minor wrongdoing
chinese: 輕罪；不端行為；品行不良
example: In this context, “misdemeanour” refers to a crime less serious than a felony.

definition: stingy like a miser; (of an amount) meager
chinese: 吝嗇的；小氣的；極少的
example: A generous person enriches themselves by giving; a miserly person impoverishes themselves by taking.

definition: a feeling of doubt or apprehension
chinese: 疑慮；擔憂；不安
example: Happy days of childish credulity, when fact and fiction were swallowed alike without a misgiving!

definition: an unlucky accident; a minor mishap or misfortune
chinese: 不幸事故；小意外；災禍
example: Isabel's adroit handling of the scheduling mishap didn't go unnoticed by her superiors.

definition: a wrong or inaccurate name or designation
chinese: 名不副實；誤稱；用詞不當
example: It's a misnomer to refer to non-crypto-currency as "fiat," since cryptocurrency is also fiat.

definition: to give a false or misleading account of
chinese: 歪曲；誤傳；不實陳述；扭曲
example: Journalists need to be careful not to misrepresent information.

definition: a false or misleading account; (law) a false statement inducing a contract
chinese: 歪曲；不實陳述；誤傳；（法律）虛偽陳述
example: As soon as the news of this discovery was made known, false reports, misrepresentation, and slander flew as on the wings of the wind in every direction.

definition: a self-propelled weapon carrying a warhead; an object thrown or fired at a target
chinese: 飛彈；導彈；投擲物；發射物
example: Their missile strikes had a limited impact, mostly creating craters in open terrain.

definition: a tiny arachnid; a very small creature or thing; a small amount; a small child; (archaic) a small coin
chinese: 蟎；微小之物；一點點；小孩；（古）小額錢幣
example: Scabies is caused by a mite.

definition: to make less severe or painful; to alleviate; (law) to lessen the gravity of
chinese: 減輕；緩和；（法律）從輕
