definition: designed to impress or attract notice; showy, pretentious
chinese: 炫耀的；賣弄的；鋪張的；招搖的
example: The passage describes its subject as ostentatious, meaning intended to attract notice and impress others.

definition: to exclude from a society or group; to shun; (ancient Greece) to banish by popular vote
chinese: 排斥；排擠；放逐；（古希臘）陶片放逐
example: In this context, “ostracize” means avoid speaking to or dealing with.

definition: to remove from a position or office; to drive out; to replace
chinese: 罷黜；免職；逐出；取代
example: In this context, “oust” means remove from a position or office.

definition: no longer fashionable or current; old-fashioned; no longer valid
chinese: 過時的；舊式的；失效的
example: There is nothing more out-of-date than youthful entitlement.

definition: a natural result or development of something; a product; something that grows out of something else
chinese: 自然結果；產物；衍生物；分枝
example: The reform was an outgrowth of years of public dissatisfaction.

definition: strikingly strange or unusual; bizarre; absurd
chinese: 古怪的；奇異的；荒誕的
example: His right-wing media bubble served to validate even his most outlandish ideas.

definition: a summary of main points; the shape or contour of something; to describe the main points of; to draw the outer edge of
chinese: n. 大綱；概要；輪廓；v. 概述；勾勒輪廓
example: sketch the outline of the book

definition: to gain an advantage over by more skillful or clever tactics; to outwit
chinese: 以策略勝過；智勝
example: He tried to outmaneuver me to get the promotion instead of me.

definition: no longer in fashion; out-of-date; no longer usable or acceptable
chinese: 過時的；陳舊的；不再適用的
example: The teacher's method of teaching is so outmoded.

definition: shockingly bad or offensive; wildly unreasonable or exaggerated; exceeding the limits
chinese: 駭人聽聞的；令人憤慨的；荒唐的；過分的
example: At least ninety percent of the students disagreed with the professor's outrageous statement.

definition: the start or beginning
chinese: 開端；開始
example: It was clear from the outset that the discussion would end again in argument.

definition: to exceed or surpass; to move faster than and overtake
chinese: 超過；勝過；超越
example: In this context, “outstrip” means be or do something to a greater degree.

definition: to defeat or get the better of by being cleverer
chinese: 以智取勝；智勝
example: In this context, “outwit” means beat through cleverness and wit.

definition: unpleasantly domineering and arrogant; overwhelming in importance or effect
chinese: 專橫的；傲慢的；壓倒性的
example: What really makes us stand out is actually our great and overbearing number.

definition: to extend over and partly cover; to coincide in part; a part or amount that overlaps; common ground
chinese: v. 部分重疊；交疊；n. 重疊部分；共通處
example: The directors' style is far more different than similar, but there is certainly some overlap.

definition: to be more important than; to take precedence over; to set aside or overrule (a decision)
chinese: 凌駕；優先於；推翻；否決
example: We view compliance with existing standards as important, but this does not override our own requirements.

definition: to make seem less important by comparison; to cast a shadow over; to cast gloom over
chinese: 使相形見絀；使黯然失色；遮蔽；蒙上陰影
example: I never intended to overshadow her accomplishments.

definition: done or shown openly; plainly apparent; not hidden
chinese: 公開的；明顯的；不加掩飾的
example: The speaker believes that overt expression of feeling for others helps people tap into their own repressed emotions.

definition: a formal proposal or approach to begin negotiations or a relationship; an orchestral introduction to an opera; an introductory part
chinese: 提議；試探性接觸；（音樂）序曲；開端
example: A majority of two thirds is required to ratify an overture.

definition: showing excessive confidence or pride; arrogant; excessive or immoderate
chinese: 傲慢的；過分自負的；過度的
example: Mark was so convinced of his basketball skills that in his overweening pride he could not fathom that his name was not on the varsity list; he walked up to the basketball coach and told her she had forgotten to add his name.

definition: to overpower in thought or feeling; to defeat completely; to bury or flood
chinese: 壓倒；使不知所措；使難以承受；淹沒
example: Too much emotion can overwhelm the mind and hinder clear thinking.

definition: in a state of nervous excitement or anxiety; (of writing or decoration) too elaborate or ornate
chinese: 極度激動的；焦躁不安的；（文風）過分雕琢的；（裝飾）過分華麗的
example: At the funeral, the widow was overwrought with grief.

definition: a figure of speech combining contradictory terms; something self-contradictory
chinese: 矛盾修飾法；矛盾語；自相矛盾的說法
example: The phrase 'honest politician' is an oxymoron.

definition: to calm the anger or agitation of; to soothe; to bring peace to (an area) by force
chinese: 使平靜；安撫；平息；綏靖
example: He finds it easier to just pacify her than be straight up with her.

definition: soft material used to fill, shape, or protect; unnecessary material added to lengthen speech or writing
chinese: 襯墊；填充物；（文章中的）贅詞；灌水內容
example: Her jacket had padding in the shoulders.

definition: a song or expression of praise or triumph; an enthusiastic tribute
chinese: 讚歌；頌揚；歡樂之歌
example: This is a precise and poetic paean to the peregrine.

definition: a public spectacle with elaborate costumes, often depicting history; an impressive display; a beauty contest; empty or showy display
chinese: 盛大遊行；露天歷史劇；壯觀場面；選美比賽；虛飾
example: Do you know what the name of last year's beauty pageant winner is?

definition: done with or employing great care and thoroughness; diligent
chinese: 煞費苦心的；極其仔細的；勤勉的
example: Restoring and refurbishing the carousel and its animals after years of alterations was a slow, painstaking process.

definition: acceptable or agreeable to the mind; pleasant to taste
chinese: 可接受的；令人滿意的；美味的；可口的
example: The pilot was revised to be more palatable to a mature audience.

definition: resembling a palace; spacious and splendid
chinese: 宮殿般的；富麗堂皇的；宏偉的
example: The passage describes its subject as palatial, meaning relating to or being a palace.

definition: prolonged idle talk; tedious fuss; a parley or conference; to talk idly and at length
chinese: n. 閒扯；冗長的討論；大驚小怪；談判；v. 閒聊；嘮叨
example: We have no time to waste in idle palaver.

definition: lacking color; light in shade; dim or feeble; to seem less important by comparison; to become pale; a boundary or limit (beyond the pale); a fence stake
chinese: adj. 蒼白的；淺色的；暗淡的；微弱的；v. 相形見絀；變蒼白；n. 界限；範圍；柵欄
example: pale seagreen

definition: of or relating to the early Stone Age; very ancient
chinese: 舊石器時代的；遠古的
example: paleolithic artifacts

definition: a manuscript on which earlier writing has been partly erased and overwritten; something bearing visible traces of earlier forms
chinese: 重寫本；層層疊加的事物；留有歷史痕跡之物
example: The downtown was a palimpsest of the city’s checkered past: a new Starbucks had opened up next to an abandoned, shuttered building, and a freshly asphalted road was inches away from a pothole large enough to swallow a house pet.

definition: to become less interesting or attractive; a dark cloud or covering of smoke; a gloomy atmosphere; a cloth spread over a coffin
chinese: v. 失去吸引力；變得乏味；n. 籠罩的陰影；（煙等）幕罩；棺罩
example: The city is being blanketed again today by a thick pall of smoke from nearby bushfires.

definition: to make less severe without curing; to make (an offense) seem less serious; to excuse
chinese: 減輕；緩和；掩飾（過錯）；辯解
example: His friend tried to palliate the offense but nobody cared about that.

definition: relieving pain or symptoms without curing; superficially easing; a remedy that relieves without curing; a stopgap measure
chinese: adj. 緩和的；減輕痛苦的；治標不治本的；n. 緩和劑；權宜之計
example: She was a palliative care nurse until her retirement.

definition: pale, typically from poor health; lacking vitality or interest; dull
chinese: 蒼白的；無血色的；缺乏活力的；乏味的
example: Only someone who never spent any time in the sun could look so pallid.

definition: flourishing and prosperous (as in palmy days); thriving
chinese: 繁榮的；興盛的；全盛的
example: The passage describes its subject as palmy, meaning very lively and profitable.

definition: so intense or obvious as to be easily perceived; able to be touched or felt
chinese: 明顯的；可察覺的；可觸知的
example: The regret in his voice was palpable.

definition: a noticeably rapid, strong, or irregular heartbeat; a throbbing or trembling
chinese: 心悸；（心臟）急速跳動；顫動
example: In this context, “palpitation” refers to a rapid and irregular heart beat.

definition: to act or talk insincerely or evasively; to equivocate; to haggle
chinese: 含糊其辭；搪塞；敷衍；討價還價
example: In this context, “palter” means be deliberately ambiguous or unclear in order to mislead or withhold information.

definition: (of an amount) very small or meager; trivial or worthless; contemptible
chinese: 微不足道的；少得可憐的；無價值的；卑劣的
example: They apologize for the paltry offering and hope you'll accept $50,000.

definition: to criticize severely; to swing (a camera) horizontally; to wash gravel for gold; a shallow metal cooking vessel; a dish
chinese: v. 嚴厲批評；酷評；（鏡頭）搖攝；淘洗（金沙）；n. 平底鍋；盤
example: It looks like you've gone out of the frying pan and into the fire.

definition: a supposed remedy for all ills or difficulties; a cure-all
chinese: 萬靈丹；萬能藥；解決一切問題的方法
example: It's no panacea, but it can serve as a temporary remedy.

definition: flamboyant confidence of style or manner; dash; a plume of feathers on a helmet
chinese: 神氣十足；瀟灑的氣派；華麗風采；（頭盔上的）羽飾
example: You have to lose with panache.

definition: an outbreak of disease spreading over a whole country or the world; (of a disease) widespread; prevalent everywhere
chinese: n. 全球大流行病；大流行；adj. （疾病）大範圍流行的；普遍的
example: What this pandemic has provided is an opportunity to reflect on these many blessings.

definition: wild and noisy disorder or confusion; uproar
chinese: 大混亂；喧囂；騷動
example: When the musicians threw t-shirts into the audience, pandemonium ensued.

definition: a public speech or text in high praise of someone or something; a eulogy
chinese: 頌詞；讚頌文；頌揚
example: The art review sounded more like a panegyric than a neutral assessment.

definition: providing a wide, unbroken view; comprehensive in scope
chinese: 全景的；概觀的；全面的
example: This castle tower commands a panoramic view of the whole city.

definition: a typical example or model of something; a framework of theories and methods; a pattern
chinese: 典範；範式；模式；範例
example: We need to postulate a completely different paradigm to explain all these phenomena.

definition: heaven; an ideal or idyllic place or state; a state of supreme happiness
chinese: 天堂；樂園；理想境地；極樂
example: At first glance, the videos conjure up visions of a secluded utopian paradise.

definition: a seemingly absurd or self-contradictory statement that may be true; a contradictory person or situation
chinese: 矛盾；悖論；似非而是的說法；矛盾的人或事
example: This has been a paradox, but now the time gives it proof.

definition: a model of excellence or perfection; a perfect example of a quality
chinese: 典範；模範；完美典型
example: In this context, “paragon” refers to an ideal instance; a perfect embodiment of a concept.

definition: more important than anything else; supreme
chinese: 至高無上的；最重要的；首要的
example: The regular upkeep of our servers is paramount to ensuring high uptime.

definition: unreasonably suspicious or mistrustful; suffering from paranoia; a person with paranoia
chinese: adj. 多疑的；偏執的；有被害妄想的；n. 偏執狂患者
example: He had reached the point where he was paranoid about being paranoid.

definition: to express the meaning of in different words; a restatement of a text in other words
chinese: v. 改述；意譯；釋義；n. 改寫；意譯
example: Don't repeat or paraphrase the question you're being asked because it sounds patronizing.

definition: to make or become dry through intense heat; to roast lightly; to make thirsty
chinese: 使乾透；烤乾；使焦乾；使口渴
example: In this context, “parch” means cause to wither or parch from exposure to heat.

definition: dried out by heat; extremely thirsty; (of grain) roasted
chinese: 乾透的；焦乾的；極渴的；（穀物）炒過的
example: The person who consumes chili will be parched.

definition: either of a pair of round brackets; a word or phrase inserted as an explanation; an interlude or interval
chinese: 括號；插入語；插曲；間歇
example: You have an unmatched open parenthesis in your first sentence.

definition: an outcast; a person who is despised or rejected by society
chinese: 被排斥者；遭唾棄的人；賤民
example: The once eminent scientist, upon being inculpated for fudging his data, has become a pariah in the research community.

definition: the state of being equal, especially in pay or status; equivalence of currency value; (math) the property of being odd or even
chinese: 平等；同等；對等；（經濟）平價；（數學）奇偶性
example: Guterres, who referred to himself as “a proud feminist,” also called for dismantling the “patriarchy” and moving toward gender parity.

definition: having a limited or narrow outlook; provincial; relating to a church parish
chinese: 狹隘的；眼界窄的；地方性的；教區的
example: Jasmine was sad to admit it, but her fledgling relationship with Jacob did not work out because his culinary tastes were simply too parochial; “After all,” she quipped on her blog, “he considered Chef Boyrdee ethnic food.”

definition: an imitation of a style for comic effect; a feeble or absurd imitation; to imitate mockingly
chinese: n. 諷刺性模仿作品；拙劣的模仿；v. 戲謔模仿；拙劣地模仿
example: The newspaper published a hilarious parody of the president's speech.

definition: a sudden outburst of emotion or activity; a sudden attack or intensification of a disease
chinese: （情緒的）突然爆發；一陣發作；（疾病的）陣發
example: Then suddenly he slapped his thigh in a paroxysm of amusement.

definition: to repeat mechanically without understanding; a tropical bird that can mimic speech; a person who repeats without understanding
chinese: v. 鸚鵡學舌般重複；機械模仿；n. 鸚鵡；學舌者
example: Be careful not to leave any small objects around that the parrot could swallow.

definition: to evade (a question) skillfully; to ward off (a blow); a defensive deflection; an evasive reply
chinese: v. 迴避（問題）；擋開（攻擊）；n. （擊劍）擋開；迴避
example: In this context, “parry” means (fencing) blocking a lunge or deflecting it with a circular motion of the sword.

definition: unwilling to spend money or resources; stingy; (of a theory) using the fewest assumptions
chinese: 極度節儉的；吝嗇的；（理論）簡約的
example: Even with millions in his bank account, Fred was so parsimonious that he followed a diet consisting of nothing more than bread and canned soup.

definition: extreme unwillingness to spend money; stinginess; economy of assumptions in explanation
chinese: 過度節儉；吝嗇；（理論的）簡約性
example: In this context, “parsimony” refers to extreme care in spending money; reluctance to spend money unnecessarily.

definition: biased in favor of one side; existing only in part; incomplete; having a liking for (partial to); (math) relating to partial derivatives
chinese: 偏袒的；偏頗的；部分的；不完全的；偏愛的；（數學）偏的
example: The finite element method enables us to find approximate solutions of partial differential equations.

definition: the quality of being individual or specific; a particular detail; fastidiousness
chinese: 特殊性；獨特性；細節；講究；挑剔
example: the particularity of human situations

definition: to treat or describe individually and in detail; to be specific about
chinese: 詳述；逐一列舉；具體說明
example: In this context, “particularize” means be specific about.

definition: relating to or composed of separate particles; a minute particle, especially as a pollutant
chinese: adj. 微粒的；顆粒狀的；n. 微粒；懸浮微粒
example: Some cruise ships emit as much particulate matter as 1m cars.

definition: strongly and often blindly supporting one party or cause; biased; a committed supporter; a guerrilla fighter
chinese: adj. 黨派性的；偏袒的；有偏見的；n. 堅定支持者；黨羽；游擊隊員
example: The partisan media is trying to keep the protests out of sight.

definition: the act of dividing; the division of a country into separate nations; a dividing wall; to divide into parts; to separate
chinese: n. 分割；劃分；（國家的）分治；隔牆；v. 分割；隔開
example: Some local authorities worry that further evacuations could deepen divisions and reinforce calls for a partition of the country.

definition: a person or group involved in an agreement or dispute; a political organization; a group of people; a social gathering; to celebrate at a party
chinese: n. 當事人；參與者；政黨；團體；聚會；宴會；v. 參加聚會
example: He said he wouldn't go to the party because he had to study.

definition: a person who has suddenly risen to wealth or status but lacks the corresponding manners; characteristic of such a person
chinese: n. 暴發戶；新貴；adj. 暴發戶的
example: In this context, “parvenu” refers to of or characteristic of a parvenu.

definition: no longer fashionable; out-of-date; past one's prime
chinese: 過時的；落伍的；已過全盛期的
example: The passage describes its subject as passe, meaning out of fashion.

definition: showing or driven by strong feeling; intensely enthusiastic; easily moved by emotion
chinese: 熱情的；熱烈的；熱愛的；易動感情的
example: William was a passionate student of science, eager to learn and discover new things.

definition: the quality of being inactive or submissive; lack of initiative or resistance
chinese: 被動；消極；順從；無抵抗
example: The difficulty of a task is no reason for passivity and doing nothing.

definition: an artistic work imitating the style of another work, artist, or period; a hodgepodge of mixed sources
chinese: 仿作；模仿作品；拼湊之作；大雜燴
example: Only an ardent fan could create such a faithful pastiche of the artist's works.

definition: something made of many different parts; a jumble; needlework of sewn-together pieces of cloth
chinese: 拼湊而成之物；大雜燴；拼布；拼布作品
example: From the plane, the landscape was just a patchwork of fields.

definition: easily recognizable; obvious; (of leather) glossy; an exclusive government right to an invention; to obtain a patent for
chinese: adj. 明顯的；顯而易見的；（皮革）亮漆的；n. 專利；專利權；v. 取得…的專利
example: He wore a tunic over a silk shirt and high patent leather boots.

definition: clearly; without doubt; openly
chinese: 明顯地；顯然地；公然地
example: The action occurs patently, meaning unmistakably (`plain' is often used informally for `plainly').

definition: arousing pity; pitiful; miserably inadequate
chinese: 可憐的；令人同情的；可悲的；差勁的
example: He had, she thought, the most pathetic eyes, large and honest, but quite irredeemably stupid.

definition: compulsive or markedly abnormal; relating to or caused by disease; relating to pathology
chinese: 病態的；極不正常的；強迫性的；病理學的
example: Sadness is not a pathological state; it is an unavoidable consequence of consciousness.

definition: a quality that evokes pity or sadness
chinese: 悲愴感；哀婉動人之處；引人憐憫的力量
example: the film captured all the pathos of their situation

definition: a superficial impression or aura; a sheen on a surface from age and use; a green or brown film on bronze or copper
chinese: 外在氣息；表象；（器物）光澤；包漿；銅綠
example: It has a nice patina on it.

definition: relating to a system in which men hold power; ruled by the male head of a family; of a patriarch
chinese: 父權的；男性主導的；家長制的；族長的
example: Society's patriarchal norms perpetuate the notion that femininity is inherently weaker or less valuable.

definition: belonging to the aristocracy; refined; an aristocrat; a person of refined upbringing and manners
chinese: adj. 貴族的；出身名門的；高雅的；n. 貴族；名門子弟；有教養的人
example: In this context, “patrician” refers to a person of refined upbringing and manners.

definition: a person who loves and supports his or her country
chinese: 愛國者
example: Frankly speaking, he is more of a hypocrite than a patriot.

definition: to treat with condescension; to support financially; to be a regular customer of
chinese: 以高人一等的態度對待；屈尊俯就；贊助；資助；光顧
example: Americans would respect you more if you did not patronize their culture and language.

definition: treating others with apparent kindness that betrays a feeling of superiority; condescending
chinese: 擺出高人一等姿態的；屈尊俯就的；居高臨下的
example: Don't repeat or paraphrase the question you're being asked because it sounds patronizing.

definition: the presence of something in only small amounts; scarcity; dearth
chinese: 缺乏；稀少；不足
example: There is a paucity of jobs hiring today that require menial skills, since most jobs have either been automated or outsourced.

definition: a small, relatively unimportant offense or fault
chinese: 小過失；輕罪；小毛病
example: The committee treated the minor bookkeeping error as a peccadillo.

definition: to strike or pick up with the beak; to kiss lightly; to eat in small bites; a light stroke; a unit of dry volume; a large amount
chinese: v. 啄；啄食；輕吻；小口吃；n. 啄；（容量）配克；大量
example: Woodpeckers peck tree trunks with their long pointed beaks and eat insects found there.

definition: to embezzle money or property entrusted to one's care
chinese: 盜用；挪用（公款）；侵吞
example: In this context, “peculate” means appropriate (as property entrusted to one's care) fraudulently to one's own use.

definition: strange or odd; belonging exclusively to (peculiar to); distinctive; special
chinese: 奇怪的；古怪的；特有的；獨特的；特殊的
example: That way of speaking is peculiar to people in this part of the country.

definition: a distinctive feature or characteristic; an odd habit or trait; strangeness
chinese: 特點；特性；怪癖；奇特之處
example: I have this peculiarity: I always spoil everything.

definition: relating to or consisting of money
chinese: 金錢的；金錢上的；財務的
example: I'm suffering from pecuniary embarrassment.

definition: relating to teaching or the methods of teaching; of a teacher
chinese: 教學的；教育學的；教師的
example: The passage describes its subject as pedagogical, meaning of or relating to pedagogy.

definition: a teacher; an educator, especially a strict or pedantic one
chinese: 教師；教育者；迂腐的教師
example: He is an extremely fine and articulate pedagogue.

definition: a foot-operated lever; to work the pedals of; to ride a bicycle; relating to the foot
chinese: n. 踏板；v. 踩踏板；騎（腳踏車）；adj. 腳的
example: the word for a pedal extremity is ‘foot’

definition: a person excessively concerned with minor details, rules, or displays of learning
chinese: 學究；賣弄學問者；拘泥細節或規則的人
example: He is what is called a pedant.

definition: excessively concerned with minor details or rules; showing off learning
chinese: 賣弄學問的；學究式的；拘泥細節的；迂腐的
example: Vanya is even more pedantic than I am.

definition: to sell goods by going from place to place; to promote an idea persistently; to spread (rumors); to sell (illegal drugs)
chinese: 兜售；叫賣；鼓吹（觀念）；散布（謠言）；販賣（毒品）
example: Peddle your wares somewhere else.

example: The piquant aroma of his food made everyone's mouth water.

definition: to stimulate (interest or curiosity); to irritate or wound the pride of; a feeling of irritation or resentment from wounded pride
chinese: v. 激起（好奇心）；引起（興趣）；使惱怒；傷…自尊心；n. 不悅；惱怒
example: This book might pique your mother’s curiosity.

definition: a person who robs ships at sea; a person who reproduces work illegally; to use or reproduce without permission
chinese: n. 海盜；盜版者；剽竊者；v. 盜版；盜用；剽竊
example: The pirate captain was secretly a slaver who sold prisoners across the sea.

definition: a hidden or unsuspected danger or difficulty; a covered pit used to trap animals
chinese: 隱患；潛在危險；陷阱；（捕獸）陷坑
example: The specimen was caught in a pitfall trap sunk in the ground.

definition: concise and forcefully expressive; terse and meaningful; containing much pith
chinese: 精練的；簡潔有力的；言簡意賅的；（果皮）多髓的
example: He couldn't come up with a pithy barb on the spot.

definition: showing no pity; cruel; harsh or relentless
chinese: 無情的；冷酷的；毫無憐憫的；（天氣）嚴酷的
example: The revenge will be pitiless.

definition: a very small or inadequate amount of money; a small portion
chinese: 微薄的收入；少量的錢；一點點
example: Vinny’s uncle beamed smugly about how he’d offered his nephew fifty dollars for his Harvard tuition; even twice the amount would have been a mere pittance.

definition: of crucial importance in relation to development or success; central
chinese: 關鍵的；極重要的；樞紐的
example: Chapter fifteen contained a pivotal moment in the protagonist's character arc.

definition: to make less angry or hostile, often by concessions; to appease; to pacify
chinese: 安撫；平息（怒氣）；撫慰
example: A compromise was reached to placate both sides.

definition: a harmless substance given for psychological effect or as a control; something said or done merely to appease
chinese: 安慰劑；聊以安慰的事物；敷衍搪塞的話
example: Even if faith were a placebo, I would rather have it than not.

definition: not easily upset or excited; calm and peaceful; (of water) smooth
chinese: 平靜的；溫和的；沉著的；（水面）平靜無波的
example: His placid face and regular breathing showed that he was fast asleep.

definition: to take the work or ideas of someone else and pass them off as one's own
chinese: 剽竊；抄襲
example: My sentences are original: this is why those who shamelessly plagiarize me denounce themselves.

definition: to cause continual trouble or distress; a cause of widespread affliction; a contagious epidemic disease; the bubonic plague
chinese: v. 困擾；折磨；使苦惱；n. 禍害；災害；瘟疫；鼠疫
example: The squirrels let the aliens know that mankind is a particularly nasty habitat-destroying plague.

definition: sounding sad and mournful; expressing suffering
chinese: 哀傷的；悲哀的；哀怨的
example: He accompanies his songs with plaintive chords played on a poor-quality zither.

definition: (of a sound) loud, resonant, and mournful; plaintive; reverberating
chinese: 哀婉的；淒切的；（聲音）響亮而迴盪的
example: The passage describes its subject as plangent, meaning loud and resounding.

definition: easily shaped or molded; easily influenced; relating to modeling or sculpture; relating to plastic surgery; artificial; a synthetic material; things made of it
chinese: adj. 可塑的；易受影響的；（藝術）造型的；整形的；虛假的；n. 塑膠；塑膠製品
example: She had a reaction to the anesthesia she was given prior to plastic surgery.

definition: an area of high, level ground; a state of little or no change after progress; to reach a stable level
chinese: n. 高原；平穩期；停滯期；v. 趨於平穩；進入停滯期
example: The panting breathless climbers were on the edge of the plateau.

definition: a remark that has been used too often to be interesting or thoughtful; a banal statement; banality
chinese: 陳腔濫調；老生常談；平庸
example: The audience wanted a concrete plan rather than another platitude.

definition: seeming reasonable or probable; believable; skilled at producing persuasive but possibly deceptive arguments
chinese: 似乎合理的；可信的；能言善辯的
example: What is plausible in a certain culture may not be plausible in another culture.

definition: fond of games and amusement; joking or teasing; lighthearted
chinese: 愛玩耍的；開玩笑的；嬉戲的；輕鬆幽默的
example: Nothing's more playful than a young cat, nor more grave than an old one.

definition: of or belonging to the common people; lacking refinement; coarse; a commoner
chinese: adj. 平民的；庶民的；粗俗的；n. 平民；庶民
example: His outlook on life, as with his habits were so stolid and plebeian.

definition: an abundance; the condition of being full or complete
chinese: 充足；豐富；大量；完全
example: "And while in plenitude of power he went, / and high in princely counsels waxed his fame, / I too could boast of credit and a noble name."

definition: a large or sufficient amount; abundance; prosperity; more than enough; fully; quite
chinese: n. 大量；充足；豐富；富足；adv. 十分；相當
example: Some have everything, others have plenty of time and some still see it all.

definition: an excessive amount; an overabundance; (medicine) an excess of blood
chinese: 過多；過剩；大量；（醫學）多血症
example: Mennad had a plethora of excuses not to live life.

definition: easily influenced or persuaded; docile; flexible; easily bent
chinese: 易受影響的；順從的；柔韌的；易彎曲的
example: With enough money, it's a simple matter to find and work the most pliable politicians.

definition: easily influenced; yielding; bending easily; supple
chinese: 順從的；易受影響的；易彎曲的；柔韌的
example: They hoped that a few more days of solitary confinement would make the prisoner more pliant.

definition: a dangerous, difficult, or unfortunate situation
chinese: 困境；苦境；窘境
example: The king was unsympathetic to the plight of the peasants, so he was unpopular.

definition: dull and monotonous; slow-moving and unexciting; walking heavily; working slowly but steadily; a slow heavy walk; laborious work
chinese: adj. 單調乏味的；沉悶的；步履沉重的；緩慢費力的；n. 沉重緩慢的步行；埋頭苦幹
example: The passage describes its subject as plodding, meaning the act of walking with a slow heavy gait.

definition: a cunning plan or action designed to gain an advantage; a maneuver; a trick
chinese: 策略；計謀；手段；花招
example: In this context, “ploy” refers to a maneuver in a game or conversation.

definition: spirited courage; determination in difficulty; to pick or pull off; to remove feathers from; to sound (a string) with the fingers; to tug
chinese: n. 勇氣；膽量；v. 摘；採；拔（毛）；撥（弦）；拉
example: One day she went out with the other village children to pluck strawberries.

definition: showing courage and determination in the face of difficulty or danger
chinese: 有膽量的；勇敢的；堅毅的
example: This plucky hero never backed down from danger.

definition: to examine deeply or explore; to measure depth; exactly vertical; utter, complete; completely; exactly
chinese: v. 探究；深入探測；adj. 垂直的；完全的；adv. 完全地；正好
example: That house was so poorly built that no floors were level and no walls were plumb.

definition: to fall or drop suddenly and steeply
chinese: 驟降；暴跌；垂直落下
example: Sales will surely plummet without this change.

definition: pleasantly rounded or chubby; to give full support to one choice; to make fuller; to sit or drop heavily
chinese: adj. 豐滿的；圓胖的；v. 堅決支持；使鼓起；重重坐下
example: The lady of the house is fashionably plump with a taste for gourmet chocolates.

definition: to steal goods by force, especially in war; goods taken by force; the act of plundering
chinese: v. 掠奪；搶劫；n. 戰利品；掠奪物；掠奪
example: Deeper into the eerie room the party went with hopes of gold and plunder.

definition: to fall suddenly; to throw or be thrown into a state or situation; to rush headlong; to immerse; a sudden fall; a dive
chinese: v. 驟降；陷入；猛衝；投入；n. 驟降；跳水
example: Mugabe's regime did not so much slide as plunge headlong into kleptocracy.

definition: richly luxurious and comfortable; a fabric with a long soft nap
chinese: adj. 豪華的；奢華舒適的；n. 長毛絨
example: After the calves are weaned they are moved to the plush river-flats for fattening.

definition: to hunt or fish illegally; to lure away staff or players from another; to take unfairly; to cook in simmering liquid
chinese: 盜獵；挖角；竊取；（烹飪）水煮
example: Why go through all that trouble to poach a gazelle?

definition: evoking a keen sense of sadness; deeply moving; keenly felt, intense; sharp or cutting
chinese: 令人感傷的；深刻動人的；強烈的；尖銳的
example: The eating of delicious food is one of the most intense and poignant pleasures of life.

definition: a stick or device used to point; a needle on a dial; a useful hint or tip; a hunting dog
chinese: 指示棒；指針；建議；提示；指示犬
example: Our geography teacher always enters the classroom with a map and a pointer.

definition: to divide into sharply opposing groups; (physics) to cause light waves to vibrate in one plane
chinese: 使兩極分化；使分裂對立；（物理）使偏振
example: Use of such divisive language tends to polarize the public.

definition: a strong verbal or written attack on a position; aggressive controversial argument; controversial
chinese: n. 激烈抨擊；論戰；爭論文章；adj. 爭論的
example: I find that this discussion takes place with too much polemic and not enough respect.

definition: of or involving strongly critical, controversial argument; disputatious
chinese: 論戰性的；抨擊性的；好辯的；引起爭議的
example: The author's polemical tone sometimes obscures the strength of her evidence.

definition: refined and elegant; cultured; accomplished and skillful; made shiny by rubbing
chinese: 精練的；優雅的；有教養的；純熟完美的；擦亮的
example: She's made an appointment with her dentist to have her teeth scraped and polished.

definition: prudent and wise; shrewd and tactful in dealing; artful or crafty
chinese: 明智的；審慎的；精明的；圓滑的；狡詐的
example: A certain convocation of politic worms are e'en at him.

definition: the activities of government; maneuvering for power within a group; political views; political science
chinese: 政治；（組織內）權力鬥爭；政見；政治學
example: office politics is often counterproductive

definition: unrealistically or naively optimistic
chinese: 盲目樂觀的；過分樂觀的；天真樂觀的
example: Even in the midst of a lousy sales quarter, Debbie remained Pollyannaish, never losing her shrill voice and wide smile, even when prospective customers hung up on her.

definition: a person of wide-ranging, encyclopedic learning
chinese: 博學者；通才
example: A polymath is someone who knows a whole lot about a whole lot.

definition: self-important and pretentious; (of language) excessively grand or ornate
chinese: 自大的；傲慢的；（言辭）浮誇的；華而不實的
example: Sedulously avoid all polysyllabic profundity, pompous prolixity, psittaceous vacuity, ventriloquial verbosity, and vaniloquent vapidity.

definition: to think about carefully and at length
chinese: 沉思；仔細考慮；琢磨
example: Don't ponder on it too long or someone else will buy it out from under you.

definition: capable of being weighed or appraised; worth considering
chinese: 可衡量的；可估量的；值得考慮的
example: The passage describes its subject as ponderable, meaning capable of being weighed or considered.

definition: heavy and clumsy; of great weight; (of style) dull and labored; slow and laborious
chinese: 笨重的；沉重的；（文體）沉悶冗長的；緩慢吃力的
example: Seals are clumsy and ponderous on land, but very graceful in the water.

definition: to speak or express opinions in a pompous, dogmatic way; the office or term of a pope
chinese: v. 自以為是地發言；武斷說教；n. 教宗任期
example: He likes to pontificate in his spare time.

definition: the people of a country or area as a whole; the common people
chinese: 民眾；大眾；平民；全體居民
example: Their inability to satisfy the desires of the populace led to their electoral defeat.

definition: to read or study attentively; to ponder; a tiny opening in skin or a surface
chinese: v. 仔細閱讀；鑽研；沉思；n. 毛孔；細孔
example: Experts will now pore over the fine print of the contract.

definition: full of tiny holes; letting liquid or air pass through; (of a border) easily crossed; full of gaps
chinese: 多孔的；可滲透的；（邊界）管控鬆散的；漏洞百出的
example: The countries have competing claims to villages and towns along the porous, undefined border.

definition: to be a sign or warning of, especially something momentous or bad
chinese: 預示；預兆；預告（不祥之事）
example: We now understand, the black birds in the painting portend the fate of the painter.

definition: ominous; of or like an omen; pompously solemn or self-important; marvelous, amazing
chinese: 不祥的；預兆的；裝腔作勢的；故作嚴肅的；驚人的
example: Of late, this portentous mansion has begun to give signs of dilapidation and decay.

definition: a person who behaves affectedly to impress others; an insincere person
chinese: 裝腔作勢的人；故作姿態者；虛偽的人
example: The books of this literary poseur were widely read but they are now forgotten.

definition: to put forward as a basis of argument; to assume as fact; to place or position
chinese: 假定；假設；提出（論點）；安置
example: The well-preserved bones led its early 20th-century excavators to posit that the site marked a burial ground created by a predecessor to early modern humans.

definition: occurring or awarded after death; published after the author's death; born after the father's death
chinese: 死後的；身後出版的；遺腹的
example: a posthumous award

definition: a note added after the signature of a letter; an additional remark or sequel
chinese: 附言；後記；補充說明
example: The postscript for good intentions is: next time.

definition: a candidate seeking admission to a religious order; an applicant
chinese: （宗教）修會候選人；申請入會者；申請人
example: In this context, “postulant” refers to one submitting a request or application especially one seeking admission into a religious order.

definition: to assume as true as a basis for reasoning; something assumed as a starting point; an axiom
chinese: v. 假定；假設；n. 假設；前提；（數學）公設
example: We need to postulate a completely different paradigm to explain all these phenomena.

definition: the position of the body; an attitude or stance; to behave in a way meant to impress or mislead; to pose
chinese: n. 姿勢；態度；立場；v. 故作姿態；裝模作樣；擺姿勢
example: A lot of back problems can be attributed to poor sitting posture.

definition: safe or suitable for drinking; a drink, especially an alcoholic one
chinese: adj. 可飲用的；n. 飲料；酒類
example: Make sure the campsite has access to potable water.

definition: having great power or effect; strong in effect; convincing; influential; sexually capable
chinese: 強有力的；效力強的；有說服力的；有權勢的；（男性）有性能力的
example: At high doses, fluoride is a potent poison that is almost on par with arsenic.

definition: a monarch or ruler, especially an autocratic one; a powerful person
chinese: 君主；統治者；有權勢者
example: In this context, “potentate” refers to a ruler who is unconstrained by law.

definition: existing in possibility; latent capacity for development; possibility; (physics) electric potential
chinese: adj. 潛在的；可能的；n. 潛力；可能性；（物理）電位
example: a potential problem

definition: to increase the power or effect of; to act synergistically with (a drug)
chinese: 增強；加強（藥效）；產生協同作用
example: In this context, “potentiate” means increase the effect of or act synergistically with (a drug or a physiological or biochemical phenomenon).

definition: a commotion or fuss; to worry or trouble
chinese: n. 騷動；喧擾；忙亂；v. 使煩惱；使不安
example: In this context, “pother” refers to make upset or troubled.

definition: to push out the lips to show displeasure; to sulk; a pouting expression
chinese: v. 噘嘴；生悶氣；n. 噘嘴；不悅
example: He has a tendency to pout even over little things.

definition: the state of being very poor; scarcity or lack; (of soil) infertility
chinese: 貧窮；貧困；缺乏；（土地）貧瘠
example: Abject poverty and lack of work has led people to go to extreme measures.

definition: having great power or force; influential; having a strong effect
chinese: 強大的；有權勢的；有力的；有影響力的；效力強的
example: the most powerful government in western Europe

definition: a meeting for discussion; a North American Indian ceremony or gathering; a medicine man; to confer
chinese: n. 會議；商議；（北美原住民）集會；巫醫；v. 商議
example: Before the team takes the field, the coach always calls for a powwow so that he can make sure all the players are mentally in the right place.

definition: a person engaged in a profession, especially medicine or law; a person who practices an activity
chinese: 從業者；執業者；執業醫師；實踐者
example: Becoming a family practitioner was far less stressful for the doctor and offered similar pay.

definition: dealing with things sensibly and practically; based on practical results; (linguistics) relating to pragmatics
chinese: 務實的；實用的；實用主義的；（語言學）語用的
example: I agree on an emotional level, but on the pragmatic level I disagree.

definition: to talk foolishly or at length; idle or foolish talk
chinese: v. 空談；喋喋不休；n. 空談；廢話
example: In this context, “prate” means idle or foolish and irrelevant talk.

definition: to deliver a sermon; to advocate earnestly; to give moral advice in a tiresome way
chinese: 傳道；鼓吹；宣揚；說教
example: The world is full of people who preach water and drink wine.

definition: a preliminary statement or introduction; the introductory part of a law or constitution; a preliminary event
chinese: 序言；開場白；前言；（法律）序文；前奏
example: I'll plunge into the matter without further preamble.

definition: not secure; dangerously likely to fall or collapse; uncertain; based on unwarranted assumptions
chinese: 不穩定的；岌岌可危的；危險的；（論點）缺乏根據的
example: The first-time precarious fisherman lazily fished dangerous poisonous fish, but soon stopped to shell peas.

definition: to come or go before in time, order, or position; to rank above
chinese: 先於；在前發生；走在前面；優先於
example: Stone tools precede bronze tools

definition: an earlier event or action used as an example or guide; a prior legal decision; preceding in time
chinese: n. 先例；前例；（法律）判例；adj. 先前的；在前的
example: It's totally without precedent for the suspect's attorney to be the true culprit.

definition: to cause to happen suddenly; to hasten; to throw into a state; to separate as a solid; done hastily or rashly; a solid deposit
chinese: v. 促成；加速；使陷入；（化學）使沉澱；adj. 倉促的；魯莽的；n. 沉澱物
example: A sudden decline in stock prices could precipitate a financial crisis.

definition: rain, snow, etc. falling; its amount; rash haste; (chemistry) the forming of a precipitate; the causing of an event
chinese: 降水；降水量；倉促；（化學）沉澱；促成
example: The areas with lowest precipitation are on the leeward side of the mountains.

definition: dangerously steep; (of a change) sudden and dramatic; done hastily; rash
chinese: 陡峭的；急遽的；倉促的；魯莽的
example: On the top of the precipitous shore, looking out to sea, was a large castle.

definition: to prevent from happening; to make impossible in advance; to rule out
chinese: 排除；阻止；使不可能；預先防止
example: That, of course, would effectively preclude the underlying tombs ever being investigated archaeologically.

definition: showing abilities earlier than usual; developing unusually early; (of plants) flowering early
chinese: 早熟的；過早發展的；（植物）早開花的
example: She's a precocious one eh?

definition: a person or thing that comes before another of the same kind; a forerunner; a sign; (chemistry) a precursor compound
chinese: 先驅；前身；先兆；（化學）前驅物
example: Domestic corn's wild precursor was teosinte.

definition: a person who held a position before another; a thing replaced by another
chinese: 前任；前輩；前身；先前的事物
example: He believes it to be an honor to follow in his predecessor's footsteps.

definition: to determine or decree beforehand; (theology) to foreordain by divine will
chinese: 預先注定；（神學）命定
example: In this context, “predestine” means decree or determine beforehand.

definition: a difficult, unpleasant, or embarrassing situation
chinese: 困境；窘境；尷尬處境
example: finds himself in a most awkward predicament

definition: to say in advance that something will happen
chinese: 預測；預言；預報
example: Some scientists predict that the world oil reserves will be used up within a century.

definition: a preference or special liking for something
chinese: 偏好；偏愛；癖好
example: She always had a predilection for round numbers.

definition: a tendency or inclination; susceptibility, especially to a disease; natural disposition
chinese: 傾向；癖性；（醫）易感性；素質
example: Hallucinogen use can trigger certain psychiatric conditions in people with a predisposition to them.

definition: present as the strongest or main element; having the most power; most common
chinese: 主要的；佔主導地位的；佔優勢的；最普遍的
example: Wallace says iron is still the predominant metal due to its populist appeal and its function as material for tooling and intricate art pieces.

definition: surpassing all others; of the highest rank or distinction
chinese: 卓越的；傑出的；首屈一指的
example: Monge stood preeminent above his contemporaries.

definition: to acquire before others; to forestall by acting first; to prevent in advance; to replace a scheduled program
chinese: 搶先佔有；先發制人；預先阻止；取代（原定節目）
example: The urgent announcement will preempt the scheduled lecture.

definition: to groom oneself with elaborate care; to congratulate oneself smugly; (of a bird) to clean its feathers with its beak
chinese: 精心打扮；沾沾自喜；（鳥）以喙理羽
example: A duck will preen its feathers many times over the course of the day.

definition: an introduction to a book; a preliminary statement; to provide with a preface; to introduce or begin with
chinese: n. 序言；前言；開場白；v. 為書作序；以……為開端
example: A book without a preface is like a body without a soul.

definition: to be an early sign of; to foreshadow; to imagine beforehand
chinese: 預示；成為……的先兆；預想
example: In this context, “prefigure” means imagine or consider beforehand.

definition: full of meaning or significance; filled with; carrying a developing fetus
chinese: 意味深長的；含意豐富的；充滿的；懷孕的
example: Gustavo has to go to the ranch and take care of a pregnant cow.

definition: coming before and preparing for something more important; a preparatory action; a preliminary round
chinese: adj. 初步的；預備的；n. 準備工作；預賽；初步措施
example: a preliminary investigation

definition: to think out or plan beforehand, especially a crime
chinese: 預謀；預先策劃；預先考慮
example: Investigators sought evidence that the defendant had time to premeditate the act.

definition: of superior quality; a payment for insurance; an amount above the usual price; an extra charge; a bonus
chinese: adj. 高級的；優質的；n. 保險費；溢價；附加費；獎金
example: I received a premium six-piece cheese knife set as a birthday gift.

definition: giving warning of something to come; (medicine) indicating the onset of disease
chinese: 預兆的；預先警告的；（醫）前驅的
example: Sometimes I have premonitory dreams.

definition: the state of being absorbed in thought; extreme concern; a matter that dominates one's mind
chinese: 全神貫注；過度關注；縈繞心頭之事
example: Don't open your mouth, and your physiognomy demonstrates a preoccupation.

definition: absorbed in thought; worried; already occupied
chinese: 全神貫注的；心事重重的；被佔據的
example: The values of a society totally preoccupied with making money are not altogether reassuring.

definition: to make ready in advance; to make mentally ready; to make or cook (food, a potion, a medicine)
chinese: 準備；籌備；使有心理準備；調製；製備（藥劑）
example: Then the witch placed her cauldron on the fire, to prepare the magic draught.

definition: superior in power, influence, number, or importance
chinese: 佔優勢的；佔主導的；更重要的
example: The passage describes its subject as preponderant, meaning having superior power and influence.

definition: to be greater in number, power, or importance; to weigh more heavily
chinese: 佔優勢；勝過；（重量）超過
example: In this context, “preponderate” means weigh more heavily.

definition: creating a favorable impression; attractive or appealing
chinese: 給人好感的；有魅力的；討人喜歡的
example: The passage describes its subject as prepossessing, meaning creating a favorable impression.

definition: contrary to reason or common sense; utterly absurd
chinese: 荒謬的；可笑的；違反常理的
example: His story is too preposterous to be a lie.

definition: something required beforehand; a course required before another; required as a prior condition
chinese: n. 先決條件；前提；先修課程；adj. 必備的；先決的
example: The basic prerequisite for every progress is the conviction that the necessary is possible.

definition: an exclusive right or privilege; the special power of a sovereign
chinese: 特權；特有權利；（君主）大權
example: It's your prerogative to decide whether to go on the trip.

definition: to be a sign or warning of; to foretell; an omen; a feeling of foreboding
chinese: v. 預示；預言；n. 預兆；預感
example: In this context, “presage” refers to a foreboding about what is about to happen.

definition: knowledge of events before they happen; foresight
chinese: 先見之明；預知
example: In this context, “prescience” refers to the power to foresee the future.

definition: having or showing knowledge of events before they occur
chinese: 有先見之明的；預知的
example: extraordinarily prescient memoranda on the probable course of postwar relations

definition: a doctor's written order for medicine; the medicine prescribed; a rule or recommendation; (law) acquisition of rights by long use
chinese: 處方；處方藥；規定；指示；（法律）時效取得
example: Can you get that medicine over the counter or do you need a prescription?

definition: to keep in its original state; to maintain; to protect; to treat food to prevent decay; an exclusive domain; a reserve; jam
chinese: v. 保存；維持；保護；醃製；n. 專屬領域；保護區；果醬
example: preserve the peace in the family

definition: the elected head of a republic; the head of a company, college, or society
chinese: 總統；總裁；董事長；（大學）校長；會長
example: a President is elected every four years

definition: requiring urgent action; insistent; the act of pressing; a record or object made by pressing
chinese: adj. 緊迫的；迫切的；堅持的；n. 壓製；壓製品
example: too pressing to permit of longer delay

definition: widespread respect and admiration based on achievement or quality
chinese: 聲望；威望；名望
example: Power and prestige can play an important role in the spread of a language.

definition: to suppose to be true without proof; to take the liberty of doing; to be overconfident; (law) to presume legally
chinese: 假定；推測；擅自；冒昧；（法律）推定
example: Woe to those who presume that they are destined to ‘enlighten’ others, not themselves!

definition: failing to observe proper limits; overstepping one's place; arrogantly overconfident
chinese: 冒昧的；放肆的；自以為是的；傲慢的
example: It would be presumptuous to call myself his replacement, but I could offer some guidance.

definition: to assume beforehand; to require as a precondition
chinese: 預先假定；以……為前提；預設
example: I presuppose that you have done your work

definition: the act of pretending; a false show; a pretext; affectation; an exaggerated claim to importance
chinese: 假裝；偽裝；藉口；矯飾；自命不凡
example: He made a pretense of knowing my father.

definition: claiming undeserved importance or distinction; affected; showy or ostentatious
chinese: 自命不凡的；矯揉造作的；炫耀的；浮華的
example: a pretentious country house

definition: beyond what is normal or natural; extraordinary; supernatural
chinese: 超乎尋常的；異常的；超自然的
example: The passage describes its subject as preternatural, meaning surpassing the ordinary or normal.

definition: to be widespread or current; to prove superior; to win; to persuade (prevail on)
chinese: 盛行；普遍存在；勝過；佔上風；說服
example: In this world, rules of conduct prevail that differ from what is accepted in public life.

definition: widespread in a particular area or time; commonly occurring or accepted
chinese: 普遍的；盛行的；流行的
example: Regardless of whether this test is valid or not, it is very prevalent.

definition: to speak or act evasively; to avoid the truth; to lie
chinese: 支吾其詞；推諉；搪塞；撒謊
example: Bobby learned not to prevaricate when his teacher asked him where his homework was; by giving a straightforward answer, he would avoid invoking the teacher’s wrath.

definition: to keep from happening; to stop someone from doing something
chinese: 防止；預防；阻止；妨礙
example: They confirmed the importance of strengthening global precautions in order to prevent devastating losses.

definition: existing or occurring before a war
chinese: 戰前的
example: prewar levels of industrial production

definition: easily irritated; touchy; tricky to deal with; covered with prickles; causing a stinging feeling
chinese: 易怒的；難相處的；棘手的；多刺的；刺痛的
example: Orangutans have been observed using sticks to pry nutritious seeds from prickly plants.

definition: a self-righteously moralistic person who behaves as if superior to others
chinese: 自命清高的人；一本正經的人；道學先生
example: If you often think of yourself as a saint, you may simply be a prig.

definition: self-righteously moralistic; exaggeratedly proper
chinese: 自命清高的；一本正經的；拘泥形式的
example: The passage describes its subject as priggish, meaning exaggeratedly proper.

definition: the state of being first in importance or rank; the office of an archbishop
chinese: 首要地位；首位；卓越；（宗教）首席主教職位
example: Tensions grew when the laity questioned the primacy of the clergy in moral decision-making.

definition: relating to early ages; instinctive and basic; original; fundamental; primary
chinese: 原始的；本能的；最初的；根本的；首要的
example: Some politicians try to evoke the primal fear of everything foreign.

definition: of first importance; direct and firsthand; elementary; earliest; a preliminary election; a primary color
chinese: adj. 主要的；首要的；第一手的；初級的；最初的；n. （政治）初選；原色
example: primary goals

definition: of the earliest ages of the world; ancient and original; instinctive
chinese: 遠古的；原始的；太古的；本能的
example: You went back to the camp leaving me alone in the primeval forest.

definition: belonging to an early stage of development; simple and crude; unsophisticated; basic
chinese: 原始的；早期的；簡陋的；粗糙的；基本的
example: The sentence was primitive, scraping its knuckles on the floor and grunting with heavy threats.

definition: existing from the beginning of time; earliest; fundamental
chinese: 原始的；最初的；太初的；根本的
example: Our biological ancestors thrived in the primordial soup hundreds of millions of years ago.

definition: to groom or dress with elaborate care
chinese: 精心打扮；刻意修飾
example: In this context, “primp” means dress or groom with elaborate care.

definition: something regarded as more important; the right to precede others; precedence in time
chinese: 優先事項；優先；優先權；（時間）在先
example: Not being able to decide what the priority should be is the biggest problem.

definition: in its original condition; unspoiled; pure; clean and new as if unused
chinese: 原始的；未受汙染的；純淨的；嶄新的；完好如新的
example: The article of clothing was in pristine condition, with not a stain nor spot.

definition: a state of extreme poverty; lack of basic necessities; loss or absence
chinese: 貧困；匱乏；缺乏必需品；喪失
example: In this context, “privation” refers to a state of extreme poverty.

definition: sharing secret knowledge of (privy to); private; hidden; an outdoor toilet
chinese: adj. 參與機密的；知情的；私人的；隱蔽的；n. 茅廁
example: a privy place to rest and think

definition: to investigate thoroughly; to explore physically; a thorough investigation; an unmanned exploratory craft; a slender instrument
chinese: v. 探究；深入調查；探測；n. 調查；探測器；探針
example: Under the moon's layer of ice, a submarine probe scooted through the water ocean.

definition: the quality of having strong moral principles; honesty and integrity
chinese: 正直；誠實；廉潔
example: The defense attorneys cast aspersions on the probity of the witness.

definition: to continue or go on; to carry out; to move forward; to arise from; (law) to start legal action
chinese: 繼續進行；進行；前進；源自；（法律）起訴
example: Tea is like the lubricating oil of work to allow it to proceed smoothly.

definition: to announce officially or publicly; to declare; to show clearly
chinese: 宣告；宣布；公開聲明；顯示；表明
example: To save the world requires faith and courage: faith in reason, and courage to proclaim what reason shows to be true.

definition: a natural tendency or inclination, often toward something undesirable
chinese: 傾向；癖性；偏好
example: You have a proclivity for getting yourself into difficult situations.

definition: to delay or postpone action, especially habitually
chinese: 拖延；耽擱；延宕
example: I like to procrastinate, then binge work, even though it isn't healthy.

definition: to obtain, especially with effort; to purchase; to bring about; to obtain someone for prostitution
chinese: 取得；獲得；採購；促成；拉皮條
example: This decision was a self-serving measure designed to procure immunity from prosecution.

definition: to urge or stir into action; to poke; an act of urging; a poke; a pointed stick
chinese: v. 督促；激勵；戳；n. 督促；戳刺；刺棒
example: No matter how much I prod her, she refuses to start working on the assignment.

definition: recklessly wasteful; lavish or generous; abundant; a spendthrift; a returning wanderer
chinese: adj. 揮霍的；浪費的；慷慨的；豐富的；n. 揮霍者；浪子
example: The chariest maid is prodigal enough if she unmask her beauty to the moon.

definition: remarkably great in size or degree; causing amazement; extraordinary
chinese: 巨大的；驚人的；了不起的；非凡的
example: Chess players with prodigious memories perform incredible feats, such as playing blindly, at the same time, a large number of matches.

definition: a young person with exceptional talent; an amazing or unusual thing
chinese: 神童；奇才；奇蹟；非凡事物
example: she is a chess prodigy

definition: irreverent toward God or sacred things; vulgar or obscene; secular; to treat with irreverence; to desecrate
chinese: adj. 褻瀆的；不敬的；粗俗的；世俗的；v. 褻瀆；玷汙
example: The most profane word and the rudest letter are the best, they're more educated than silence.

definition: to claim, often falsely; to declare openly; to affirm faith in a religion; to practice as a profession
chinese: 聲稱；自稱；公開宣稱；信奉（宗教）；以……為業
example: I do profess to be no less than I seem.

definition: to hold out or offer for acceptance
chinese: 提供；提出；奉上
example: Good sir, we would like to proffer this wonderful item for your consideration.

definition: competent or skilled in doing or using something
chinese: 熟練的；精通的；擅長的
example: You won't become proficient if you only study the things you enjoy.

definition: recklessly extravagant or wasteful; dissolute; a wasteful or dissolute person
chinese: adj. 揮霍的；肆意浪費的；放蕩的；n. 揮霍者；浪蕩子
example: City were profligate in front of goal, wasting chance after chance.

definition: showing great insight; very great or intense; far-reaching; having deep knowledge; difficult to understand
chinese: 深刻的；深遠的；極大的；淵博的；深奧的
example: the differences are profound

definition: produced or existing in great abundance; extravagant or lavish
chinese: 大量的；豐富的；毫不吝惜的；過分慷慨的
example: Maite halted the profuse hemorrhage by pressing down on the wound with both hands.

definition: an abundance or large quantity; lavish extravagance
chinese: 大量；豐富；繁多；浪費
example: There's a profusion of rhododendron in her garden, blooming in a variety of colours.

definition: a forecast of the likely course of events; (medicine) the likely outcome of a disease
chinese: 預測；（醫）預後；預斷
example: Marcus was spot on in his prognosis, as the results before us now show.

definition: to foretell or predict; to be a sign of
chinese: 預言；預測；預示
example: The mayor refused to prognosticate as to his margin of victory in the election.

definition: (of a price) so high as to prevent purchase or use; excessive; forbidding or restricting something
chinese: （價格）高得令人卻步的；過高的；禁止的；抑制性的
example: I must admit that lately living in the city has become almost prohibitive.

definition: to estimate from current trends; to cast an image; to present oneself in a certain way; to stick out; a planned undertaking or scheme
chinese: v. 預測；預計；投射；展現（形象）；突出；n. 計畫；專案；工程
example: Without a feasibility study, it makes no sense to even think about beginning the project.

definition: to increase rapidly in number; to spread; (biology) to reproduce rapidly
chinese: 激增；擴散；迅速蔓延；（生物）增殖
example: Small errors can proliferate when copied from one report to another.

definition: producing much work or many results; plentiful; producing many offspring
chinese: 多產的；豐富的；繁殖力強的；大量的
example: a prolific writer

definition: using too many words; tediously lengthy
chinese: 冗長的；囉嗦的；嘮叨的
example: The manual was so prolix that I still haven't understood how it works.

definition: an introductory section of a literary or dramatic work; an event leading to another
chinese: 序言；開場白；序幕；前奏
example: Victor's editor insisted that he cut out the prologue from his novel draft.

definition: to extend the duration of; to make longer
chinese: 延長；拖延；延續
example: If we don’t make it, we shall need to prolong the time frame.

definition: easily noticed; important or famous; projecting from a surface
chinese: 顯著的；突出的；著名的；傑出的；凸出的
example: The repeated triplets are the most prominent motif in that movement of the symphony.

definition: to proclaim a law or decree officially; to make widely known; to promote an idea
chinese: 頒布（法令）；公布；宣揚；傳播
example: They are simply trying to promulgate an accurate version of the facts.

definition: strongly marked; easily noticeable; decided or definite; spoken or declared (past of pronounce)
chinese: adj. 明顯的；顯著的；斷然的；v. 發音；宣布
example: Many words are pronounced according to the spelling, but some are not.

definition: to read a text and mark errors for correction
chinese: 校對；校稿
example: With oral language there isn't only one language and one can't proofread.

definition: biased information spread to promote a political cause or point of view; materials used for this
chinese: （政治）宣傳；宣傳活動；宣傳品
example: Your making propaganda seems to indicate that you care greatly what other people think.

definition: to spread an idea widely; to breed or grow new plants; to multiply; (physics) to transmit
chinese: 傳播；宣傳；繁殖；增殖；（物理）傳導
example: Ziri used some rooting hormone to help his ivy propagate in the garden.

definition: to drive or push forward; to spur into action or a situation
chinese: 推進；推動；驅使；促使
example: Going all out like this is going to propel me right into an all-or-nothing struggle.

definition: a natural inclination or tendency
chinese: 傾向；癖好；習性
example: From a very young age, he showed his propensity for studying.

definition: accurately predicting the future; of or like a prophet
chinese: 預言的；預示的；有先見之明的；先知的
example: However, it would be nice if it doesn't become a prophetic dream.

definition: intended to prevent disease or harm; a preventive medicine or measure; a condom
chinese: adj. 預防性的；預防疾病的；n. 預防藥；保險套
example: In some cases, mastectomy is prophylactic surgery - a preventive measure taken by those considered to be at high risk of breast cancer.

definition: to win or regain the favor of; to appease or placate; to make offerings to appease a god
chinese: 安撫；撫慰；討好；（祭祀）求神息怒
example: The two sons, plying their angry father with cheesy neckties for Christmas, were hardly able to propitiate him – the father already had a drawer full of ones he had never worn before or ever planned to.

definition: favorable; giving a good chance of success; auspicious; favorably disposed
chinese: 有利的；吉利的；適宜的；（神靈）慈悲的
example: We await a propitious time to act.

definition: a person who advocates or supports a cause or proposal; one who proposes
chinese: 支持者；擁護者；提倡者；提議者
example: A proponent of passivism, he tended to let events unfold as fate willed.

definition: owned and controlled exclusively, as under a patent or trademark; privately owned; of an owner; possessive
chinese: 專有的；專利的；私有的；業主的；以主人自居的
example: I've come here today to talk about the dangers of proprietary software.

definition: conformity to accepted standards of behavior; appropriateness; correctness; the details of proper conduct
chinese: 得體；適當；正當；禮節；規矩
example: The way tourists dress offends the local standard of propriety.

definition: lacking poetic beauty; dull and unimaginative; commonplace; having the style of prose
chinese: 平淡無奇的；乏味的；平凡的；散文的
example: Unlike the talented artists in his workshop, Paul had no such bent for the visual medium, so when it was time for him to make a stained glass painting, he ended up with a prosaic mosaic.

definition: to forbid, especially by law; to denounce or condemn; to banish or outlaw
chinese: 禁止；排斥；放逐；剝奪法律保護
example: The church does not proscribe monarchy and prescribe democracy, or proscribe democracy and prescribe monarchy.

definition: ordinary written or spoken language without metrical structure; a writer's style; dull, commonplace expression
chinese: 散文；文筆；平淡乏味的話語
example: Her prose is full of needlessly florid, cliched descriptions, securing her career as a romance novelist.

definition: the institution of legal proceedings against someone; the prosecuting party; the carrying out of a plan or course of action
chinese: 起訴；控訴；（法律）檢方；實行；執行
example: This decision was a self-serving measure designed to procure immunity from prosecution.

definition: a person who has converted to a new religion or opinion, especially to Judaism
chinese: 新皈依者；改變信仰者；皈依猶太教的人
example: The same law shall be to him that is born in the land, and to the proselyte that sojourneth with you.

definition: to try to convert to one's religion; to advocate one's beliefs or views insistently; to recruit
chinese: 勸人改變信仰；傳教；宣揚（觀點）；拉攏
example: The problem is that professors use their classrooms as political soap boxes to proselytize their views.

definition: the likelihood of a future event; outlook; an extensive view; a potential customer; to search for minerals; to explore
chinese: n. 可能性；前景；展望；景色；潛在客戶；v. 勘探；探查
example: No peril daunts her, no prospect of fatigue or discomfort disheartens or repels her.

definition: successful and flourishing, especially financially; wealthy; thriving
chinese: 繁榮的；興旺的；富裕的；成功的
example: The inherent difficulty of quantifying prosperity complicates the question of which countries are most prosperous.

definition: lying face down; overcome with exhaustion or distress; helpless; to throw oneself flat; to reduce to extreme weakness; to subdue
chinese: adj. 俯臥的；拜倒的；衰竭的；一蹶不振的；v. 使俯伏；使衰竭；使屈服
example: The bride is prostrate while the tambourine is in full swing.

definition: the leading character in a story or play; a main figure in a contest or cause; an advocate
chinese: 主角；主人翁；主要人物；倡導者；擁護者
example: In the action movie, the protagonist had to confront a bloodthirsty and merciless adversary.

definition: readily taking many forms; changeable; versatile
chinese: 多變的；變化多端的；多才多藝的；能扮演多種角色的
example: Peter Sellers was truly a protean actor—in Doctor Strangelove he played three very different roles: a jingoist general, a sedate President and a deranged scientist.

definition: to keep safe from harm or injury; to shield; to safeguard
chinese: 保護；防護；保障；保衛
example: The study of biology can help us better understand and protect the natural world.

definition: rules of official etiquette; a code of correct procedure; an international agreement; a plan for a scientific study; rules for data exchange
chinese: 禮節；（外交）禮儀；規程；協定；（研究）試驗方案；（電腦）通訊協定
example: Some investigators deal with protocol violations by excluding the participants from the analysis.

definition: an original model on which later versions are based; a first example; a typical example
chinese: 原型；雛形；樣品；典範
example: The prototype for the hero of the book was the son of the writer.

definition: to prolong in time or space; to drag out
chinese: 延長；拖延；使拖長
example: Further procedural disputes could protract the negotiations for months.

definition: to stick out from a surface; to thrust forward
chinese: 突出；伸出；使凸出
example: In this type of break, the bone will actually protrude from the skin.

definition: bulging or swelling out; projecting
chinese: 凸出的；隆起的；鼓起的
example: The kleptomaniac struggled with the protuberant loot.

definition: to demonstrate the truth of; to turn out to be; to test; (of dough) to rise
chinese: 證明；證實；結果是；顯示為；試驗；（麵糰）發酵
example: These dirty clothes could be a new piece of evidence to prove his innocence.

definition: the place of origin or source; the history of ownership of a work of art or antique
chinese: 出處；來源；起源；（文物）來歷
example: Who knows if they remember their provenance.

definition: a short well-known saying stating a general truth or piece of advice
chinese: 諺語；格言；箴言
example: A proverb says that one has no friends and no enemies, only teachers.

definition: referred to in a proverb or idiom; of or like a proverb; well known, notorious
chinese: 俗話說的；諺語的；眾所周知的；出了名的
example: he kicked the proverbial bucket

definition: providing carefully for the future; prudent; frugal
chinese: 有遠見的；未雨綢繆的；節儉的
example: The passage describes its subject as provident, meaning providing carefully for the future.

definition: happening at a favorable time; lucky; resulting from divine providence
chinese: 幸運的；適時的；天意的；神助的
example: A providential change in the weather allowed the rescue to proceed.

definition: an area of knowledge, activity, or responsibility; a principal administrative division of a country; regions outside the capital; an ecclesiastical district
chinese: 領域；職權範圍；省；外地；（宗教）教省
example: It was historic center of the province and remains an important transportation crossroad.

definition: narrow-minded and unsophisticated; of a province; regional; a person from the provinces
chinese: adj. 狹隘的；見識淺薄的；土氣的；省的；地方的；n. 外地人；鄉下人
example: Each commission has representatives at the zonal, provincial and district levels.

definition: arranged for the present, possibly to be changed later; temporary
chinese: 暫定的；臨時的；暫時的
example: I set up a kind of provisional office in my assistant editors' room.

definition: subject to a proviso; conditional; provisional or temporary
chinese: 有附帶條件的；附但書的；臨時的；暫定的
example: The passage describes its subject as provisory, meaning subject to a proviso.

definition: causing anger or annoyance deliberately; stimulating thought or discussion; controversial; sexually arousing

definition: exceptional skill or expertise; bravery in battle
chinese: 高超技藝；本領；英勇；勇猛

definition: to move about stealthily, as in search of prey or loot; to roam; an act of prowling

definition: nearness in space, time, or relationship

chinese: 過分拘謹的人；假正經的人；（性方面）保守古板者

definition: acting with care and thought for the future; wise and judicious; careful with money
chinese: 審慎的；謹慎的；明智的；節儉的

definition: excessively concerned with propriety or modesty, especially regarding sex
chinese: 過分拘謹的；假正經的；（性方面）古板的

definition: to trim a plant by cutting branches; to cut away the unnecessary; to reduce; a dried plum

definition: a fictitious name, especially one used by an author
chinese: 假名；筆名；化名

definition: playful in a mischievous way
chinese: 淘氣的；頑皮的；惡作劇的

definition: childishly silly; immature; of a child
chinese: 幼稚的；不成熟的；孩子氣的；兒童的

definition: eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight; combative
chinese: 好鬥的；好戰的；愛爭吵的

definition: great power or influence; might; (show jumping) a high-wall jumping competition
chinese: 權勢；力量；威力；（馬術）高障礙賽

definition: having great power or influence; mighty
chinese: 強有力的；強大的；有權勢的
example: The passage describes its subject as puissant, meaning powerful.

definition: physical beauty, especially of a woman
chinese: 美貌；美麗；（尤指女性）姿色
example: In this context, “pulchritude” refers to physical beauty (especially of a woman).

definition: to reduce to fine powder or dust; to defeat utterly; to demolish
chinese: 粉碎；磨成粉；徹底擊敗；摧毀
example: In this context, “pulverize” means make into a powder by breaking up or cause to become dust.

definition: showing great attention to detail or correct behavior; strictly observant of etiquette
chinese: 一絲不苟的；拘泥細節的；嚴守禮節的

definition: happening or arriving at the appointed time; habitually on time; (mathematics) of a point
chinese: 準時的；守時的；嚴守時刻的；（數學）點的

definition: to pierce with a sharp point; to deflate (an illusion or pride); a small hole made by piercing; a flat tire; a medical piercing procedure
chinese: v. 刺穿；刺破；打破（幻想）；挫傷；n. 刺孔；（輪胎）破洞；（醫）穿刺

definition: an expert who frequently gives opinions to the public; a commentator; a learned Hindu scholar
chinese: 專家；權威人士；評論家；（印度）學者

definition: having a sharply strong taste or smell; (of remarks) biting and caustic; sharp and to the point
chinese: 辛辣的；刺鼻的；尖刻的；犀利的；一針見血的
example: Wasabi is a pungent plant that is difficult to cultivate.

definition: small and weak; feeble; poor in quality or amount; trivial
chinese: 弱小的；孱弱的；微小的；微不足道的
example: He is too puny to be a soldier.

definition: to remove contaminants from; to refine or concentrate; to make pure; to cleanse of sin
chinese: 淨化；提純；精煉；使純潔；（宗教）滌罪
example: purify the water

definition: the outskirts or adjacent area of a place; a place one frequents; one's own haunt or territory
chinese: 鄰近地區；周邊；郊區；常去之處；（個人）活動範圍

definition: to steal, often in a petty way
chinese: 偷竊；竊取；盜用

definition: to claim or profess, often falsely; to appear to be; the general meaning or substance; intention
chinese: v. 聲稱；自稱；看似；n. 主旨；大意；意圖

chinese: 供應；提供（食品等）；販賣；散布（資訊）

definition: a person easily persuaded or taken advantage of; an opponent easily defeated; something easily done
chinese: 易被說服的人；好欺負的人；軟柿子；輕而易舉的事

definition: showing a contemptible lack of courage or resolution; timid
chinese: 膽小的；懦弱的；畏首畏尾的
example: The general condemned the retreat as a pusillanimous response to a manageable risk.

definition: generally considered or reputed to be; supposed or assumed
chinese: 推定的；假定的；公認的；所謂的

definition: (of a victory) won at too great a cost to be worthwhile; an ancient Greek war dance; a metrical foot of two unstressed syllables
chinese: adj. 代價慘重的；得不償失的；n. （古希臘）出征舞；（詩律）抑抑格

definition: an unqualified person who pretends to have medical skill; a charlatan; the cry of a duck; fraudulent; to make a duck's cry
chinese: n. 庸醫；江湖郎中；騙子；鴨叫聲；adj. 冒牌的；v. （鴨）呱呱叫

definition: to drink heartily or deeply; a hearty drink or draft
chinese: v. 大口喝；痛飲；n. 一大口（酒）；痛飲

definition: an awkward, complex, or hazardous situation; a soft boggy area of land
chinese: 困境；泥淖；泥沼；沼澤地
example: The rain turned the road into a quagmire.

definition: to feel or show fear; to cower; a small game bird
chinese: v. 畏縮；膽怯；退縮；n. 鵪鶉
example: Janos talked about different ways of cooking quail.

definition: to limit or modify a statement; to make or become eligible or competent; (grammar) to modify a word
chinese: 限定；修正（說法）；使具資格；具備資格；（文法）修飾
example: The first statement shows my unqualified love for San Francisco. In the second statement I qualify, or limit, my love for San Francisco.

definition: an uneasy feeling of doubt or worry, especially about one's conduct; a scruple; a sudden feeling of sickness
chinese: 疑慮；良心不安；顧忌；一陣噁心
example: He did not have any qualm of conscience.

definition: a state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do; a dilemma
chinese: 進退兩難；困境；窘境；困惑
example: We're in a quandary because we have two excellent candidates.

definition: a state or period of isolation to prevent spread of disease; to isolate; to cut off
chinese: n. 隔離；檢疫；隔離期；v. 隔離；使孤立
example: Students in quarantine are keeping up with their assignments online and continuing their internships remotely.

definition: to have an angry argument; to disagree; to object to (quarrel with); an angry argument; a reason for disagreement
chinese: v. 爭吵；爭論；挑剔；n. 爭吵；不和；異議

definition: to put an end to; to suppress forcibly; (law) to annul or reject as invalid
chinese: 平息；鎮壓；撲滅；（法律）撤銷；駁回

definition: strange or odd; suspicious; relating to LGBTQ identity; a person who is LGBTQ; to spoil or ruin
chinese: adj. 古怪的；異常的；可疑的；酷兒的；n. 酷兒；同性戀者；v. 破壞；搞砸

definition: to put an end to (a rebellion or disorder) by force; to suppress or subdue a feeling such as fear or anger
chinese: 鎮壓；平息；消除（恐懼等）；抑制
example: He ought to go to anger management classes to quell his explosive anger.

definition: to satisfy (thirst); to put out (a fire); to suppress or extinguish a desire; to cool hot metal rapidly
chinese: 解（渴）；熄滅；平息（慾望等）；（金屬）淬火
example: Water will quench your thirst quicker than any other drink when you're feeling thirsty.

definition: complaining in a whining or petulant way; peevish
chinese: 愛抱怨的；發牢騷的；易怒的

definition: to argue or raise objections about a trivial matter; a minor objection or criticism; an evasion
chinese: v. 吹毛求疵；為小事爭論；n. 小異議；遁詞

definition: in a state of inactivity or dormancy; quiet and at rest
chinese: 靜止的；休眠的；沉寂的；不活躍的

definition: death or release from life; something that ends or settles a matter; discharge of a debt
chinese: 死亡；解脫；終結；（債務）清償

definition: the most perfect example of a quality or class; the essential part of something; the fifth element of ancient philosophy
chinese: 典範；精髓；精華；（古代哲學）第五元素

definition: representing the most perfect or typical example of a class or quality
chinese: 典型的；精髓的；最具代表性的

definition: having peculiar or unexpected traits; unconventional
chinese: 古怪的；奇特的；別具一格的

definition: exceedingly idealistic and impractical
chinese: 不切實際的；空想的；唐吉訶德式的

definition: a fixed share or limited quantity that is officially allowed or required
chinese: 配額；限額；定額

definition: ordinary or commonplace; occurring every day
chinese: 平凡的；日常的；每日的

definition: a disorderly crowd; a mob; the common people (contemptuous)
chinese: 烏合之眾；暴民；下層民眾

definition: fanatical or extreme in opinion; affected with rabies
chinese: 狂熱的；極端的；患狂犬病的

definition: slightly indecent or risqué; lively and spirited; having a strong distinctive flavor
chinese: 猥褻的；有點色情的；生動活潑的；（味道）濃郁的

definition: unconventional and slightly disreputable in an attractive way; vulgar or flashy
chinese: 放蕩不羈的；俗麗的；不入流的

definition: a large number or amount; a flat floating structure of logs or an inflatable boat; to travel by raft
chinese: n. 大量；一大批；筏；救生筏；v. 乘筏

definition: violent uncontrollable anger; a widespread fad; to feel or show violent anger; (of a storm or conflict) to continue violently

definition: old and torn; wearing torn clothes; having an uneven or jagged edge; exhausted
chinese: 破舊的；衣衫襤褸的；參差不齊的；凹凸不平的；疲憊的

definition: to complain or protest strongly and bitterly; a bar forming part of a fence; a track for trains; railway transport
chinese: v. 怒斥；抱怨；猛烈抨擊；n. 欄杆；扶手；鐵軌；鐵路

definition: dissolute or immoral, like a rake; dashing and jaunty in appearance; set at a jaunty angle
chinese: 放蕩的；浪蕩的；瀟灑時髦的；（帽子）歪戴的
example: A tricorn trimmed with gold lace was set at a rakish angle over a wig of white curls that dropped down to his waist.

definition: to talk or write at length in a wandering, unfocused way; to walk for pleasure; (of a plant) to grow in a straggling way; a leisurely walk
chinese: v. 漫談；東拉西扯；離題冗談；漫步；（植物）蔓生；n. 漫步；散步

definition: lengthy and confused or wandering; spreading out irregularly; (of a plant) climbing; aimless talk; walking for pleasure
chinese: adj. 散漫的；冗長而離題的；（建築）布局雜亂的；（植物）蔓生的；n. 閒談；漫步
example: Sarah gets very bored listening to her grandparents rambling on about old times.

definition: uncontrollably exuberant; boisterous and noisy
chinese: 喧鬧的；精力旺盛而難管束的；狂暴的
example: The child continues to be rambunctious.

definition: a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or event; a branching or offshoot
chinese: （衍生的）後果；影響；分支

definition: spreading or flourishing unchecked; (of plants) growing luxuriantly; (heraldry) rearing on the hind legs

definition: in a state of severe disrepair and likely to collapse; loosely or carelessly organized

definition: bitter, deep-seated resentment or ill will
chinese: 積怨；深仇；怨恨

definition: made or happening without method, pattern, or conscious choice
chinese: 隨機的；任意的；無規律的

definition: the ordinary members of an organization as opposed to its leaders; the enlisted soldiers of an army
chinese: 普通成員；基層；（軍隊）士兵
example: the strike was supported by the union rank and file

definition: to cause lasting annoyance or bitterness; to irritate persistently
chinese: 使怨恨難消；使耿耿於懷；激怒

definition: to speak or shout at length in an angry, impassioned way; a long, angry, impassioned speech
chinese: v. 激昂地叫嚷；大聲抱怨；n. 激昂冗長的言論；怒斥
example: I had to listen to that nitwit's nonsensical rant for hours; it was unbearable.

definition: aggressively greedy or grasping; given to plunder; (of animals) predatory
chinese: 貪婪的；掠奪成性的；（動物）捕食其他動物的
example: Ukrainians don't deserve to be invaded by a rapacious army.

definition: to force someone to have sex against their will; to plunder or despoil; the act of rape; destruction or spoliation; a plant grown for its oil-rich seed
chinese: v. 強暴；掠奪；破壞；n. 強暴；掠奪；（植物）油菜
example: In this context, “rape” refers to Eurasian plant cultivated for its seed and as a forage crop.

definition: happening in a short time or at great speed; (usually rapids) a fast-flowing, turbulent part of a river
chinese: adj. 迅速的；快速的；急促的；n. 急流；湍灘

definition: a close and harmonious relationship of mutual understanding
chinese: 融洽關係；和諧；默契
example: The new teacher developed a rapport with the pupils straight away.

definition: the establishment or resumption of harmonious relations, especially between states
chinese: （國家間）恢復友好關係；和解；修好
example: This should push the two nations toward diplomatic rapprochement.

definition: a mischievous person; a rascal or scoundrel
chinese: 淘氣鬼；無賴；流氓
example: My pet mouse is a rapscallion; she keeps escaping from her cage!

definition: completely fascinated or absorbed; filled with intense delight
chinese: 全神貫注的；專心的；著迷的；狂喜的
example: I can see them over there paying rapt attention to every word that comes out of my mouth.

definition: to make thinner or less dense; to make more refined or purified
chinese: 使稀薄；使純化；使精煉
example: In this context, “rarefy” means lessen the density or solidity of.

definition: (of air) of lower density; esoteric or lofty; exclusive and remote from ordinary life
chinese: 稀薄的；高深的；曲高和寡的；脫離大眾的
example: The passage describes its subject as rarified, meaning having low density.

definition: acting hastily without considering consequences; reckless; an area of red spots on the skin; a series of many unpleasant things in a short time
chinese: adj. 輕率的；魯莽的；n. 疹子；（一連串）大量
example: More often, the rash appears in large folds of the skin and is very itchy.

definition: harsh and grating in sound; hoarse; rough
chinese: （聲音）刺耳的；沙啞的；粗糙的
example: Ziri heard a strange raspy voice outside his tent.

definition: to sign or give formal consent to a treaty or agreement, making it officially valid
chinese: （正式）批准；認可；使生效
example: A majority of two thirds is required to ratify an overture.

definition: the process of exact, methodical, logical thinking
chinese: 推理；推論；推理過程
example: It has been said that the principal utility of abstraction is as an instrument in ratiocination.

definition: to allow each person only a fixed amount of something; to use sparingly; a fixed amount allowed to each person; food provisions
chinese: v. 配給；定量供應；節約使用；n. 配給量；定量；口糧
