definition: based on reason or logic; able to think clearly and sensibly; (math) expressible as a ratio of integers
chinese: 理性的；合理的；（數學）有理的
example: Any irrational number can be approximated by a rational number with arbitrarily large precision.

definition: a set of reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief
chinese: 理由；根本原因；基本原理

definition: to praise enthusiastically; to talk wildly or incoherently; a highly enthusiastic review; a large all-night dance party
chinese: v. 熱烈讚揚；激賞；胡言亂語；怒吼；n. 熱烈讚揚；銳舞派對

definition: to tangle or complicate; to unravel or fray; to disentangle
chinese: 糾纏；使複雜化；拆散；解開
example: In this context, “ravel” means French composer and exponent of Impressionism (1875-1937).

definition: extremely hungry; voracious; intensely eager for gratification
chinese: 極度飢餓的；貪婪的；狼吞虎嚥的
example: Livestock overgrazing can lead to outbreaks of ravenous locusts, according to a new study.

definition: to fill with intense delight; to seize and carry off by force; to rape
chinese: 使陶醉；使狂喜；強暴；強奪
example: In this context, “ravish” means force (someone) to have sex against their will.

definition: delightful; entrancing; extremely beautiful
chinese: 令人陶醉的；極其美麗的；迷人的
example: a ravishing blonde

definition: a feeling of delight and enchantment; the act of seizing by force; rape
chinese: 陶醉；狂喜；強奪；強暴
example: In this context, “ravishment” refers to a feeling of delight at being filled with wonder and enchantment.

definition: to completely destroy a building or town; to tear down to the ground
chinese: 徹底摧毀；將…夷為平地

definition: completely destroyed or torn down to ground level
chinese: 被夷為平地的；被徹底摧毀的

definition: opposing political or social progress or reform; a person who holds such views
chinese: adj. 反動的；極端保守的；反對變革的；n. 反動分子；保守派
example: Idealism has always been and remains a philosophy serving the conservative and reactionary classes.

definition: (usually reams) a large quantity, especially of writing; 500 sheets of paper; to rebuke severely; to widen a hole
chinese: n. 大量；令（紙張單位）；v. 嚴厲斥責；擴孔
example: She got us exactly one ream of printer paper, which in our office will last about five hours.

definition: to say or do something to remove someone's doubts or fears; to restore confidence
chinese: 使安心；使放心；打消疑慮
example: It’s tough to reassure you when jealousy has such a grip.

definition: resisting authority or control; showing a desire to defy convention; engaged in rebellion
chinese: 叛逆的；反抗的；難控制的；造反的
example: temperamentally rebellious

definition: to reject an offer or friendly approach abruptly or ungraciously; to repel; an abrupt rejection
chinese: v. 斷然拒絕；冷落；擊退；n. 斷然拒絕；冷落
example: Annoyed at the churlish rebuff, I turned my back and walked home.

definition: to express sharp disapproval or criticism of; a sharp expression of disapproval
chinese: v. 指責；斥責；非難；n. 斥責；指責
example: He took it for an implied rebuke.

definition: to claim or prove that an argument or accusation is false; to refute
chinese: 反駁；駁斥；提出反證
example: You'll have three minutes to rebut the argument of the opposing side.

definition: stubbornly resisting authority or control; uncooperative; a recalcitrant person
chinese: adj. 頑抗的；桀驁不馴的；不服從的；n. 頑抗者
example: The passage describes its subject as recalcitrant, meaning marked by stubborn resistance to authority.

definition: to formally withdraw or renounce a statement, opinion, or belief
chinese: 公開撤回（聲明）；放棄（信仰或主張）；改口
example: The witness refused to recant her earlier statement.

definition: to summarize and restate the main points of; (biology) to repeat evolutionary stages in development
chinese: 概括；扼要重述；（生物）重演
example: I asked my colleague to recapitulate everything that was said in a few words.

definition: to be given or sent something; to accept; to greet or welcome guests; to experience or undergo; to respond to in a specified way
chinese: 收到；接到；接受；接待；遭受；（反應）受到
example: receive payment

definition: willing to consider or accept new ideas or suggestions; quick to receive impressions
chinese: 樂於接受的；能接納的；感受性強的
example: receptive to reason and the logic of facts

definition: (of genes) expressed only when inherited from both parents; tending to recede
chinese: （遺傳）隱性的；後退的；退行的
example: The passage describes its subject as recessive, meaning (of genes) producing its characteristic phenotype only when its allele is identical.

definition: to relapse into crime or bad behavior
chinese: 重犯；故態復萌；舊病復發
example: In this context, “recidivate” means go back to bad behavior.

definition: the tendency of a convicted criminal to reoffend; relapse into previous behavior
chinese: 再犯；累犯；故態復萌
example: The amount will go up in the case of recidivism.

definition: a convicted criminal who reoffends repeatedly; relating to repeat offending
chinese: n. 慣犯；累犯；adj. 累犯的；慣犯的
example: In this context, “recidivist” refers to someone who is repeatedly arrested for criminal behavior (especially for the same criminal behavior).

definition: to respond to a gesture or action with a corresponding one; to give in return; (of a part) to move backward and forward
chinese: 回報；報答；互換；（機械）往復運動
example: He doesn't reciprocate my feelings.

definition: the practice of exchanging things with others for mutual benefit; a relation of mutual dependence or influence
chinese: 互惠；相互性；互惠關係
example: The demand for reciprocity in love doesn't come from love, but from vanity.

definition: to repeat aloud from memory; to state or list a series of facts
chinese: 背誦；朗誦；列舉；詳述
example: Every student must learn a poem and recite it in front of the class.

definition: heedless of danger or consequences; rash
chinese: 魯莽的；不計後果的；輕率的
example: A quick flick through the data shows that there was reckless spending.

definition: to retrieve or recover something; to make land usable; to recover material from waste; to reform a person
chinese: 收回；取回；開墾；回收再利用；感化
example: After weeks of planning, he was ready to reclaim his mobility once again.

definition: a person who lives in seclusion and avoids others; solitary and withdrawn
chinese: n. 隱士；離群索居者；adj. 隱居的；遁世的
example: Johnson is a recluse; he prefers to isolate himself from the rest of the students in our class.

definition: avoiding the company of others; solitary
chinese: 隱遁的；隱居的；離群索居的
example: lived an unsocial reclusive life

definition: to identify from previous encounters; to acknowledge the existence, validity, or legality of; to show official appreciation of
chinese: 認出；認可；承認；（正式）承認；賞識；表彰
example: He is fat and bloated; those who do not know him cannot recognize him.

definition: to suddenly spring back in fear or disgust; to rebound; (of a gun) to move back when fired; the backward kick of a gun
chinese: v. 退縮；畏縮；彈回；（槍砲）後座；n. 後座力；畏縮
example: This is a great rifle to snipe with, if you can handle the recoil.

definition: to make compatible or consistent; to restore friendly relations between; to make someone accept something unwelcome
chinese: 調和；使一致；使和解；使順從（某情況）
example: It's best not to try to reconcile the contradictions.

definition: little known; abstruse; difficult to understand
chinese: 深奧的；難解的；晦澀的
example: The theories of relativity can seem recondite even for people who are well versed in the sciences.

definition: military observation of an area to gain information; preliminary exploration or survey
chinese: 偵察；勘察；勘查
example: an exchange of fire occurred on a reconnaissance mission

definition: to make a military observation of a region; to explore in order to gain information
chinese: 偵察；勘察；探查
example: In this context, “reconnoiter” means explore, often with the goal of finding something or somebody.

definition: to build up again or reorganize; to restore dried food to its original state by adding water
chinese: 重組；重建；（加水）使還原
example: After years of inactivity, the club decided to reconstitute its leadership committee.

definition: to break out again after a dormant period; to recur
chinese: 復發；再發作；再爆發
example: In this context, “recrudesce” means happen.

definition: a four-sided plane figure with four right angles
chinese: 長方形；矩形
example: A square is always a rectangle, but a rectangle is not always a square.

definition: morally correct behavior or thinking; integrity
chinese: 正直；誠實；公正
example: You're hardly a model of moral rectitude.

definition: lying down, especially in a position of comfort or rest; reclining
chinese: 躺著的；斜靠的；橫臥的
example: The passage describes its subject as recumbent, meaning lying down; in a position of comfort or rest.

definition: to recover from illness or exertion; to regain something lost
chinese: 恢復健康；康復；復原；挽回（損失）
example: Mennad needs at least a weak to recuperate from that trip.

definition: promoting or relating to recovery of health or strength
chinese: 有助康復的；恢復的；有恢復力的
example: recuperative powers

definition: to compensate for faults; to save from sin or error; to regain possession by payment; to fulfill a promise; to exchange a coupon for goods
chinese: 彌補；挽回（聲譽）；救贖；贖回；兌現（承諾）；兌換
example: The only thing that will redeem mankind is co-operation.

definition: strongly suggestive of something; strongly smelling of something; fragrant
chinese: 令人聯想到…的；散發…氣味的；芳香的
example: The dinner was served in two huge tin-plated vessels, whence rose a strong steam redolent of rancid fat.

definition: formidable, especially as an opponent; worthy of respect
chinese: 令人敬畏的；可怕的；值得尊敬的
example: She was politely described as a redoubtable dowager.

definition: not needed; superfluous; (of a component) included as a backup; (British) dismissed from a job as no longer needed
chinese: 多餘的；冗贅的；（電腦）備援的；（英）被裁員的
example: Just as he was starting to get the hang of things, he was made redundant.

definition: to stagger or lurch; to feel shocked or bewildered; to feel giddy; to wind on a reel; a cylinder for winding film, thread, or line
chinese: v. 搖晃；蹣跚；震驚；眩暈；捲（線）；n. 捲軸；（影片）一盤
example: The films shown in this modest cinema had an intermission during which the projectionist changed the reel.

definition: an official who enforces rules in a game; a person who settles disputes; a reviewer of academic work; a person who provides a reference; to act as referee
chinese: n. 裁判；仲裁者；審稿人；推薦人；v. 擔任裁判；審查（論文）
example: The commentator began yelling when the referee gave the defender a second yellow card.

definition: to improve by making small changes; to make more precise or elegant; to remove impurities from
chinese: 改進；使精確；完善；提煉；精煉
example: Journalists are people who believe that you can refine an announcement if you call it a report.

definition: to show or embody; to throw back light, heat, or sound; to think deeply; to bring credit or discredit on
chinese: 反映；表明；反射；深思；（對名聲）帶來影響
example: Snow is white because its molecules reflect all the colors of the sun's rays.

definition: thoughtful and contemplative; characteristic of something; reflecting light
chinese: 沉思的；反映…的；反光的；反射的
example: The tyre wall is coated with a reflective material to provide extra visibility in the dark.

definition: to make light or sound waves change direction when entering a different medium
chinese: 使折射
example: refract a light beam

definition: stubbornly resistant to authority or control; (of a disease) not responsive to treatment; (of a material) heat-resistant
chinese: 倔強的；難駕馭的；（疾病）難治的；耐高溫的；難熔的
example: Owing to the refractory nature of alumina it is with difficulty that it can be diffused in alkaline silicates, borates, or lead silicates.

definition: to stop oneself from doing something; a repeated chorus or line in a song or poem; a frequently repeated comment
chinese: v. 克制；抑制；避免；n. 副歌；疊句；老調
example: He could not refrain from smiling, though with a slight sense of guilt.

definition: pleasingly new or different; restoring energy; cooling and invigorating
chinese: 令人耳目一新的；提神的；清爽的
example: When you're wanting to have a drink, there's nothing as refreshing as drinking water.

definition: a person forced to leave their country to escape war, persecution, or disaster
chinese: 難民；流亡者
example: Words alone cannot convey the untold misery endured by people in these refugee camps.

definition: shining very brightly; radiant
chinese: 燦爛的；光輝的；耀眼的
example: The refulgent dome was visible from across the valley.

definition: able to be proved false or wrong
chinese: 可反駁的；可駁倒的；可證偽的
example: A scientific claim must be refutable by contrary evidence.

definition: to prove a statement or argument to be wrong; to deny
chinese: 駁斥；反駁；證明…錯誤；否認
example: It is much harder to refute a lie than to tell one.

definition: to regrow tissue; to bring new life or energy to; to reform spiritually; reborn or renewed
chinese: v. 再生；使復興；使重生；革新；adj. 重生的；新生的
example: I was surprised to learn that a stingray can actually regenerate its stinger if it gets broken off.

definition: a government, especially an authoritarian one; a system or ordered way of doing things; a regimen
chinese: 政權；政體；體制；（養生）方案
example: The regime maintained a notional parliament whose votes were written before the sessions began.

definition: a prescribed course of diet, exercise, or medical treatment; (archaic) government or rule
chinese: 養生法；（飲食或運動）規劃；療程；（古）統治
example: He's encouraged to maintain a strict eating regimen.

definition: relating to a regiment
chinese: （軍隊）團的；屬於團的
example: regimental units

definition: to return to a former or less developed state; the action of regressing
chinese: v. 退步；倒退；退化；n. 倒退；退化
example: It is quite clear that they are going to make us regress.

definition: to control by rules or regulations; to adjust the rate, amount, or degree of
chinese: 管制；規範；調節；調整
example: regulate the temperature

definition: to restore someone's reputation or standing; to restore to health through therapy; to help a former prisoner readapt to society; to restore a building to good condition
chinese: 恢復名譽；使康復；使重返社會；修復（建築等）
example: In this context, “rehabilitate” means help to readapt, as to a former state of health or good repute.

definition: to reuse old ideas or material without significant change; to go over again; a reuse of old material
chinese: v. 老調重彈；重複；換湯不換藥地改寫；n. 重複；舊調重彈
example: I don't want to rehash all that stuff from the past.

definition: a practice performance in preparation for a public one; a recounting of things already said
chinese: 排練；彩排；預演；複述
example: Tomorrow there will be no normal lessons, in view of the athletic meet rehearsal.

definition: the period during which a monarch rules; dominance; to rule as monarch; to prevail or be predominant
chinese: n. 統治期；統治；支配；v. 統治；盛行；占優勢
example: Under the reign of tyranny, innocent people were deprived of their citizenship.

definition: (often reins) a means of control or restraint; a strap used to guide a horse; to check or restrain
chinese: n. 控制；約束；韁繩；v. 控制；約束；勒住（馬）
example: Being a teacher, you must learn to keep a tight rein on your emotions.

definition: to say something again or repeatedly, usually for emphasis
chinese: 重申；反覆說；重複
example: Ziri had to reiterate his original terms.

definition: to refuse to accept, believe, or agree to; (of the body) to fail to accept a transplant; a substandard item; a person rejected
chinese: v. 拒絕；駁回；排斥；（身體）排斥（器官）；n. 不合格品；被拒絕者
example: I reject the idea of starting a war

definition: to feel or show great joy or delight
chinese: 欣喜；歡欣鼓舞；高興
example: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

definition: to make look or feel younger or more vigorous; to revitalize; (geology) to renew the erosive power of a stream
chinese: 使年輕；使恢復活力；使振興；（地質）使（河流）回春
example: Exploring new activities can rejuvenate your spirit.

definition: to fall back into a former bad state or habit; to suffer a recurrence of illness; a recurrence or deterioration after improvement
chinese: v. 故態復萌；舊病復發；再犯；n. 復發；故態復萌
example: Many survivors report joint pain and vision problems, and experts also are worried about the risk of relapse.

definition: oppressively constant and unremitting; harsh and inflexible; persistent
chinese: 無情的；持續不斷的；堅持不懈的
example: Rodrigo felt isolated and anxious due to the relentless online bullying he encountered.

definition: closely connected or appropriate to the matter at hand
chinese: 相關的；有關的；切題的
example: Moreover, they underscored the need for providing policy relevant ready-to-use scientific results and methodology.

definition: belief in and worship of a superhuman power; a particular system of faith; a pursuit followed with great devotion
chinese: 宗教；信仰；（奉為信條的）嗜好
example: Every religion, like every person, has brought good and bad things into the world.

definition: to voluntarily give up a right, power, or possession; to let go of
chinese: 放棄；讓出（權力或職位）；鬆手放開
example: They will relinquish power and dismantle the single-party state.

definition: to enjoy greatly; to look forward to; great enjoyment; a condiment of chopped pickled vegetables
chinese: v. 享受；喜愛；期待；n. 喜好；樂趣；（調味）佐料
example: Thousand island dressing can be made of mayonnaise, ketchup, and sweet pickle relish.

definition: unwilling and hesitant
chinese: 不情願的；勉強的
example: He was reluctant to get involved in the argument and chose to remain neutral.

definition: to continue to be in a state; to stay in a place; to be left over; (remains) what is left, such as ruins or a corpse
chinese: v. 保持；仍然是；留下；剩餘；n. 遺跡；遺體
example: He was reluctant to get involved in the argument and chose to remain neutral.

definition: worthy of attention; extraordinary or striking
chinese: 非凡的；引人注目的；顯著的
example: a remarkable sight

definition: a means of counteracting something undesirable; a treatment or medicine; legal redress; to set right or cure
chinese: n. 補救方法；療法；藥物；（法律）救濟；v. 補救；矯正；治療
example: remedy these deficiencies

definition: a thing that causes someone to remember something; a message reminding someone of something
chinese: 提醒物；令人回想的事物；提示；催單
example: The empty chair at the dinner table was a constant reminder of his absence.

definition: to indulge in enjoyable recollection of past events
chinese: 追憶；緬懷往事；回憶
example: Combat soldiers during peaceful moments like to reminisce of their halcyon days.

definition: tending to remind one of something; suggestive of; nostalgic
chinese: 令人聯想起…的；懷舊的；回憶往事的
example: What's complicated about their language is the writing, not the grammar, which is reminiscent of a creole.

definition: lacking care or attention to duty; negligent
chinese: 疏忽的；怠忽職守的；不負責任的
example: Remiss in his duty to keep the school functioning efficiently, the principle was relieved of his position after only three months.

definition: a temporary decrease in the severity of a disease; reduction of a prison sentence; forgiveness of sins; cancellation of a debt
chinese: （病情）緩解；減輕；減刑；赦免；豁免
example: his cancer is in remission

definition: a small remaining quantity or part; a surviving trace; a leftover piece of cloth
chinese: 殘餘；遺跡；剩餘物；零頭布
example: A remnant of the old army is supporting and perhaps leading the current chaos.

definition: a forcefully reproachful protest
chinese: 抗議；諫言；規勸；抱怨
example: Despite the residents' remonstrance, the council approved the project.

definition: to make a forcefully reproachful protest; to argue in opposition
chinese: 抗議；諫諍；規勸；據理力爭
example: I remonstrate with my boss about my performance evaluation.

definition: deep regret or guilt for a wrong committed
chinese: 懊悔；悔恨；自責
example: Narcissists exhibit a lack of remorse or guilt for their hurtful actions towards others.

definition: to pay someone for services rendered or work done
chinese: 給予報酬；酬謝；補償
example: There are labours which no salary can remunerate, services which no fees can requite.

definition: a revival of interest in something; (the Renaissance) the revival of European art and learning in the 14th to 16th centuries
chinese: 復興；再生；（大寫）文藝復興（時期）
example: Renaissance comedies are staged in the town square.

definition: to tear into pieces; to split apart; to cause emotional pain to
chinese: 撕裂；扯開；使分裂；（心）使痛苦
example: But where was he to go, in order to escape the relentless monster that sought to rend him?

definition: a person who deserts a cause, party, or religion; having betrayed a principle or group
chinese: n. 叛徒；變節者；背教者；adj. 叛變的；變節的
example: Tracing a renegade's family background, you'll find him the black sheep.

definition: to go back on a promise or agreement; to fail to fulfill an obligation; (cards) to revoke
chinese: 食言；違約；背棄（承諾）；（牌戲）藏牌違規
example: In this context, “renege” means fail to fulfill a promise or obligation.

definition: to formally give up a claim, right, or possession; to refuse to recognize any longer; to abandon a belief or habit
chinese: （正式）放棄；宣布斷絕關係；拒絕承認；摒棄
example: I renounce everything as long as I can be with you.

definition: to restore something old to good condition by repairing and remodeling
chinese: 翻新；整修；修復
example: Kalman decided to renovate the house to make it look like a log cabin.

definition: conversation or speech marked by quick, witty replies; skill in making such replies
chinese: 機智的應答；妙語反擊；鬥嘴
example: In this context, “repartee” refers to adroitness and cleverness in reply.

definition: to send someone back to their own country; to bring money or profits back to one's own country; a person who has returned to their country of origin
chinese: v. 遣返；（資金）匯回；n. 被遣返者；歸國者
example: In this context, “repatriate” means a person who has returned to the country of origin or whose citizenship has been restored.

definition: to revoke or annul a law or act; the act of revoking a law
chinese: v. 撤銷；廢除（法律等）；n. 撤銷；廢除
example: I think they should repeal that law.

definition: to say or do again; to recite; an action or event that repeats; a rebroadcast
chinese: v. 重複；重做；複述；n. 重複；重播
example: Algeria has learned the lesson and is determined not to repeat the same mistakes.

definition: to drive or force back; to keep away; to cause disgust in; to resist mixing with or penetration by
chinese: 驅除；擊退；使反感；使厭惡；排斥
example: Marigolds repel nematodes, as well as some humans who don't like the way they smell.

definition: expressing or feeling sincere regret for wrongdoing
chinese: 悔過的；懺悔的；後悔的
example: The passage describes its subject as repentant, meaning feeling or expressing remorse for misdeeds.

definition: an unintended consequence of an event or action, especially an unwelcome one; an echo or recoil
chinese: （間接的）影響；後果；反響；回聲
example: Medical experts say the only possible negative repercussion of using laboratory-produced elastin to repair tissue, is that it could cause inflammation or calcification.

definition: a stock of plays, songs, or pieces a performer is prepared to perform; the whole body of skills or techniques a person has
chinese: 全部劇目；全部曲目；全部技能
example: It's important for every musician to ensure there is variety in their repertoire.

definition: characterized by tedious repetition
chinese: 重複乏味的；反覆的；嘮叨的
example: The passage describes its subject as repetitious, meaning characterized by repetition.

definition: to feel or express discontent; to fret; to yearn for something
chinese: 抱怨；不滿；渴望
example: In this context, “repine” means express discontent.

definition: to take the place of; to substitute for something broken or lost; to put back in a previous position
chinese: 取代；替換；更換；放回原處
example: It is difficult to replace an employee that is as qualified as he is.

definition: to fill something up again; to restore a stock or supply
chinese: 補充；重新填滿；補足
example: The creatures emerged to replenish their ranks by kidnapping children and turning them into creatures like them.

definition: filled or well supplied with something; very full of food
chinese: 充滿的；充足的；飽食的
example: The annals of sports are replete with the names of great black athletes.

definition: to make an exact copy of; to repeat a study or experiment to obtain consistent results; (of genetic material) to reproduce itself
chinese: 複製；重複（實驗並得到相同結果）；（細胞）自我複製
example: No one was able to replicate the results of that study.

definition: a state of rest, peace, or calm; composure; to lie down or rest; to place trust in
chinese: n. 寧靜；安寧；休息；沉著；v. 休息；躺；寄託（信任）
example: At times also they would repose side by side under a goatskin.

definition: a place where things are stored; a rich source of information; a person entrusted with secrets
chinese: 儲藏處；寶庫；知識庫；（軟體）儲存庫；知己
example: In computer science, a software repository is a website where software can be uploaded.

definition: to reprimand or express strong disapproval of
chinese: 斥責；指責；譴責
example: In this context, “reprehend” means express strong disapproval of.

definition: deserving censure or condemnation
chinese: 應受譴責的；不可原諒的
example: It's reprehensible to exploit a person's gullibility.

definition: to restrain or prevent the expression of a feeling; to subdue by force; to keep a thought out of conscious awareness
chinese: 壓抑；抑制；鎮壓
example: The report also discusses actions by governments and other groups to repress the news media.

definition: a temporary relief from harm or discomfort; the postponement or cancellation of a punishment; to grant a reprieve to
chinese: n. 暫時緩解；緩刑；暫緩執行；v. 緩刑；暫緩；使暫時解脫
example: I'm happy to hear that grandma is doing better, even though the doctors say it's just reprieve.

definition: to rebuke someone formally; a formal expression of disapproval
chinese: v. 斥責；懲戒；n. 申斥；懲戒
example: No one likes to reprimand students for poor behavior, but it comes with the territory when you're a teacher.

definition: to express disapproval or disappointment to; criticism; a source of discredit or disgrace
chinese: v. 責備；指責；n. 責備；恥辱
example: Don't reproach him; he has mental health problems.

definition: an unprincipled person; morally depraved; unprincipled
chinese: n. 墮落者；無賴；adj. 墮落的；放蕩的；道德敗壞的
example: The town's reprobate element gathered nightly in the dim corner of the tavern.

definition: an expression of blame or disapproval
chinese: 責備；譴責；斥責
example: He who loves instruction loves knowledge, but whoever hates reproof is an ignoramus.

definition: to reprimand or censure, often gently
chinese: 責備；指責；訓斥
example: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.

definition: a cold-blooded vertebrate such as a snake, lizard, turtle, or crocodile; a contemptible person
chinese: 爬行動物；爬蟲類；卑鄙的人
example: Australian paleontologists have discovered a new species of a prehistoric flying reptile.

definition: to refuse to accept or recognize as valid; to deny the truth of; to disown; to refuse to pay a debt
chinese: 拒絕承認；否認；駁斥；與…斷絕關係；拒絕履行（債務）
example: In this context, “repudiate” means refuse to acknowledge, ratify, or recognize as valid.

definition: intense distaste or aversion; inconsistency between ideas
chinese: 強烈反感；厭惡；矛盾；牴觸
example: I cannot overcome my repugnance to eating snails.

definition: extremely distasteful; unacceptable; incompatible with
chinese: 令人厭惡的；令人反感的；不相容的
example: Those views are outmoded and repugnant.

definition: to drive back an attack; to rebuff; to cause disgust in; the act of repelling or rebuffing
chinese: v. 擊退；拒絕；使厭惡；n. 擊退；拒絕
example: His work adds long descriptions of rotting corpses to nauseate and repulse.

definition: the beliefs or opinions generally held about someone or something; high esteem
chinese: 名聲；名譽；聲望
example: He's a financial analyst with a pretty good reputation for his analysis of economic trends.

definition: the opinion generally held of someone or something; good reputation; to be generally regarded as
chinese: n. 名聲；聲譽；好名聲；v. 被認為；被稱為
example: In this context, “repute” refers to the state of being held in high esteem and honor.

definition: a Mass for the repose of the souls of the dead; a musical composition for such a Mass; a lament or tribute
chinese: 安魂曲；安魂彌撒；輓歌；悼念
example: In this context, “requiem” refers to a musical setting for a Mass celebrating the dead.

definition: made necessary by circumstances or rules; a thing that is necessary for a purpose
chinese: adj. 必需的；必要的；必備的；n. 必需品；必要條件
example: The car had the requisite tail fins that you would expect from that era.

definition: to make appropriate return for a favor or service; to retaliate for an injury; to return love or affection
chinese: 回報；報答；報復；回應（愛意）
example: There are labours which no salary can remunerate, services which no fees can requite.

definition: to revoke, cancel, or repeal a law, order, or agreement
chinese: 廢除；撤銷；取消
example: He wants to rescind it.

definition: to look like or be similar to
chinese: 像；類似；與…相似
example: All happy families resemble each other, each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

definition: to feel bitterness or indignation at
chinese: 憎恨；怨恨；對…感到憤慨
example: I resent your implication that I am engaged to you only because of your money.

definition: slow to reveal emotion or opinions; restrained; kept for a particular person or purpose
chinese: 拘謹的；寡言的；矜持的；預訂的；保留的
example: He was the opposite of his brother in almost every respect, being unusually shy and reserved.

definition: remaining after the greater part has gone; a quantity left over; (statistics) the difference between observed and predicted values
chinese: adj. 殘餘的；剩餘的；殘留的；n. 殘餘；（統計）殘差
example: Large residual stomach contents may lead to loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting.

definition: a small amount of something that remains after the main part has gone; the part of an estate left after debts and bequests
chinese: 殘留物；殘渣；剩餘；（遺產）剩餘部分
example: Always run hot water after using the sink to clear away any soap residue.

definition: to voluntarily leave a job or office; to give up a right or claim; to accept something undesirable as inevitable
chinese: 辭職；放棄（權利等）；聽任；使順從（於）
example: There is widespread conviction that the prince should resign his claim to the throne.

definition: the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; the ability of a material to spring back into shape
chinese: 韌性；復原力；適應力；彈性
example: Algeria's journey since gaining independence has been one of resilience, progress, and cultural richness.

definition: to withstand the action or effect of; to struggle against; to refrain from despite temptation; a protective coating
chinese: v. 抵抗；抗拒；忍住；耐（腐蝕等）；n. （印刷）防染劑
example: He who walks the straight and narrow path must resist temptations of all sorts.

definition: admirably purposeful, determined, and unwavering
chinese: 堅決的；果斷的；堅定的
example: Undeterred by obstacles, he remained resolute in his pursuit of a new chapter in life.

definition: (of sound) deep, clear, and continuing to sound; evoking images or emotions; producing resonance
chinese: 洪亮的；回響的；引起共鳴的；能喚起聯想的
example: Our group played guitars while the others randomly hit resonant objects.

definition: to evoke a feeling of shared emotion or belief; to produce or be filled with a deep, reverberating sound
chinese: 引起共鳴；產生共鳴；回響；共振
example: Not everyone will resonate with your story; that's just how it is.

definition: having the ability to find quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties
chinese: 足智多謀的；善於應變的；機智的
example: I doubt he will make it, he is not very resourceful.

definition: a feeling of admiration or deference; a particular aspect or point; to admire deeply; to comply with
chinese: n. 尊敬；尊重；方面；v. 尊敬；尊重；遵守
example: I respect his judgement

definition: a short period of rest or relief from something difficult; a delay granted
chinese: 暫緩；喘息；暫時的休息；延期
example: The cool water of the swimming hole was a refreshing respite from the hot summer sun.

definition: attractive and impressive through being richly colorful or sumptuous
chinese: 燦爛的；華麗的；輝煌的
example: Leave while you are resplendent.

definition: reacting quickly and positively; responding readily to treatment or influence; (of a website) adapting to screen size
chinese: 反應迅速的；有回應的；敏感的；（網頁）響應式的
example: These patients were not responsive to other therapies and had experienced several recurrences of their disease.

definition: the restoration of something lost or stolen to its owner; compensation for injury or loss; return to an original state
chinese: 歸還；賠償；補償；恢復原狀
example: In this context, “restitution” refers to the act of restoring something to its original state.

definition: unable to keep still or silent, especially due to boredom or dissatisfaction; resistant to control
chinese: 焦躁不安的；不受管束的；（馬）不聽駕馭的
example: The crowd grew restive as the comedian’s opening jokes fell flat.

definition: unable to rest or relax because of anxiety or boredom; without rest or sleep
chinese: 焦躁不安的；坐立不安的；靜不下來的；無法安眠的
example: The fear of sleeping alone often leads to restless nights and disrupted sleep patterns.

definition: having the ability to restore health, strength, or well-being; a medicine or drink that restores health
chinese: adj. 恢復健康的；滋補的；有恢復力的；n. 補藥；恢復劑
example: She felt stronger and full of life, as if she just woke up from a restorative rest.

definition: to prevent from doing something; to keep under control or within limits
chinese: 抑制；遏制；約束；限制
example: Before the horse race begins, the jockeys grip the reins tightly to restrain the impatient horses.

definition: to rise again
chinese: 再起；復甦；復活
example: In this context, “resurge” means rise again.

definition: an increase or revival after a period of little activity or popularity
chinese: 復甦；復興；再起
example: We see a resurgence of the wildlife.

definition: to restore a dead person to life; to revive the practice or use of
chinese: 使復活；使重新流行；重新起用
example: Let's go back and resurrect that old idea.

definition: to revive from unconsciousness or apparent death; to restore vigor to
chinese: 使復甦；使恢復知覺；使復興
example: Ziri tried to resuscitate his father.

definition: a servant or follower of a noble; a fee paid in advance to secure services; a dental appliance that holds teeth in position
chinese: 家臣；侍從；聘用訂金；（牙科）維持器
example: They met at the estate of the shogun's retainer to play a game of cards.

definition: to make an attack in return for a similar attack; to pay back an injury
chinese: 報復；反擊；以牙還牙
example: Ziri said he will retaliate tomorrow.

definition: to delay or hold back the development or progress of; (offensive) a person with an intellectual disability
chinese: v. 延緩；阻礙；妨礙；n. （侮辱性）弱智者
example: The way you talk about her, she sounds like a half-retard.

definition: (of memory) able to retain facts and impressions; able to retain or hold
chinese: 記憶力強的；保持的；有保持力的
example: With deliberate malice I loaded a prolix narrative with every triviality that a fairly retentive memory could rake out of the half-forgotten past.

definition: not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; reserved; inclined to be silent
chinese: 沉默寡言的；有所保留的；含蓄的
example: He is reticent and he never speaks unless spoken to.

definition: tending to avoid company; shy; about to retire from a job
chinese: 靦腆的；不愛交際的；即將退休的
example: Nelson was always the first to leave soirees—rather than mill about with “fashionable” folk, he was retiring, and preferred the solitude of his garret.

definition: to say something sharp or witty in answer; a sharp or witty reply; a glass container used for distillation
chinese: v. 反駁；回嘴；n. 反駁；機智的回答；（化學）曲頸瓶
example: He was tempted to retort, but thought better of it.

definition: to improve a painting or photograph with slight alterations; to touch up dyed hair; an act of retouching
chinese: v. 潤飾；修飾（照片等）；補染（頭髮）；n. 潤飾；修改
example: In this context, “retouch” means give retouches to (hair).

definition: to withdraw a statement or accusation as untrue; to go back on an agreement; to draw something back in
chinese: 撤回；收回（聲明或承諾）；縮回
example: The author of the article was forced to retract her previous article after the information was debunked.

definition: to withdraw or move back; to change one's mind out of fear; a withdrawal; a quiet secluded place; a period of seclusion for reflection
chinese: v. 撤退；退縮；退避；（價格）下跌；n. 撤退；退縮；隱居處；靜修
example: Some arrangements about his horse and baggage formed the pretext for his sudden retreat.

definition: to reduce costs or spending; to cut down or curtail
chinese: 削減開支；緊縮；削減
example: In this context, “retrench” means tighten one's belt; use resources carefully.

definition: punishment inflicted as vengeance for a wrong or criminal act
chinese: 懲罰；報應；報復
example: But retribution was at hand, and the wicked city met with sudden destruction.

definition: to get or bring back; to set right a bad situation; to find and extract stored information; (of a dog) to fetch
chinese: 取回；尋回；挽回；檢索（資料）；（狗）銜回（獵物）
example: Bruno's dog balances on a bodyboard to retrieve his ball in a pool.

definition: taking effect from a date in the past; relating to the past
chinese: 有追溯效力的；溯及既往的
example: Retroactive jealousy is more toxic than reactive jealousy.

definition: directed or moving backward; reverting to an earlier, worse state; (of a planet) apparently moving opposite to the usual direction; to go backward or decline
chinese: adj. 倒退的；退步的；（天文）逆行的；v. 倒退；退化
example: The readiest support for planets' having confocal orbits is their sometimes retrograde motion.

definition: looking back on past events; taking effect from a past date; an exhibition showing an artist's development over a career
chinese: adj. 回顧的；懷舊的；有追溯效力的；n. 回顧展
example: We'll start the meeting with a retrospective look at the past year.

definition: to take great pleasure in something; to engage in lively and noisy festivities; lively celebration
chinese: v. 陶醉；著迷；狂歡；n. 狂歡；歡宴
example: I am too sick at heart to revel, carouse, and make merry through the night.

definition: a surprising and previously unknown fact made known; the act of revealing; divine disclosure of truth
chinese: 揭露；爆料；驚人的發現；啟示
example: Revelation is necessarily out of the question with respect to those books.

definition: the act of inflicting harm in return for an injury or wrong; to inflict harm in return for a wrong done
chinese: n. 報復；復仇；v. 報仇；為…復仇
example: Make sure the snake is completely dead, or he will surely take his revenge.

definition: income, especially of a company or government; the total amount of money received
chinese: 收入；營收；歲入；稅收
example: The sale of postage stamps to foreign collectors is an important source of revenue.

definition: having a tendency to reverberate; echoing
chinese: 迴響的；回音繚繞的；反射的
example: a reverberant room

definition: (of a sound) to be repeated as an echo; to have continuing and serious effects
chinese: 迴盪；迴響；產生持續影響
example: The loud sounds of sawing, drilling and scraping reverberate around the room.

definition: to feel deep respect or admiration for
chinese: 崇敬；尊崇；敬畏
example: In this context, “revere” means American silversmith remembered for his midnight ride (celebrated in a poem by Longfellow) to warn the colonists in Lexington and Concord that British troops were coming (1735-1818).

definition: deep respect mixed with awe; veneration; to regard with deep respect or awe
chinese: n. 崇敬；敬畏；尊崇；v. 尊敬；崇敬
example: The stars awaken a certain reverence, because though always present, they are inaccessible.

definition: to overturn (a decision); to turn the other way; to back up; the opposite; the back side (of a coin); a setback; opposite in direction
chinese: v. 推翻（判決）；扭轉；顛倒；倒車；n. 反面；背面；挫折；adj. 相反的；反向的
example: The scholar's monograph on ancient coins detailed the obverse and reverse of each specimen.

definition: capable of being reversed or undone; able to be revoked; (of clothing) wearable inside out
chinese: 可逆的；可撤銷的；（衣物）兩面可穿的
example: reversible hypertension

definition: to return to a previous state, practice, or condition; (of property) to return to a former owner
chinese: 恢復（原狀）；回復；（財產）歸還
example: The situation will soon revert to the way things were before.

definition: to criticize in an abusive or angrily insulting manner
chinese: 辱罵；痛斥；謾罵
example: Love me or revile me, but do not ignore me.

definition: to alter or correct (a text); to reconsider and change (an opinion or estimate); (British) to review for an exam
chinese: 修訂；修改；修正（看法）；（英）複習
example: revise a thesis

definition: the act of revising or altering; an altered version; (British) review for an exam
chinese: 修訂；修正；修訂版；（英）複習
example: Branching and merging are two basic operations of revision control.

definition: to give new life, energy, or vigor to; to revive
chinese: 使復興；使恢復活力；使重振
example: City planners hope that new businesses will revitalize the downtown area.

definition: restored to new life and vigor
chinese: 重振的；恢復活力的；復甦的
example: a revitalized economy

definition: to restore to life or consciousness; to bring back into use or popularity; to become active again
chinese: 使復甦；使甦醒；復興；重新流行
example: You'll never be able to revive someone who is only pretending to be dead.

definition: to officially cancel or annul (a law, license, or decision)
chinese: 撤銷；廢除；吊銷（執照）
example: They should revoke the driving license of motorcyclists who drive on the sidewalk.

definition: a rebellion or uprising; to rise in rebellion; to fill with disgust
chinese: n. 反叛；起義；反抗；v. 反叛；使厭惡；使反感
example: After a brief gathering, it was decided to start the revolt immediately.

definition: language that is impressive or persuasive but often insincere; the art of effective or persuasive speaking or writing
chinese: 花言巧語；誇飾言辭；修辭；修辭學
example: The rhetoric of hate is often most effective when couched in the idiom of love.

definition: relating to rhetoric; showy but empty in language; (of a question) asked for effect, not for an answer
chinese: 修辭的；言辭浮誇的；（問句）反問的
example: When someone speaks with such rhetorical flourish, it starts to sound like they're lying.

definition: humorously vulgar or indecent in speech or behavior
chinese: 下流的；粗俗的；猥褻的
example: The passage describes its subject as ribald, meaning a ribald person; someone who uses vulgar and offensive language.

definition: poorly made and likely to collapse; shaky; feeble
chinese: 搖搖欲墜的；不穩固的；（體弱）搖晃的
example: A rickety clavichord gathered dust in a forgotten corner of the drawing room.

definition: a long narrow raised strip of land or mountain crest; a raised line or strip; to form into ridges
chinese: n. 山脊；山脈；脊；隆起處；v. 使成脊狀
example: It's very pleasant to live in a beautiful city at the foot of a mountain ridge.

definition: to mock or make fun of; mockery or derision
chinese: v. 嘲笑；揶揄；n. 嘲笑；譏諷
example: That magazine often functions as a modern satirical pamphlet, aiming to ridicule the powerful.

definition: deserving or inviting mockery; absurd
chinese: 荒謬的；可笑的；荒唐的
example: Generally speaking, the errors in religion are dangerous; those in philosophy only ridiculous.

definition: (of something bad) widespread; full of (rife with)
chinese: （壞事）盛行的；充斥的；普遍的
example: The village is rife with dirty shops selling cheapjack souvenirs.

definition: a serious break in friendly relations; a crack or split in rock or ground
chinese: 裂痕；不和；分歧；裂縫
example: A deep rift opened up between them.

definition: unable to adapt; inflexible; strict; stiff and not able to bend
chinese: 僵化的；死板的；嚴格的；堅硬的
example: a rigid strip of metal

definition: a long, complicated, and pointless procedure; confused or meaningless talk
chinese: 冗長無謂的程序；繁瑣手續；混亂無意義的話
example: In this context, “rigmarole” refers to a set of confused and meaningless statements.

definition: thoroughness and precision; strictness; harshness or severity of conditions
chinese: 嚴謹；嚴密；嚴格；嚴酷；艱苦
example: When translating, one must have all the rigor and no respect for the original.

definition: extremely thorough and accurate; strictly applied; harsh or severe
chinese: 嚴謹的；嚴密的；嚴格的；嚴酷的
example: rigorous application of the law

definition: to make someone annoyed or irritated
chinese: 惹怒；激怒；使煩躁
example: In this context, “rile” means cause annoyance in; disturb, especially by minor irritations.

definition: a violent public disturbance; a vivid profusion (a riot of color); to take part in a violent disturbance
chinese: n. 暴動；騷亂；（色彩等）豐富多彩；v. 暴動；鬧事
example: There was an angry crowd gathered outside the courthouse causing a riot.

definition: to become or make ripe; to develop fully
chinese: 成熟；使成熟；（時機）成熟
example: She watched the gardens grow, and she watched the apples turn red and ripen.

definition: a ceremonial act or procedure, especially religious; a customary practice
chinese: 儀式；典禮；慣例
example: Naming his son after himself felt like a rite of passage.

definition: to tear or split apart violently
chinese: 撕裂；劈開；使分裂
example: In this context, “rive” means tear or be torn violently.

definition: completely engrossing; holding one's attention
chinese: 引人入勝的；吸引人的；扣人心弦的
example: The passage describes its subject as riveting, meaning direct one's attention on something.

definition: strong and healthy; sturdy and able to withstand problems; (of flavor) full and rich
chinese: 強健的；穩健的；健全的；（酒味）濃郁的
example: The company has implemented robust security measures to protect sensitive customer data.

definition: to make (liquid) muddy by stirring up sediment; to throw into disorder; to irritate or disturb
chinese: 攪渾；使混亂；激怒；使不安
example: In this context, “roil” means make turbid by stirring up the sediments of.

definition: a beginner or newcomer; a new recruit
chinese: 新手；菜鳥；新兵
example: The rookie dancer's movements, though energetic, were still a bit graceless compared to the seasoned veterans'.

definition: promising or hopeful; (of skin or lips) pink and healthy-looking; rose-colored
chinese: 樂觀的；美好的；玫瑰色的；紅潤的
example: And then he kissed her rosy mouth and played with her long waving hair.

definition: mechanical memorization or repetition without understanding; routine
chinese: 死記硬背；機械式重複；例行公事
example: This is something that you'll just have to learn by rote.

definition: having an uneven surface; approximate; violent; difficult; a preliminary sketch; long grass on a golf course; to treat roughly; to sketch out
chinese: adj. 粗糙的；概略的；粗暴的；艱難的；n. 草稿；（高爾夫）長草區；v. 粗暴對待；擬草稿
example: trees with rough bark

definition: to stir up or provoke (feeling or action); to wake from sleep; to anger
chinese: 激起；喚起；喚醒；激怒
example: The slogan was designed to rouse the people.

definition: a line of people or things; a noisy quarrel; to propel a boat with oars; to argue noisily
chinese: n. 排；行；爭吵；吵鬧；v. 划船；爭吵
example: A row of old houses is being destroyed to make way for new flats.

definition: a payment to an author or patent holder for each copy or use; royal persons; royal status
chinese: 版稅；權利金；王室成員；王族身分
example: One bethinks that they have heard enough of royalty, but yet another scandal arises.

definition: having a ruddy, healthy reddish complexion
chinese: （臉色）紅潤的；氣色好的
example: The passage describes its subject as rubicund, meaning inclined to a healthy reddish color often associated with outdoor life.

definition: impolite or offensive; roughly made; primitive or crude; abrupt and unpleasant (a rude awakening)
chinese: 無禮的；粗魯的；簡陋的；原始的；突然的
example: Stefan went down to the front desk to complain about a rude employee.

definition: involving only basic principles; elementary; undeveloped; (of an organ) vestigial
chinese: 基本的；初步的；未發展完全的；（器官）退化的
example: Digital cameras aren't as good as rudimentary cameras.

definition: to bitterly regret; regret or sorrow; a strong-scented herb
chinese: v. 後悔；懊悔；n. 悔恨；（植）芸香
example: I rue the day I crossed paths with this asshole.

definition: to disturb the composure of; to make uneven or messy; to rustle; a gathered frill; a ripple
chinese: v. 激怒；使心煩；弄亂；n. 褶邊；漣漪
example: Igor heard something ruffle in the woods.

definition: sturdy and durable; rough-featured; having a rough uneven surface; tough and determined
chinese: 堅固耐用的；粗獷的；崎嶇的；（性格）剛毅的
example: with a house full of boys you have to have rugged furniture

definition: to think deeply about something at length; to chew the cud
chinese: 反覆思考；沉思；（牛等）反芻
example: In this context, “ruminate” means chew the cuds.

definition: deep or prolonged thought; the act of chewing the cud
chinese: 沉思；反覆思考；反芻
example: Rumination is an important stage of making decisions.

definition: to make or become wrinkled or untidy; a wrinkle or crease
chinese: v. 弄皺；弄亂；n. 皺褶
example: In this context, “rumple” means become wrinkled or crumpled or creased.

definition: mysterious or cryptic; relating to or written in runes
chinese: 神祕的；古代北歐文字的；如詩謎般的
example: The passage describes its subject as runic, meaning relating to or consisting of runes.

definition: a breaking or bursting; a breach of relations; to break or burst; to sever
chinese: n. 破裂；決裂；斷絕；v. 破裂；使斷絕
example: After extensively studying the quake and its aftermath, scientists say the rupture is unprecedented.

definition: an action intended to deceive; a trick
chinese: 詭計；計謀；花招
example: All the sweet talk was just a ruse to get her into bed.

definition: characteristic of the countryside; simple and plain; roughly made; an unsophisticated country person
chinese: adj. 鄉村的；質樸的；粗糙的；n. 鄉下人；鄉巴佬
example: The rock gardens, waterfalls, gazebos, amphitheater and rustic cement bridges have survived virtually intact.

definition: to make a soft crackling sound; to steal (cattle); to move quickly; a soft crackling sound
chinese: v. 沙沙作響；偷（牲畜）；迅速行動；n. 沙沙聲
example: When it's windy, the leaves of the old oak rustle and its branches creak.

definition: having no pity or compassion
chinese: 無情的；殘忍的；冷酷的
example: Those guys are ruthless, covering up their tracks like that after all their wrongdoing.

definition: to deliberately destroy or obstruct; to undermine; deliberate destruction or obstruction
chinese: v. 蓄意破壞；暗中阻撓；n. 破壞活動；蓄意破壞
example: She knew they were going to sabotage her, but she had no way to stop them.

definition: excessively sweet or sentimental; sugary
chinese: 過於甜膩的；矯情的；甜的
example: The passage describes its subject as saccharine, meaning overly sweet.

definition: connected with religion; regarded with great respect and reverence; not to be violated
chinese: 神聖的；宗教的；不可侵犯的；受崇敬的
example: sacred texts

definition: violation or misuse of something sacred or highly valued
chinese: 褻瀆；褻瀆神聖；冒瀆
example: In this context, “sacrilege” refers to blasphemous behavior; the act of depriving something of its sacred character.

definition: too important or sacred to be interfered with
chinese: 神聖不可侵犯的；極神聖的
example: The judge reminded the jury that the right to a fair trial was sacrosanct to their nation.

definition: a seat for riding a horse; a seat on a bicycle; to burden with something unwelcome; to put a saddle on
chinese: n. 馬鞍；（車）座墊；v. 使負擔；加重負擔；裝鞍
example: Many of the cowboys spend more than eight hours a day in the saddle.

definition: a measure taken to protect; protection; to protect from harm
chinese: n. 保護措施；防護；v. 保護；捍衛
example: The safeguard of the state shall be the supreme law.

definition: having keen judgment and wisdom; shrewd
chinese: 睿智的；精明的；有洞察力的
example: A sagacious activist would have pointed out the assumptions underlying those loaded questions.

definition: keen discernment and sound judgment; wisdom
chinese: 睿智；精明；洞察力
example: I fear my loose tongue has belied any pretentions I had of sagacity.

definition: a profoundly wise person; an aromatic herb; wise and judicious
chinese: n. 智者；聖賢；（植）鼠尾草；adj. 睿智的；明智的
example: There is no need to explain to a sage what is expected of him.

definition: lustful; having undue interest in sexual matters; indecent
chinese: 好色的；淫穢的；猥褻的
example: He goaded him on to ever more salacious revelations.

definition: most noticeable or important; conspicuous; a projecting part of a battle line
chinese: adj. 顯著的；最突出的；n. 突出部
example: I'm spending seven out of five of my working days writing pseudo-salient quips.

definition: promoting health; pleasant; (of a place) clean and respectable
chinese: 有益健康的；宜人的；（地區）體面的
example: The mountain air was crisp and salubrious, restoring her energy after weeks in the city.

definition: producing a beneficial effect, often despite being unpleasant; promoting health
chinese: 有益的；有教育意義的；有益健康的
example: Releasing anger can be salutary.

definition: a greeting or gesture of greeting; the opening words of a letter, such as "Dear Sir"
chinese: 問候；致意；（書信的）稱呼語
example: In the second example, the interpreter mistranslates the salutation.

definition: to honor or praise formally; to greet with a gesture of respect; a gesture of respect; a firing of guns as a mark of honor
chinese: v. 致敬；表揚；行禮；n. 敬禮；禮炮；致意
example: The captain gave orders for a salute to be fired.

definition: to rescue or save from loss or ruin; the rescue of a ship or goods; property saved from destruction
chinese: v. 搶救；挽回；n. 海難救助；搶救出的財物
example: The only way to salvage the situation, he said, was to reduce the birth rate.

definition: a soothing ointment; something that soothes; to ease (guilt or conscience); to soothe
chinese: n. 藥膏；慰藉；v. 緩和；安撫（良心等）
example: A lovely bit of cake like this is the best salve for a wounded heart.

definition: to make holy; to give official approval or moral sanction to
chinese: 使神聖；認可；使正當化
example: I am too alone in the world, and yet not alone enough to sanctify every hour...

definition: making a hypocritical show of piety or moral superiority
chinese: 假裝虔誠的；道貌岸然的；自以為道德高尚的
example: Even during the quiet sanctity of evening prayer, she held her chin high, a sanctimonious sneer forming on her face as she eyed those who were attending church for the first time.

definition: hypocritical devoutness or self-righteousness
chinese: 偽善；假虔誠；道貌岸然
example: In this context, “sanctimony” refers to the quality of being hypocritically devout.

definition: official permission or approval; a penalty for disobeying a law; to authorize or approve; to impose a penalty on
chinese: n. 批准；認可；制裁；處罰；v. 批准；認可；制裁
example: It is necessary to obtain the sanction of the authorities to enter this building.

definition: a place of refuge or safety; protection; a nature reserve; a holy place
chinese: 避難所；庇護；保護區；聖所
example: Marine sanctuary managers use a combination of science, education, and enforcement to protect marine life.

definition: optimistic or confident, especially in a difficult situation; (of complexion) ruddy
chinese: 樂觀的；自信的；（臉色）紅潤的
example: With the prospect of having to learn 3,000 words during the course of the summer, Paul was anything but sanguine.

definition: the quality of being optimistically cheerful and confident
chinese: 樂觀；自信；開朗
example: In this context, “sanguinity” refers to feeling sanguine; optimistically cheerful and confident.

definition: relating to health and cleanliness; hygienic; relating to sanitation
chinese: 衛生的；清潔的；公共衛生的
example: Sanitary napkin, tampon, feminine protection -- all those terms mean the same thing.

definition: the ability to think and behave normally; soundness of mind; sound judgment
chinese: 神智正常；心智健全；明智
example: The thin line between sanity and madness has gotten finer.

definition: to gradually weaken or drain (strength or energy); the fluid in a plant; vitality; a foolish person
chinese: v. 削弱；耗盡（體力等）；n. 樹液；活力；（口）傻瓜
example: Maple trees are famous for their sweet sap, which is used to produce maple syrup.

definition: wise or showing great discernment; (of a being) intelligent and self-aware
chinese: 有智慧的；睿智的；有知覺的
example: Sapient beings are far more advanced than humans.

definition: the use of mocking irony to show contempt
chinese: 挖苦；諷刺；嘲諷
example: Narcissists engage in passive-aggressive behavior, using sarcasm and veiled insults to manipulate others' emotions.

definition: marked by mocking irony meant to wound or show contempt
chinese: 挖苦的；諷刺的；尖酸的
example: He realized she was being sarcastic when she flexed her fingers for flamboyant air quotes.

definition: grimly mocking or cynical; scornfully humorous
chinese: 嘲諷的；冷笑的；譏諷的
example: his rebellion is the bitter, sardonic laughter of all great satirists

definition: relating to clothing, tailoring, or style of dress
chinese: 服裝的；衣著的；裁縫的
example: You can't just pass off your questionable sartorial decisions as "pushing the envelope" of fashion.

definition: to satisfy (an appetite or desire) fully; (archaic) past tense of sit
chinese: 使飽足；充分滿足；（古）坐（過去式）
example: Then, girt with guards, within the temple's gate / beneath the centre of the dome she sate.

definition: to satisfy fully or to excess; fully satisfied
chinese: v. 使飽足；使厭膩；滿足；adj. 飽足的
example: All the money in the world will not be enough to satiate his greed.

definition: the use of humor, irony, or ridicule to criticize; a work using such methods
chinese: 諷刺；諷刺作品；諷刺文學
example: Satire has a point, and that point can be criticized like any serious argument.

definition: to mock or criticize through satire
chinese: 諷刺；譏諷
example: In this context, “satirize” means ridicule with satire.

definition: to soak thoroughly; to fill completely; to cause to reach saturation; to supply a market beyond demand
chinese: 浸透；使充滿；使飽和；（市場）飽和
example: Kaleidoscopic prints saturate my blank mind, creating vital memories and burning thoughts.

definition: holding the maximum amount of a dissolved substance; thoroughly soaked; full; (of color) intense
chinese: 飽和的；浸透的；充滿的；（色彩）濃豔的
example: a saturated solution

definition: gloomy, morose, or sullen in temperament
chinese: 陰沉的；憂鬱的；冷漠的
example: Deprived of sunlight, humans become saturnine; that’s why in very northerly territories people are encouraged to sit under an extremely powerful lamp, lest they become morose.

definition: to walk in a slow, relaxed manner; a leisurely stroll or gait
chinese: v. 閒逛；漫步；n. 漫步；悠閒的步伐
example: In this context, “saunter” refers to a careless leisurely gait.

definition: a learned person; a person with exceptional ability in one area despite a developmental disorder
chinese: 學者；博學之士；學者症候群患者
example: There are no objectively definitive statistics about how many people have savant skills.

definition: to enjoy or appreciate fully; to taste with pleasure; a characteristic taste or smell; a distinctive quality
chinese: v. 品味；細細享受；n. 滋味；風味；韻味
example: We only get healed from a passion when we savor it till the end.

definition: (of food) salty or spicy rather than sweet; appetizing; morally respectable; a savory snack
chinese: adj. 鹹香可口的；美味的；體面的；n. 鹹味點心
example: Matthew's soup recipe included garlic powder and thyme for a savory flavor.

definition: shrewd and knowledgeable; practical know-how; shrewdness
chinese: adj. 精明的；有見識的；n. 實際知識；精明
example: Successful fascists today are savvy enough not to call themselves fascists.

definition: a large number or quantity
chinese: 大量；許多
example: Scads of online daters constantly check their desirability.

definition: causing general outrage; shocking; containing scandal or slander
chinese: 可恥的；駭人聽聞的；誹謗的
example: The fact that soccer players are so rich is something most people find scandalous.

definition: barely sufficient; very little; to give inadequate attention to; to skimp on
chinese: adj. 不足的；極少的；勉強夠的；v. 輕忽；吝於給予
example: The volunteer firefighters fought the blaze bravely, with scant regard for their own safety.

definition: almost not; barely; only just (before something else happened); surely not
chinese: 幾乎不；勉強；剛剛（就）；絕不
example: She had scarcely started reading the book, when someone knocked at the door.

definition: witheringly scornful or severely critical
chinese: 嚴厲的；尖刻的；猛烈抨擊的
example: He behaved, unconsciously, in ways that sometimes inspired sharp criticism and scathing rebukes.

definition: pleasure derived from another person's misfortune
chinese: 幸災樂禍
example: From his warm apartment window, Stanley reveled in schadenfreude as he laughed at the figures below, huddled together in the arctic chill.

definition: represented in simplified or symbolic form; overly simplified; a diagram, especially of an electrical circuit
chinese: adj. 概略的；圖解的；簡化的；n. 示意圖；電路圖
example: Could you send me the schematic for this?

definition: a systematic plan or program; an arrangement or system; a secret or devious plot; to plot secretly
chinese: n. 計畫；方案；體系；陰謀；v. 密謀；策劃
example: He retires before the new pension scheme is due to come into effect.

definition: a split or division between opposing groups; a formal breach within a church
chinese: 分裂；分歧；（教會）分立
example: Helen's forum experienced an irreconcilable schism over whether to use one or two oven mitts.

definition: a tiny trace or barely detectable amount
chinese: 極微量；一絲；絲毫
example: There is not an iota, not a scintilla, not a hint of any real evidence.

definition: to emit flashes of light; to sparkle; to be brilliantly lively or witty
chinese: 閃爍；發出火花；（言談）煥發才氣
example: Her eyes scintillate with joy.

definition: brilliantly clever, lively, or witty; sparkling
chinese: 妙趣橫生的；才氣煥發的；閃爍的
example: Richard Feynman was renowned for his scintillating lectures—the arcana of quantum physics was made lucid as he wrote animatedly on the chalkboard.

definition: the act of cutting or dividing; a split
chinese: 切斷；分裂；分離
example: In this context, “scission” refers to the act of dividing by cutting or splitting.

definition: to cut with scissors; to remove or cut out; to move in a scissor-like motion
chinese: 剪；剪開；刪去；交叉擺動
example: The fault could scissor the rock layers in opposite directions.

definition: to speak scornfully; to mock; to eat greedily; an expression of scorn
chinese: v. 嘲笑；譏諷；（口）狼吞虎嚥；n. 嘲笑
example: I'm not going to change my opinion no matter how much you scoff.

definition: an angry rebuke or harsh reprimand
chinese: 責罵；斥責
example: It was cathartic to finally watch him get the scolding he deserved.

definition: to burn the surface of; to dry out with intense heat; a burn mark
chinese: v. 燒焦；烤焦；使枯萎；n. 焦痕
example: You can still see the scorch marks from last week's fire.

definition: contempt or disdain; to regard as worthless; to refuse with contempt
chinese: n. 輕蔑；鄙視；v. 蔑視；不屑（做）
example: Don't speak of holy things with such scorn, not even in a joke.

definition: to decisively put an end to; to discredit (a rumor); Scotch whisky
chinese: v. 阻止；粉碎（謠言等）；使終止；n. 蘇格蘭威士忌
example: These gatherings always get rowdy after hours, when the boss breaks out the single-malt scotch.

definition: to search thoroughly; to clean by hard rubbing; to erode by flowing water
chinese: 徹底搜查；搜索；擦洗；沖刷
example: To solve the mystery she will have to scour his personal belongings for clues.

definition: a cause of great suffering; a whip; to cause great suffering to; to whip; to punish severely
chinese: n. 禍害；禍根；鞭子；v. 使受苦；鞭打；嚴厲懲罰
example: Empowered, informed citizens are the scourge of any tyrant.

definition: to frown in an angry or bad-tempered way; an angry frown
chinese: v. 皺眉怒視；n. 怒容；蹙眉
example: He had a thatch of white hair and a red, wrinkled face with blue eyes and a scowl.

definition: a small piece or amount; waste material; a fight; to discard or abandon as useless
chinese: n. 碎片；少許；廢料；（口）打架；v. 廢棄；取消
example: Encourage your friends and family to be conscious of food scrap disposal as well.

definition: determined and tenacious; quarrelsome; made up of disorganized bits
chinese: 鬥志旺盛的；好鬥的；零碎的；雜亂的
example: Google was once small and scrappy.

definition: to write in a hurried, careless way; messy, careless handwriting
chinese: v. 潦草書寫；亂塗；n. 潦草的字跡
example: A terrible, almost illegible scrawl.

definition: a long, tedious speech or piece of writing; a leveling layer of material on a floor
chinese: 冗長的長篇大論；冗長文章；（抹灰）找平層
example: Joey had difficulty hanging out with his former best friend Perry, who, during his entire cup of coffee, would enumerate all of the government’s deficiencies, only to break ranks and launch into some screed against big business.

definition: a display surface; a partition or shelter; to examine or test systematically; to conceal or shield; to show (a film)
chinese: n. 螢幕；屏障；隔板；v. 篩選；檢查；遮蔽；放映
example: Tap on the earth icon on the iPad screen to launch the map app.

definition: to write or draw carelessly or hurriedly; hasty, illegible writing
chinese: v. 潦草地寫；亂塗；n. 潦草字跡；塗鴉
example: I remember that I used to scribble things on my eraser during class.

definition: to be very economical; to spend as little as possible
chinese: 節省；縮衣節食；吝嗇
example: The group had to scrimp, connive, and hustle in order to get by.

definition: a feeling of doubt about whether an action is morally right; to hesitate on ethical grounds
chinese: n. （道德上的）顧忌；躊躇；v. 有顧忌；躊躇
example: If they do not agree they will without scruple act contrary to that decision.

definition: extremely careful and thorough; concerned to avoid doing wrong; principled
chinese: 一絲不苟的；嚴謹的；有道德原則的；正直的
example: You can see that the architect paid scrupulous attention to detail.

definition: capable of being understood through study or observation
chinese: 可理解的；可解讀的
example: The passage describes its subject as scrutable, meaning Discoverable by scrutiny, inquiry, or critical.

definition: to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly
chinese: 仔細審查；細看；詳細檢查
example: We're going to scrutinize everything.

definition: critical observation or examination; close watch
chinese: 仔細審查；細看；監督
example: The new policy was under intense juridical scrutiny to ensure it complied with constitutional law.

definition: to scrape or roughen a surface by wear; to drag one's feet; a mark made by scraping
chinese: v. 磨損；拖著腳走；n. 磨損痕跡
example: Please don't scuff your shoes on the recently mopped floor.

definition: making scandalous or slanderous claims to damage reputation; grossly abusive or vulgar
chinese: 惡意中傷的；粗俗下流的；誹謗的
example: When freedom of the press was fresh, newspapers were even more scurrilous and libelous than today.

definition: a disease caused by lack of vitamin C; contemptible or mean
chinese: n. 壞血病；adj. 卑鄙的；可鄙的
example: To fight scurvy, we added rose hips and black currant syrup to our food.

definition: sordid and disreputable; showing the unpleasant side of life
chinese: 污穢的；醜惡的；墮落的
example: There is a seamy side to everything.

definition: to withdraw formally from a federation, alliance, or organization
chinese: 脫離（聯邦）；退出（組織）
example: Trying to secede from the mainland, the fissiparous polities have been causing serious problems to the central authority.

definition: to keep away from other people; to isolate
chinese: 使隔離；使隱居；使隔絕
example: You should seclude him from temptation.

definition: sheltered and private; away from other people
chinese: 僻靜的；隱蔽的；隱居的
example: At first glance, the videos conjure up visions of a secluded utopian paradise.

definition: a person who handles correspondence and records; the head of a government department
chinese: 祕書；書記；（政府）部長；大臣
example: Officially it is his responsibility, but in fact his secretary does all the work.

definition: to produce and discharge (a substance); to conceal or hide
chinese: 分泌；隱藏；藏匿
example: Glands secrete chemical substances into the body.

definition: relating to sects or factions; narrow-minded or bigoted; a person who rigidly follows a sect
chinese: adj. 宗派的；派系的；狹隘的；n. 宗派主義者
example: Lebanon needs to get rid of its sectarian system.

definition: excessive attachment to a particular sect or party, often leading to bigotry or conflict
chinese: 宗派主義；派系偏見；門戶之見
example: In this context, “sectarianism” refers to a narrow-minded adherence to a particular sect or party or denomination.

definition: not connected with religion or spiritual matters; worldly; (of trends) long-term
chinese: 世俗的；非宗教的；長期的
example: The general trend seems to be that the whole world is becoming more secular.

definition: calm, dignified, and unhurried; to calm with a sedative drug
chinese: adj. 沉著的；穩重的；平靜的；v. 給服鎮靜劑
example: The passage describes its subject as sedate, meaning cause to be calm or quiet as by administering a sedative to.

definition: a drug that calms or induces sleep; having a calming effect
chinese: n. 鎮靜劑；adj. 鎮靜的；使安靜的
example: The doctor gave him a sedative.

definition: involving much sitting and little activity; (of animals) not migratory
chinese: 久坐的；缺乏運動的；（動物）定居的
example: Many people lead a sedentary life, which can lead to weight gain.

definition: matter that settles to the bottom of a liquid; material deposited by water or wind; to deposit as sediment
chinese: n. 沉積物；沉澱物；v. 沉積；沉澱
example: By means of a super high-pressure water spray practically all the sediment is removed.

definition: inciting rebellion against authority
chinese: 煽動叛亂的；煽動性的
example: Do not disturb the soul with seditious truth; better a virtuous lie.

definition: to attract or entice; to persuade into sexual activity; to lead astray
chinese: 引誘；誘惑；勾引；誘使誤入歧途
example: Being a language, mathematics may be used not only to inform but also, among other things, to seduce.

definition: tempting and attractive; enticing
chinese: 誘人的；有魅力的；誘惑的
example: That's a very seductive idea but you should be careful.

definition: showing dedication and persistent careful effort
chinese: 勤勉的；孜孜不倦的；刻苦的
example: The passage describes its subject as sedulous, meaning marked by care and persistent effort.

definition: conforming to accepted standards of propriety; decorous
chinese: 得體的；合宜的；端莊的
example: The passage describes its subject as seemly, meaning according with custom or propriety.

definition: a portion or section; to divide into parts
chinese: n. 部分；片段；區段；v. 分割；劃分
example: Last summer, cigarettes from the middle price segment appeared on the market.

definition: the belittling or humiliation of oneself
chinese: 自貶；自我貶抑；自卑
example: In this context, “self-abasement” refers to voluntary self-punishment in order to atone for some wrongdoing.

definition: preoccupied with one's own emotions, interests, or situation
chinese: 只顧自己的；自我中心的；沉浸於自我的
example: They're too self-absorbed to see how much work they're creating for their parents.

definition: tending to defeat its own purpose
chinese: 適得其反的；弄巧成拙的；自我挫敗的
example: The passage describes its subject as self-defeating, meaning acting to defeat its own purpose.

definition: obvious without needing proof or explanation
chinese: 不言而喻的；不證自明的
example: It is self-evident that she needs to work hard to achieve her goals.

definition: continuing or renewing itself without external intervention
chinese: 自我延續的；自行持續的
example: The passage describes its subject as self-perpetuating, meaning continuing without ant external intervention.

definition: respect or consideration for oneself; vanity; concern for one's own interest
chinese: 自尊；自負；顧及自身利益
example: In this context, “self-regard” refers to the quality of being worthy of esteem or respect.

definition: smugly certain of one's own moral superiority
chinese: 自以為是的；自命清高的；自以為道德高尚的
example: Carol is an entitled, self-righteous person who thinks she's morally superior to everyone else and deserves special treatment.

definition: more concerned with others' needs than with one's own; unselfish
chinese: 無私的；忘我的
example: We are better off for the service rendered by this brave and selfless leader.

definition: the outward appearance of something, often misleading; a small degree or trace
chinese: 表象；外表；假象；些許
example: he hoped his claims would have a semblance of authenticity

definition: highly original and influential on later developments; relating to semen or seed
chinese: 開創性的；影響深遠的；精液的；種子的
example: The passage describes its subject as seminal, meaning pertaining to or containing or consisting of semen.

definition: a meeting for discussion or training; a small class for advanced study
chinese: 研討會；專題討論課
example: 'Seminar', in universities, refers to debates and the presentation of research results by a few students.

definition: a physical feeling or perception; the ability to feel; widespread excitement or a cause of it
chinese: 感覺；知覺；轟動；轟動事件
example: The sensation of pain can become a part of one’s identity over time.

definition: the enjoyment or pursuit of physical, especially sexual, pleasure
chinese: 感官享樂；肉慾；性感
example: In this context, “sensuality” refers to desire for sensual pleasures.

definition: given to pompous moralizing; (of style) terse and full of aphorisms
chinese: 好說教的；道貌岸然的；（文句）簡練精闢的
example: The passage describes its subject as sententious, meaning abounding in or given to pompous or aphoristic moralizing.

definition: a feeling or emotion; tender or nostalgic feeling; a view or opinion; general mood or attitude
chinese: 情感；感傷；看法；觀點；情緒
example: As far as the piano is concerned, sentiment is my forte.

definition: prompted by tender or nostalgic feelings; excessively emotional; relating to emotions
chinese: 多愁善感的；感情用事的；情感上的
example: I wouldn't call myself a sentimental person, but it brought tears to my eyes.

definition: infected with bacteria; putrefying; relating to a septic tank for sewage
chinese: （傷口）感染的；化膿的；腐敗的；（化糞池）污水處理的
example: A septic tank should not be confused with a well.

definition: gloomy and dismal; relating to a tomb or burial; (of a voice) deep and hollow
chinese: 陰森的；陰沉的；墳墓的；（聲音）低沉的
example: The passage describes its subject as sepulchral, meaning of or relating to a sepulchre.

definition: a book or film continuing an earlier story; a consequence or result
chinese: 續集；續篇；後果；結果
example: The movie was more popular than expected, and there was even talk of a sequel.

definition: a condition resulting from a previous disease or injury; a consequence
chinese: （醫）後遺症；後果
example: In this context, “sequela” refers to any abnormality following or resulting from a disease or injury or treatment.

definition: to isolate or set apart; to seclude; to seize (property) by legal authority; to capture and store (e.g. carbon)
chinese: 隔離；使隱退；扣押（財產）；（化學）封存
example: In this context, “sequester” means requisition forcibly, as of enemy property.

definition: dry and withered
chinese: 乾枯的；凋萎的
example: In spring brightly green, and spangled with wild flowers, by midsummer this prairie had grown sere and yellow.

definition: occurring by fortunate chance; discovered by happy accident
chinese: 意外發現的；機緣巧合的；幸運的
example: One's spirituality is a long serendipitous journey.

definition: the occurrence of fortunate discoveries by chance
chinese: 意外的發現；機緣巧合；意外好運
example: We all have experienced the serendipity of relevant information arriving just when we were least expecting it.

definition: calm, peaceful, and untroubled; (of weather) clear and still
chinese: 寧靜的；安詳的；平靜的；晴朗的
example: He stared at that beautiful serene face, that mouth so often kissed, those blue eyes pitiful.

definition: a religious talk given in church; a long moralizing lecture
chinese: 布道；講道；說教；訓誡
example: No sinner is ever saved after the first twenty minutes of a sermon.

definition: winding like a snake; cunning or treacherous; a dark green mineral used in decoration
chinese: adj. 蜿蜒的；彎曲的；陰險的；n. 蛇紋石
example: The rotting shanty town was not too distant from the grandiose temples of serpentine.

definition: (of rows of people or things) standing close together
chinese: 密集的；排列緊密的
example: Above the bush the trees stood in serried ranks.

definition: excessively eager to please or obey; obsequious; relating to slaves
chinese: 奴性的；卑屈的；諂媚的；奴隸的
example: All the king's subjects, fearing his wrath, often acted quite servile.

definition: to restrain or limit; to put chains on; a metal fetter; a restraint
chinese: v. 束縛；阻礙；給戴上鐐銬；n. 鐐銬；束縛
example: Let's shackle your feet with silver fetters.

definition: the darkening of areas in a drawing to show depth; a slight variation or difference
chinese: （繪畫）明暗；陰影；細微差別
example: Sponge absorbs water so it is convenient for shading water-colours and such.

definition: a dark area cast by an object blocking light; gloom; a slight trace; to follow secretly; to overshadow or darken
chinese: n. 影子；陰影；陰霾；一絲；v. 跟蹤；遮蔽；使蒙上陰影
example: Lorenzo noticed through the corner of his eye a black shadow in the corner.

definition: a thing that is not what it is claimed to be; a fake; false or pretended; to pretend
chinese: n. 假象；騙局；冒充者；adj. 虛假的；v. 假裝
example: With all its sham, drudgery and broken dreams; it is still a beautiful world.

definition: an electric razor; a person who shaves; a young boy
chinese: 電動刮鬍刀；剃刀；（口）小伙子
example: It certainly feels smooth when you run the shaver over your skin.

definition: lacking ambition or initiative; lazy
chinese: 胸無大志的；懶散的；無能的
example: Giving a scholarship to that ignorant, shiftless student is an injustice.

definition: appearing deceitful or evasive; untrustworthy
chinese: 詭詐的；不可靠的；（眼神）閃爍的
example: It was an odious face—crafty, vicious, malignant, with shifty, light-grey eyes and white lashes.

definition: orderly and neat
chinese: 井然有序的；整潔的
example: The passage describes its subject as shipshape, meaning of places; characterized by order and neatness; free from disorder.

definition: to avoid or neglect (a duty or responsibility)
chinese: 逃避；推卸（責任）；規避
example: A father shouldn't shirk his responsibilities to his children.

definition: an area of shallow water; a sandbank; a large group of fish; shallow; to become shallow; to form schools
chinese: n. 淺灘；沙洲；魚群；adj. 淺的；v. 變淺；成群游動
example: If there is a shoal or a stone under water again, it should indicate them on the map.

definition: stale from overuse; trite; (of goods) faded or damaged from being on display
chinese: 陳腐的；老套的；（商品）因陳列而舊損的
example: The passage describes its subject as shopworn, meaning worn or faded from being on display in a store.

definition: to exhibit or display favorably; a setting for displaying something to advantage; a glass display case
chinese: v. 展示；展現（優點）；n. 展示的場合；陳列櫃
example: Benedito's salad is a great way to showcase seasonal produce.

definition: skill in presenting things in an entertaining or dramatic way
chinese: 表演技巧；作秀的本領；展示才能
example: In this context, “showmanship” refers to the ability to present something (especially theatrical shows) in an attractive manner.

definition: a very small amount; a strip torn or cut off; to tear or cut into strips; to destroy completely
chinese: n. 少量；一點點；碎片；v. 撕碎；切絲；徹底摧毀
example: Algeria needs to shred the entire socialist fabric and replace it with a capitalist model.

definition: having sharp powers of judgment; astute
chinese: 精明的；敏銳的；機靈的
example: The goldsmith was shrewd and cunning, and knew full well what kind of bird it was.

definition: to become smaller in size or amount; to draw back or recoil; a psychiatrist
chinese: v. 縮小；減少；退縮；畏縮；n. （口）精神科醫師
example: Regular use of citrus fruit will shrink pores and make the skin feel fresh.

definition: to cover or conceal; to envelop; a cloth for wrapping a corpse; something that conceals
chinese: v. 遮蔽；籠罩；隱藏；n. 裹屍布；遮蔽物
example: He is surrounded by a shroud of mourning.

definition: to raise the shoulders to show indifference; to dismiss as unimportant (shrug off); an act of shrugging
chinese: v. 聳肩；不予理會；n. 聳肩
example: She gave a shrug of the shoulders.

definition: to persistently avoid, ignore, or reject
chinese: 迴避；避開；排斥
