definition: to avoid dealing with or complying with; to step aside to avoid
chinese: 迴避（問題）；規避；側步閃開
example: He attempted to sidestep a conflict with his chief.

definition: to examine thoroughly; to separate out the useful parts; to pass through a sieve
chinese: 詳細審查；篩選；過濾；篩
example: If you sift through barrels of dirt, you may eventually find a flake of gold.

definition: notable or outstanding; a sign or gesture conveying information; an indication; to indicate or convey by a sign
chinese: adj. 顯著的；非凡的；n. 信號；訊號；跡象；v. 示意；表明；發信號
example: Some scientists believe the origin of this oscillating signal to be a neutron star.

definition: important or notable in effect; large enough to be noticed; having a special or hidden meaning
chinese: 重大的；顯著的；有意義的；意味深長的
example: a significant change in tax laws

definition: resembling without being identical
chinese: 相似的；類似的
example: similar food at similar prices

definition: a figure of speech comparing two unlike things using "like" or "as"
chinese: 明喻
example: A simile is like a bridge.

definition: a foolish person lacking common sense
chinese: 笨蛋；傻子；頭腦簡單的人
example: Based on the way he formulated his arguments, one could tell that he was a simpleton.

definition: to imitate the appearance or conditions of; to model; to pretend to feel or have
chinese: 模擬；仿造；假裝
example: An aviary is a large enclosure for birds, often containing shrubbery and other plants to simulate their natural habitat.

definition: occurring or operating at the same time
chinese: 同時的；同時發生的
example: The earth experiences four simultaneous 24-hour days in a single rotation.

definition: a position requiring little or no work but giving pay or status; a church benefice without duties
chinese: 閒差；掛名職位；（無牧職的）聖俸
example: In this context, “sinecure” refers to a benefice to which no spiritual or pastoral duties are attached.

definition: a tendon; strength or power; the chief supports or resources (of something)
chinese: 肌腱；力量；支柱；資源
example: And when he saw that he could not overcome him, he touched the sinew of his thigh, and forthwith it shrank.

definition: to burn the surface or ends of lightly; a superficial burn
chinese: v. 燒焦（表面）；燎；n. 輕微燒焦
example: If you run through a crowd with the torch of truth you will singe a few beards.

definition: threatening or suggesting evil; ominous; (heraldry) on the left side
chinese: 險惡的；不祥的；陰險的；（紋章）左側的
example: Nothing sinister has turned up in clinical trials so far, but there are still unknowns.

definition: having many curves and turns; moving with graceful, flowing motion
chinese: 蜿蜒的；彎曲的；柔美靈活的
example: A sinuous melody rose from the violin, weaving through the orchestra's harmonies.

definition: to drink in small mouthfuls; a small mouthful of liquid
chinese: v. 啜飲；小口喝；n. 一小口
example: After taking a sip of his water bottle, he dove into his work.

definition: a device making a loud warning sound; a mythical sea creature luring sailors with song; a dangerously alluring woman
chinese: 警報器；汽笛；（神話）海妖；妖婦
example: Odysseus ordered his crew to plug their ears so they would not hear the Siren's fatal song

definition: to spend or use less than necessary; to do hastily or carelessly
chinese: 吝於花費；偷工減料；過度節省
example: The company decided to skimp on the quality of its products to boost the profit margin.

definition: to avoid dealing with; to go around the edge of; a garment hanging from the waist; an edge or border
chinese: v. 迴避（問題）；繞過；沿邊緣走；n. 裙子；邊緣
example: For her fifties outfit she opted for a pencil skirt and a spotted blouse.

definition: easily frightened; nervous; unpredictable or fickle; playfully frivolous
chinese: 易受驚的；膽怯的；反覆無常的；輕佻的
example: Partridges seem to be very skittish.

definition: underhanded or unscrupulous behavior; trickery
chinese: 欺詐；詭計；不正當手段
example: This kind of partisan skulduggery has no place in a government agency.

definition: underhanded or unscrupulous behavior; trickery
chinese: 欺詐；詭計；不正當手段
example: In this context, “skullduggery” refers to verbal misrepresentation intended to take advantage of you in some way.

definition: not taut; careless or lazy; (of business) slow; to be lazy or idle (slack off); the loose part of a rope; spare capacity
chinese: adj. 鬆弛的；懈怠的；疏忽的；（生意）蕭條的；v. 懈怠；偷懶；n. 鬆弛部分；餘裕
example: It is important that no one is allowed to slack off on their assigned work.

definition: to quench (thirst); to satisfy (a desire); to calm; to combine (lime) with water
chinese: 解（渴）；滿足（慾望）；平息；（化學）熟化（石灰）
example: If only he had some water with which to slake his thirst!

definition: a false spoken statement damaging a person's reputation; to make such statements about
chinese: n. 誹謗；詆毀；v. 誹謗；中傷
example: You have the right to free speech, but not the right to slander.

definition: a particular point of view or bias; a slope; to present with a bias; to slope
chinese: n. 觀點；傾向；偏見；傾斜；v. 使有偏向；傾斜
example: The paper's editorial staff traditionally has had a conservative slant.

definition: done too hurriedly and carelessly
chinese: 草率的；馬虎的；粗製濫造的
example: The office building had been constructed in a slapdash manner, so it did not surprise officials when, during a small earthquake, a large crack emerged on the façade of the building.

definition: to schedule or plan; to nominate; (British) to criticize severely; a slab of rock; a list of candidates
chinese: v. 預定；安排；提名；（英）痛批；n. 石板；候選人名單
example: At the beginning of a new year, some people like to start with a clean slate.

definition: to kill violently; to greatly impress or amuse
chinese: 殺害；殘殺；（口）使傾倒
example: Sometimes you have to slay a few dragons to get to the princess.

definition: sordid or corrupt; squalid and seedy; (of cloth) flimsy and thin
chinese: 低俗的；不正派的；骯髒破舊的；（布料）薄而劣質的
example: the coat has a sleazy lining

definition: elegant and streamlined; smooth and glossy; suave; to make smooth
chinese: adj. 時髦流線型的；光滑的；圓滑的；v. 使光滑
example: Not only is the new smartphone sleek and stylish, but it also boasts impressive performance.

definition: gracefully thin; long and narrow; small or meager
chinese: 苗條的；細長的；微薄的；不足的
example: she was slender as a willow shoot is slender

definition: a large number or amount; to turn or slide violently
chinese: n. 大量；許多；v. 使急轉；猛轉
example: A slew of corporate logos adorned the entrance to the soccer match.

definition: small in degree; slim; to insult by treating with disregard; an insult caused by disregard
chinese: adj. 輕微的；微小的；纖細的；v. 輕視；怠慢；忽視；n. 輕蔑；怠慢
example: It's a very dangerous sport, where a slight mistake can lead to serious injury.

definition: to throw; to hang or carry loosely; a support for an injured arm; a strap for lifting; a slingshot
chinese: v. 投擲；吊起；懸掛；n. 吊帶；吊索；投石器
example: It'll be difficult to do that with your arm in a sling.

definition: difficult to hold or stand on; evasive or untrustworthy; not precise in meaning
chinese: 滑的；難以捉摸的；不可靠的；（定義）含混的
example: Patricia's car skidded on a slippery spot on the road and spun completely around twice.

definition: characterized by a lack of care or thoroughness; careless
chinese: 草率的；馬虎的；不嚴謹的
example: The passage describes its subject as slipshod, meaning marked by great carelessness.

definition: careless and lacking in care or precision; untidy; (of clothes) loose-fitting
chinese: 草率的；馬虎的；邋遢的；（衣服）寬鬆的
example: Whether it's national economics, family economics, or personal economics, it's not something where sloppy accounting is good enough.

definition: reluctance to work or make an effort; laziness; a slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal
chinese: 怠惰；懶惰；（動物）樹懶
example: A sloth must conserve its energy because it eats a low-calorie diet of leaves.

definition: disinclined to work or exertion; lazy
chinese: 怠惰的；懶散的
example: The passage describes its subject as slothful, meaning disinclined to work or exertion.

definition: a lazy or incompetent person (often 'no slouch'); a drooping posture; to sit, stand, or move in a lazy, drooping way
chinese: n. 懶散的人；無精打采的姿勢；v. 無精打采地坐著；垂肩彎腰
example: I'm no slouch on the dance floor.

definition: untidy in appearance; careless and slipshod in work
chinese: 邋遢的；不整潔的；草率的
example: As to his daily life, he is very slovenly.

definition: a lazy, habitually inactive person
chinese: 懶人；懶漢
example: In this context, “sluggard” refers to an idle slothful person.

definition: slow-moving or inactive; (of an economy) not performing well; lacking energy
chinese: 遲緩的；不景氣的；懶散的
example: The president wants to jump-start the sluggish economy by lowering taxes.

definition: sleep; a state of inactivity or dormancy; to sleep
chinese: n. 睡眠；沉睡；蟄伏；v. 睡眠；沉睡
example: 'Twas now the time, when on tired mortals crept / first slumber, sweetest that celestials pour.

definition: a sudden severe fall in prices or activity; a decline; to fall suddenly; to sit or fall heavily
chinese: n. 暴跌；不景氣；衰退；v. 暴跌；驟降；頹然坐下
example: Many people will lose their jobs due to the slump in the auto industry.

definition: to speak indistinctly; to disparage; to gloss over; an insulting or disparaging remark
chinese: v. 含糊地說；詆毀；含糊帶過；n. 誹謗；侮辱
example: My uncle would always slur his words when he had had too much to drink.

definition: cunning and deceitful; knowing or insinuating; on the sly: secretly
chinese: 狡猾的；詭詐的；會意的；狡黠的
example: He was seen having a piece of cake on the sly.

definition: ingratiating and insincere in a smug, oily way
chinese: 虛情假意的；諂媚的；油腔滑調的
example: He was so sarcastic and smarmy that it was unprofessional.

definition: clever and shrewd; stylish and neat; quick; to feel a sharp stinging pain; to feel hurt
chinese: adj. 聰明的；精明的；時髦的；敏捷的；v. 刺痛；感到傷心
example: She asked him where he lived, but he was too smart to tell her.

definition: a slight, superficial knowledge of something; a small amount
chinese: 一知半解；粗淺的知識；少量
example: In this context, “smattering” refers to a slight or superficial understanding of a subject.

definition: to smile in a smug or conceited way; a smug, self-satisfied smile
chinese: v. 得意地笑；假笑；n. 得意的笑；假笑
example: He left with a smirk on his face, leaving the two lovebirds alone.

definition: to extinguish a fire by covering it; to suffocate; to suppress feelings; to cover thickly
chinese: 悶熄；使窒息；抑制；壓制；覆蓋
example: They planned to smother the flames quickly to prevent further damage.

definition: excessively pleased with oneself; complacent
chinese: 自鳴得意的；自滿的
example: I think that things like animal rights are really just humanity being smug.

definition: the illegal import or export of goods
chinese: 走私；私運
example: Examples in smuggling include suitcases with false bottoms for hiding contraband.

definition: an unexpected obstacle or drawback; to catch or tear on something; to get or obtain quickly
chinese: n. 意外障礙；隱患；v. 鉤住；扯破；搶得
example: A last-minute snag forced the cancellation of a prisoner swap.

definition: a trap for catching animals; something that entangles; to catch in a trap; to entrap
chinese: n. 陷阱；圈套；v. 誘捕；使陷入
example: A fox is not caught twice in the same snare.

definition: a tangle or confused situation; a growl; to make tangled or jammed; to growl angrily
chinese: n. 混亂；糾結；咆哮；v. 使混亂；糾纏；咆哮
example: A colorful bike share revolution is taking over on the streets, helping ease traffic snarl and keeping the air cleaner.

definition: to smile or speak scornfully; a contemptuous expression or remark
chinese: v. 冷笑；嘲笑；n. 冷笑；嘲笑
example: He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer.

definition: expressing contempt or scorn
chinese: 輕蔑的；嘲笑的
example: He turned to his orange juice sullenly, sneering that every little additive would sign him up for experiments he wanted no part in.

definition: a person who looks down on those regarded as socially or intellectually inferior
chinese: 勢利的人；自命不凡者
example: I don't know why she believes him to be a snob.

definition: the attitude of condescending to people of lower status
chinese: 勢利；諂上欺下；自命不凡
example: In this context, “snobbery” refers to the trait of condescending to those of lower social status.

definition: having an air of superiority; condescending to those of lower status
chinese: 勢利的；自命不凡的
example: It was a snobbish club full of preppy airheads.

definition: to rebuff or ignore disdainfully; to reject; an act of rebuffing or ignoring someone
chinese: v. 冷落；怠慢；拒絕；n. 冷落；怠慢

definition: deprived of courage and strength; upset and nervous

example: the steeplejack, exhausted and unnerved, couldn't hold on to his dangerous perch much longer

definition: not conspicuous or undesirably noticeable; modest and quiet
chinese: 不引人注目的；不張揚的；低調的
example: a quiet, unobtrusive life of self-denial

definition: causing discomfort or displeasure; disagreeable; unfriendly or rude
chinese: 令人不快的；討厭的；不友善的
example: an unpleasant personality

definition: never done or known before; having no precedent; novel
chinese: 空前的；前所未有的；史無前例的
example: an unprecedented expansion in population and industry

definition: not planned or thought out in advance; spontaneous
chinese: 非預謀的；臨時起意的；即興的
example: asked an unpremeditated question

definition: not trying to impress; modest; simple and natural
chinese: 樸實的；不炫耀的；謙遜的；不做作的
example: His life story is, in point of fact, vastly more complex and many-sided than the following handful of unpretentious and unoriginal pages suggest.

definition: not favorable; unlikely to lead to success; inauspicious
chinese: 不利的；不吉利的；不順遂的
example: The passage describes its subject as unpropitious, meaning not propitious.

definition: never relaxing or stopping; incessant; persistent
chinese: 不間斷的；持續的；不懈的
example: The unremitting noise was too much.

definition: difficult to control or discipline; disorderly
chinese: 難駕馭的；不守規矩的；任性的
example: The mediator asked the unruly members of the audience to stop hectoring the speaker.

definition: not injured or harmed
chinese: 毫髮無傷的；未受損的
example: Miraculously, he guided the full team of oxen through the raging river, unscathed.

definition: not proper or appropriate; not in keeping with accepted standards of conduct
chinese: 不得體的；不適宜的；不合禮節的
example: It would be unseemly to remarry the day after the divorce becomes final.

definition: to disturb the composure of; to make unstable or disordered
chinese: 使不安；擾亂；使動搖
example: The debate was full of gamesmanship, with each candidate trying to unsettle the other.

definition: unpleasant to look at; ugly
chinese: 難看的；不雅觀的；醜陋的
example: unsightly billboards

definition: based on faulty reasoning; not in good condition or decayed; not firm or secure; (of mind) not sane
chinese: 站不住腳的；謬誤的；不健全的；不牢固的；（精神）不正常的
example: an unsound foundation

definition: given freely and generously; not holding back
chinese: 慷慨的；毫不吝惜的；不遺餘力的
example: After his change of heart, the former miser became unstinting in his generosity to the poor.

definition: not celebrated or praised; unrecognized
chinese: 默默無聞的；未受讚揚的；被埋沒的
example: The volunteer firefighters are the real unsung heroes in this situation.

definition: not able to be defended or justified; (of a situation) not able to be maintained; (of a position) not able to be held
chinese: 站不住腳的；無法辯護的；難以維持的；（陣地）守不住的
example: This is an untenable point of view.

definition: too many or too great to be counted or measured; not told or revealed
chinese: 數不清的；極大的；未說出的
example: Words alone cannot convey the untold misery endured by people in these refugee camps.

definition: unexpected and inappropriate or inconvenient; unfavorable; unfortunate; (archaic) hard to control
chinese: 不恰當的；意外的；不利的；不幸的；難駕馭的
example: Some professors find teaching untoward as having to prepare for lectures and conduct office hours prevents them from focusing on attaining tenure.

definition: not yet tested or proved; inexperienced; (of a case) not yet tried in court
chinese: 未經試驗的；缺乏經驗的；（法律）未經審訊的
example: The impossible is often the untried.

definition: hard to handle or use because of size, weight, or shape; (of a system) too large or complex to manage efficiently
chinese: 笨重的；難操作的；難以管理的
example: we set about towing the unwieldy structure into the shelter

definition: not ready or willing to do something; reluctant
chinese: 不願意的；勉強的
example: unwilling to face facts

definition: not aware of the full facts; unintentional
chinese: 不知情的；無意的；未察覺的
example: She played an unwitting part in this operation.

definition: without knowledge or awareness; unintentionally
chinese: 不知情地；無意地；不知不覺地
example: he unwittingly deleted the references

definition: not habitual or ordinary; unusual; unaccustomed
chinese: 不尋常的；罕見的；不習慣的
example: The passage describes its subject as unwonted, meaning out of the ordinary.

definition: cheerful and optimistic; an unaccented beat in music
chinese: adj. 樂觀的；歡快的；n. （音樂）弱拍
example: You should try to look at the world in a more upbeat way.

definition: to reproach or scold severely
chinese: 嚴厲斥責；責罵
example: Bob took a risk walking into the “Students Barbershop”—in the end he had to upbraid the apparently hung over barber for giving him and uneven bowl cut.

definition: a sudden violent change or disruption; an upward movement of the earth's crust
chinese: 劇變；動亂；（地殼）隆起
example: The country was in a state of upheaval.

definition: to support or maintain (a principle or law); to confirm (a decision) on appeal; to keep up
chinese: 維護；支持；（法院）維持原判；堅持
example: Loyalty to an ideal is sometimes harder to uphold than loyalty to a person.

definition: moral integrity; honesty; the state of being erect
chinese: 正直；誠實；直立
example: In this context, “uprightness” refers to righteousness as a consequence of being honorable and honest.

definition: courteous and refined in manner; polite; suave and sophisticated
chinese: 溫文儒雅的；彬彬有禮的；老練世故的
example: The tall, dark and classically handsome actor was the epitome of urbane sophistication.

definition: requiring immediate action; pressing; persistent in asking
chinese: 緊急的；迫切的；一再要求的
example: Hers was a nervous disease, and a change of air was an urgent need.

definition: capable of being used; fit for use
chinese: 可用的；能使用的
example: usable byproducts

definition: to guide or escort; (usher in) to mark the start of; a person who shows people to their seats
chinese: v. 引領；開創；n. 引座員；接待員
example: Recent advances in medicine will usher in a new age in medical care.

definition: to seize power or position without legal right; to take over wrongfully
chinese: 篡奪；篡位；侵占
example: With the heirless king going crazy and royal family poisoned, the general of the army finally had his chance to usurp the throne.

definition: designed to be useful rather than attractive; of utilitarianism; a believer in utilitarianism
chinese: adj. 實用的；功利的；功利主義的；n. 功利主義者
example: utilitarian steel tables

definition: not occupied; (of a post) unfilled; showing no thought or expression; empty
chinese: 空著的；空缺的；茫然的；空虛的
example: the throne is never vacant

definition: to give a vaccine to in order to produce immunity
chinese: 接種疫苗；預防接種
example: Other people's bodies are infringed upon by your decision not to vaccinate.

definition: to alternate between opinions or choices; to waver; to sway back and forth
chinese: 猶豫不決；搖擺不定；擺動
example: The council continued to vacillate between the two proposals.

definition: lacking thought or intelligence; mindless; blank in expression; empty
chinese: 空洞的；愚蠢的；茫然的；空的
example: I do not like his inflated poetry or his vacuous comments on literature.

definition: an unpredictable or erratic change; a whimsical idea or action
chinese: 變幻莫測；反覆無常；奇想
example: In this context, “vagary” refers to an unexpected and inexplicable change in something (in a situation or a person's behavior, etc.).

definition: not clearly expressed; lacking definite shape; uncertain; (of a person) absent-minded
chinese: 含糊的；不明確的；模糊的；（人）茫然的
example: The moon, veiled by the clouds, illuminated the countryside with a glimmer, equal and vague.

definition: excessively proud of oneself; conceited; producing no result; futile (in vain: without success)
chinese: 自負的；愛虛榮的；徒然的；無效的
example: The old lady will often wait for her son in vain at the station.

definition: excessively proud and boastful; conceited
chinese: 自負的；虛榮的；自吹自擂的
example: The passage describes its subject as vainglorious, meaning feeling self-importance.

definition: the act of saying farewell; a farewell speech or statement
chinese: 告別；告別辭；告別演說
example: His inauguration speech will be effectively a valediction to our hopes.

definition: showing courage or determination; brave; (of an effort) admirable though unsuccessful
chinese: 英勇的；勇敢的；（努力）可嘉的
example: However, he did not cease from continuing his way; a young prince in search of glory is ever valiant.

definition: to check or prove the accuracy of; to make legally valid; to affirm the worth of
chinese: 證實；確認；使生效；認可
example: Users validate the accuracy of donated clips, checking that the speaker read the sentence correctly.

definition: to praise or give value to; to enhance the status of; to fix the price of (a commodity)
chinese: 推崇；頌揚；賦予價值；（經濟）穩定價格
example: The museum's new exhibition seeks to valorize overlooked local artists.

definition: having or showing valor; brave
chinese: 英勇的；勇敢的
example: The passage describes its subject as valorous, meaning having or showing valor.

definition: excessive pride in oneself; conceit; emptiness or futility; a dressing table
chinese: 虛榮心；自負；空虛；徒勞；梳妝臺
example: Laughter is the only cure against vanity, and vanity is the only laughable fault.

definition: to defeat thoroughly; to conquer; to overcome
chinese: 擊敗；征服；克服
example: We must vanquish our enemies.

definition: a position giving a good view or advantage; superiority; a point of view
chinese: 有利位置；優勢；觀點
example: The caves are situated on a hilltop and provide an excellent vantage point.

definition: lacking interest or substance; dull; lifeless
chinese: 乏味的；空洞的；無生氣的
example: I am too easily distracted by numerous forms of vapid entertainment to ever amount to anything.

definition: to turn into vapor; to disappear suddenly; to destroy completely
chinese: 汽化；蒸發；消失；消滅
example: The increase in support did not vaporize on polling day itself.

definition: the quality of being subject to variation; lack of consistency
chinese: 變異性；易變性；可變性
example: Herbal supplements sold in drugstores have poor quality control and high content variability.

definition: disagreement or discrepancy (at variance); the degree of difference; (statistics) a measure of spread; an official exemption from a regulation
chinese: 不一致；分歧；差異；（統計）變異數；（法規）特許變更
example: A random variable is definitely a constant if the variance is zero.

definition: marked with patches of different colors; varied
chinese: 雜色的；斑駁的；多樣的
example: My favorite hostas are the variegated ones, with dark green and yellow-green leaves.

definition: the quality of being diverse; an assortment or kind; a subspecies or cultivated form; entertainment of varied acts
chinese: 多樣性；種類；（生物）變種；綜藝表演
example: On a barge, floating on a river, a variety of crops are being nurtured.

definition: to gloss over or disguise (something unpleasant); to coat with varnish; a liquid giving a hard glossy finish; nail polish
chinese: v. 粉飾；掩飾；塗清漆；n. 清漆；亮光漆；指甲油
example: What colour nail varnish goes with this yellow dress?

definition: to boast about or praise excessively; a boast
chinese: v. 吹噓；誇耀；n. 自誇
example: In this context, “vaunt” means extravagant self-praise.

definition: to change direction suddenly; to shift in opinion, subject, or course
chinese: 突然轉向；改變方向；（意見或話題）轉變
example: You shouldn't veer off from the focus.

definition: showing strong feeling; forceful; passionate
chinese: 激烈的；強烈的；熱烈的
example: He pronounced his judgment over such vehement behaviour.

definition: to conceal or disguise; to cover with a veil; a piece of fabric covering the face; something that conceals
chinese: v. 掩飾；遮蓋；以面紗遮住；n. 面紗；遮蔽物；幌子
example: women in Afghanistan veil their faces

definition: open to bribery; corrupt; mercenary
chinese: 貪腐的；可收買的；受賄的
example: Can someone explain to me why a venal judge was appointed?

definition: the quality of being open to bribery; corrupt use of office or talent for gain
chinese: 貪腐；受賄；唯利是圖
example: If our legal system becomes plagued with venality, then the very notion of justice is imperiled.

definition: a person who sells goods, especially on the street; a supplier; the seller in a transaction
chinese: 小販；攤販；供應商；（法律）賣方
example: The ice cream vendor is waiting on customers at his outdoor stand.

definition: a superficial attractive appearance hiding something; a thin decorative layer of wood; to disguise; to cover with a veneer
chinese: n. 虛飾；外表；（木材）薄板；貼面；v. 掩飾；貼薄板
example: The veneer we call civilisation is only skin deep.

definition: to regard with deep respect; to revere
chinese: 尊敬；崇敬；崇拜
example: We dishonor the living and venerate the dead.

definition: a feeling of profound respect; reverence; worship
chinese: 崇敬；尊敬；崇拜
example: His ideas were more fierce and free; and he contemned many of the opinions which had been inculcated upon her as chiefly demanding her veneration.

definition: the act of inflicting harm in return for a wrong; revenge
chinese: 報復；復仇
example: Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord

definition: easily excused or forgiven; minor; (of a sin) not mortal
chinese: 可原諒的；輕微的；（宗教）可寬恕的
example: The passage describes its subject as venial, meaning warranting only temporal punishment.

definition: extreme spite or malice; poisonous fluid secreted by animals such as snakes
chinese: 惡意；怨恨；（蛇等）毒液
example: The spikes on a stonefish's fins contain glands that inject neurotoxic and cytotoxic venom.

definition: the place where an event is held; (law) the place where a case is tried
chinese: 場地；會場；（法律）審判地
example: Intoxicated patrons will be asked to leave the venue to comply with the house policy.

definition: habitually truthful; honest; accurate
chinese: 誠實的；說實話的；真實的
example: The panel considered her a careful and veracious witness.

definition: habitual truthfulness; conformity to facts; accuracy
chinese: 誠實；真實性；準確性
example: After years of political scandals, the congressman was hardly known for his veracity; yet despite this distrust, he was voted into yet another term.

definition: in exactly the same words; word for word
chinese: adv. 逐字地；一字不差地；adj. 逐字的
example: For accurate study results questions must be asked verbatim.

definition: an excess of words; wordiness; manner of expression
chinese: 冗詞；廢話；措辭
example: The esoteric verbiage of her email left him scratching his head and getting splinters.

definition: using more words than necessary; wordy
chinese: 冗長的；囉唆的；用詞過多的
example: Sven was so verbose that his friends resorted to calling him a chatterbox.

definition: green with vegetation; lush; (of a person) inexperienced
chinese: 翠綠的；青翠的；鬱鬱蔥蔥的；（人）生澀的
example: Five thousand years ago, everything here was verdant and flourishing; today, it is desert.

definition: the decision of a jury on a case; a judgment or conclusion; an opinion
chinese: 判決；裁決；結論；意見
example: Before they even began deliberations, many of the jury members had reached a verdict.

definition: proved or confirmed to be true
chinese: 已證實的；經查證的
example: a verified claim

definition: to establish the truth or accuracy of; to confirm; to check
chinese: 證實；查證；核實；驗證
example: To continue setting up your account, please verify that this is your email address.

definition: appearing to be true or real; plausible
chinese: 似真的；貌似真實的；逼真的
example: The passage describes its subject as verisimilar, meaning appearing to be true or real.

definition: the appearance or quality of seeming true or real
chinese: 逼真；擬真性；似真
example: It is interesting how this conspiracy theory author abandons all attempts at verisimilitude.

definition: truly so called; genuine (often used as an intensifier)
chinese: 名副其實的；十足的；真正的
example: Paganini dazzled his audience with (among other things) a veritable hailstorm of left-handed pizzicatos.

definition: small animals or insects that are harmful pests; contemptible or obnoxious people
chinese: 害蟲；害獸；敗類；歹徒
example: I believe that place is teeming with vermin.

definition: the everyday language of a region; nonstandard speech; jargon of a group; in the native language; (of architecture) in local, ordinary style
chinese: n. 方言；本地話；白話；行話；adj. 方言的；本地的；（建築）民間風格的
example: He uttered an incomprehensible oath in the local vernacular before going on his way.

definition: able to adapt to many activities or functions; having many uses
chinese: 多才多藝的；多用途的；用途廣泛的
example: The bonus travelog film is packaged in a splendid digital versatile disc.

definition: poetry; writing with metrical rhythm; a stanza; a numbered division of a Bible chapter; to make familiar (with)
chinese: n. 詩；韻文；詩節；（聖經）節；v. 使熟悉
example: I mostly write free verse, but I employ meter and rhyme from time to time.

definition: knowledgeable or skilled (in); experienced
chinese: 精通的；熟悉的；熟練的
example: As may be expected of an expert, he's well versed in the field.

definition: a sensation of whirling and loss of balance; dizziness
chinese: 眩暈；頭暈
example: He suffers from vertigo, he shouldn't climb trees.

definition: enthusiasm, energy, and vitality; spirit in artistic work
chinese: 活力；熱情；神韻
example: Her verve stayed with her well into her old age.

definition: a trace of something that no longer exists; the smallest amount; a degenerate organ
chinese: 遺跡；殘餘；痕跡；（生物）退化器官
example: This mousepad is a vestige of a bygone era.

definition: a person with long experience in a field; a former member of the armed forces; having long experience
chinese: n. 老手；資深人士；退伍軍人；老兵；adj. 經驗豐富的；資深的
example: Perhaps due to his experience of the team's vicissitudes, the long-time veteran was unperturbed.

definition: to reject (a proposal or law) officially; to forbid; the power or act of rejecting a decision
chinese: v. 否決；禁止；n. 否決權；否決
example: It is unclear whether he will sign the legislation or veto it, risking a congressional vote to override a veto.

definition: to annoy or irritate; to trouble or worry
chinese: 使惱怒；使煩惱；使苦惱
example: It is not right to vex ourselves at things, for they care nought about it.

definition: capable of working successfully; feasible; capable of living or developing
chinese: 可行的；能生存的；（胚胎）能存活的
example: Despite not thinking the project was viable, they decided to go ahead with it.

definition: to move rapidly back and forth; to quiver or throb; (of sound) to resonate; to thrill with emotion
chinese: 振動；顫動；（聲音）迴盪；激動
example: Tungsten is what makes cell phones vibrate, and tin is used in solder.

definition: experienced through another person's actions or feelings; done or suffered for another; delegated
chinese: 間接感受的；替代的；代理的
example: The passage describes its subject as vicarious, meaning experienced at secondhand.

definition: deliberately cruel or malicious; ferocious; violent; severe
chinese: 惡毒的；兇猛的；殘暴的；猛烈的
example: It was an odious face—crafty, vicious, malignant, with shifty, light-grey eyes and white lashes.

definition: a change of circumstances or fortune, typically unwelcome
chinese: 變遷；興衰；變化無常
example: In this context, “vicissitude” refers to a variation in circumstances or fortune at different times in your life or in the development of something.

definition: to single out for cruel or unjust treatment; to make a victim of; to cheat
chinese: 使受害；欺負；迫害；欺騙
example: Silent drones victimize more people.

definition: keeping careful watch for danger; alertly watchful
chinese: 警惕的；警覺的；警戒的
example: Benedito knew that he needed to be vigilant and protect his herd from predators.

definition: a brief evocative description or scene; a small decorative illustration; a photo with softly fading edges
chinese: 短篇描寫；片段；小插曲；（書刊）裝飾圖案；暈邊照片
example: A vignette is a short written description or a brief scene in a movie or play.

definition: physical or mental strength and energy; forcefulness; intensity
chinese: 活力；精力；力量；強度
example: The once-mighty empire had grown effete, bloated with luxury and devoid of vigor.

definition: full of energy; forceful; intense; strong and healthy
chinese: 精力旺盛的；強而有力的；激烈的；健壯的
example: Harold's arm bicycle workout was sufficiently vigorous that his pectorals burst into flame.

definition: morally despicable; wicked; extremely unpleasant; disgusting
chinese: 卑鄙的；可惡的；極壞的；令人作嘔的
example: He was a truly vile creature and the world is better without him.

definition: to speak or write about in an abusive, defamatory way; to slander
chinese: 詆毀；誹謗；中傷
example: It was an unwise decision to try to vilify the beloved singer.

definition: a wicked person; the bad character in a story; the person blamed for a problem
chinese: 壞人；惡棍；反派角色；罪魁禍首
example: If you're not the villain in someone's story then you're not doing much of anything.

definition: energy and enthusiasm
chinese: 活力；精力；熱情
example: The high percentage of oxygen makes people full of vim and vigor.

definition: to show to be right or justified; to clear of blame or suspicion; to confirm
chinese: 證明正確；為…平反；洗清（罪名）；證實
example: The findings vindicate warnings by local experts as to the poor quality of water in the nation’s capital.

definition: having or showing a strong desire for revenge; spiteful
chinese: 報復性的；懷恨在心的；有仇必報的
example: He became quite vindictive after his wife left him.

definition: of lasting quality; classic or old-fashioned in style; (of wine) of a good year; the year a wine was made; a season's grape harvest; the period something was made
chinese: adj. 經典的；復古的；（酒）上等年份的；n. 釀酒年份；葡萄收成；年代
example: The bathroom combines vintage subway tiles with satin brass fixtures for a timeless look.

definition: a domineering, violent, or scolding woman; (archaic) a heroic woman
chinese: 潑婦；悍婦；女中豪傑
example: Poor Billy was the victim of the virago’s invective—she railed at him for a good 30-minutes about how he is the scum of the earth for speaking loudly on his cellphone in public.

definition: moral excellence; a good quality; an advantage; effectiveness (by virtue of: because of)
chinese: 美德；德行；優點；功效
example: The first virtue of a painting is to be a feast for the eyes.

definition: great technical skill, especially in music or art
chinese: 精湛技藝；高超技巧
example: Virtuosity requires years of daily practice from childhood.

definition: a person highly skilled in music or another art; showing exceptional skill
chinese: n. 名家；大師；演奏能手；adj. 技藝精湛的；高超的
example: By his twenties, the young virtuoso had won international acclaim for his lyrical, powerful and disciplined artistry.

definition: having or showing high moral standards; righteous; (of a woman) chaste
chinese: 品德高尚的；正直的；有道德的；（女子）貞潔的
example: Nobody is born good, they have to learn how to be virtuous.

definition: extreme harmfulness; the capacity of a microorganism to cause disease; bitter hostility
chinese: 毒性；致病力；惡毒；敵意
example: the virulence of the plague

definition: bitterly hostile; extremely poisonous; (of a disease) severe and rapidly spreading; deadly
chinese: 惡毒的；充滿敵意的；劇毒的；（疾病）猛烈的；致命的
example: The virulent plague ravaged the whole planet, as many places became ghost towns.

definition: a tiny infectious agent that replicates inside living cells; a program that damages computer systems; a harmful influence
chinese: 病毒；（電腦）病毒；毒害
example: Scientists learned about community transmission of the virus from what happened on a cruise ship.

definition: sticky; glutinous; thick and adhesive
chinese: 黏的；黏性的；黏稠的
example: The passage describes its subject as viscid, meaning having the sticky properties of an adhesive.

definition: having a thick, sticky consistency between solid and liquid
chinese: 黏稠的；黏滯的；黏的
example: Condensed milk is more viscous than normal milk.

definition: able to be seen; apparent; obvious; prominent
chinese: 看得見的；明顯的；顯著的；引人注目的
example: a visible object

definition: thinking about the future with imagination and wisdom; idealistic and impractical; a person with original ideas; a dreamer
chinese: adj. 有遠見的；富有想像力的；空想的；不切實際的；n. 有遠見的人；空想家
example: William was a visionary leader who revolutionized the textile industry.

definition: a pleasing view, especially a long narrow one; a mental view of future possibilities
chinese: 景色；遠景；展望；前景
example: The street, lined with trees, provided a vista of the sea.

definition: absolutely necessary; essential; relating to life; full of energy
chinese: 極其重要的；必不可少的；生命的；充滿活力的
example: For a business owner, having a clear overview of one's entire business is vital.

definition: the state of being strong and active; energy; the power to live or endure
chinese: 活力；生命力；生機
example: It came back to life with even more vitality.

definition: to spoil or impair the quality of; to make legally invalid; to corrupt morally
chinese: 損害；削弱；使無效；使墮落
example: The chemical outflow from the factory threatened to vitiate the purity of the river's water.

definition: filled with bitter criticism or malice; scathing; of or like sulfuric acid
chinese: 尖酸刻薄的；惡毒的；（化學）硫酸的
example: The passage describes its subject as vitriolic, meaning harsh or corrosive in tone.

definition: to blame or insult in strong, abusive language
chinese: 辱罵；痛斥；謾罵
example: In this context, “vituperate” means spread negative information about.

definition: bitter and abusive language expressing blame or censure
chinese: 辱罵；謾罵；痛斥
example: In this context, “vituperation” refers to abusive or venomous language used to express blame or censure or bitter deep-seated ill will.

definition: attractively lively and animated
chinese: 活潑的；生氣勃勃的；快活的
example: The passage describes its subject as vivacious, meaning vigorous and animated.

definition: a strong feeling of suitability for a particular career; a person's occupation; a divine calling
chinese: 天職；使命感；職業；（宗教）神召
example: Never choose a vocation just because it permits the wearing of good clothes.

definition: vehement and loud in expressing opinions; clamorous
chinese: 大聲疾呼的；強烈表達的；喧嚷的
example: He's not the most convincing, just the most vociferous.

definition: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably; unstable; (of a substance) easily evaporated; (of a person) quick-tempered
chinese: 易變的；反覆無常的；動盪的；易揮發的；（脾氣）易怒的
example: Volatile aid and investment inflows have limited growth, and poverty remains high.

definition: the faculty or act of choosing by one's own will (of one's own volition: voluntarily)
chinese: 意志；自願；意志力
example: Despite my parents' preference, I have decided to attend an out-of-state college on my own volition.

definition: a simultaneous discharge of missiles; a burst of many things at once; (in sports) a ball hit before it bounces; to discharge together; to hit before it bounces
chinese: n. 齊射；連發；一連串；（球類）截擊；v. 齊發；截擊
example: The enemy fired a volley of shots at us.

definition: speaking fluently and at length; talkative
chinese: 健談的；口若懸河的；話多的
example: The normally quiet student became surprisingly voluble during the debate.

definition: great in quantity or volume; (of writing) lengthy or copious; (of clothing) loose and ample
chinese: 大量的；長篇的；著作多的；寬大的
example: The information the ancients didn’t have was very voluminous.

definition: done of one's own free will; unpaid; intentional; (of muscles) under conscious control
chinese: 自願的；志願的；自發的；故意的；（肌肉）隨意的
example: man is a voluntary agent

definition: devoted to sensual pleasure; (of a woman) curvaceous and attractive; luxurious
chinese: 沉溺酒色的；感官享樂的；豐滿性感的；奢華的
example: How many thousands who have drained the voluptuous bowl of pleasure to the dregs have been reclaimed by suffering!

definition: wanting great quantities of food; insatiable; very eager (e.g. a voracious reader)
chinese: 貪吃的；狼吞虎嚥的；求知若渴的；貪婪的
example: After skiing, I find that I have a voracious appetite.

definition: a devoted follower or admirer; a person bound by vows to religious service
chinese: 熱衷者；信徒；崇拜者；（宗教）立誓修道者
example: In this context, “votary” refers to one bound by vows to a religion or life of worship or service.

definition: to assert or guarantee the truth or reliability of (vouch for)
chinese: 擔保；保證；證明
example: I can give you a copy of the report, but I can't vouch for its accuracy.

definition: to grant or give graciously or condescendingly; to deign to reveal
chinese: 賜予；施予；屈尊答應；屈尊透露
example: In this context, “vouchsafe” means grant in a condescending manner.

definition: a solemn promise; a religious pledge; to promise solemnly
chinese: n. 誓言；誓約；許願；v. 發誓；立誓
example: The vow of a lover is not taken seriously.

definition: lacking refinement or taste; crude or obscene; of ordinary people; vernacular
chinese: 粗俗的；庸俗的；低俗的；通俗的
example: Arguments are extremely vulgar, for everyone in good society holds exactly the same opinion.

definition: exposed to being harmed or attacked; susceptible to physical or emotional injury
chinese: 易受傷害的；脆弱的；易受攻擊的；易受影響的
example: Felix realized how isolated and vulnerable he was to the dangers of the desert.

definition: to walk with short steps, swaying from side to side; a swaying walk
chinese: v. 搖搖擺擺地走；蹣跚而行；n. 蹣跚步態
example: Very fat people waddle when they walk, though few of them realize it.

definition: to speak or write vaguely and at length; to be indecisive; a crisp batter cake with a grid pattern; vague, wordy talk
chinese: v. 含糊其詞；胡扯；猶豫不決；n. 鬆餅；廢話
example: He doled out the waffle batter with a large soup spoon.

definition: to pass or carry gently through the air; a gentle current of air or scent
chinese: v. 飄蕩；飄送；n. 一陣（氣味）；飄蕩
example: In this context, “waft” means be driven or carried along, as by the air.

definition: to move quickly back and forth or up and down; a witty, joking person; a wagging movement
chinese: v. 擺動；搖動；n. 愛說笑的人；擺動
example: A friend in the wag is better than a penny in the purse.

definition: pale and sickly in appearance; faint or weak; (of a smile) strained
chinese: 蒼白的；病態的；無力的；（笑容）勉強的
example: Not sleeping for three days straight had left her puffy-eyed and wan.

definition: to decrease in strength or extent; to decline; (of the moon) to show decreasing illumination; a decline
chinese: v. 減弱；衰退；（月）虧；n. 衰退；減少
example: European immigration also began to wane in the 1930s because of the global depression.

definition: lacking or absent; not up to a required standard; without
chinese: adj. 不足的；欠缺的；未達標準的；prep. 缺少；沒有
example: She did not find her vocabulary wanting, yet there were so many GRE vocabulary words that inevitably she did not know a few.

definition: to sing with trills and embellishments; a warbling sound; a lump under an animal's hide caused by botfly larvae
chinese: v. 用顫音唱；（鳥）啁啾；n. 顫音；鳥鳴；（獸皮下）皮蠅瘤
example: In this context, “warble” refers to a lumpy abscess under the hide of domestic mammals caused by larvae of a botfly or warble fly.

definition: to prevent or keep away (something undesirable or harmful)
chinese: 避開；防止；擋開
example: Many squandered their money on charms and amulets, thinking that would ward off the pestilence.

definition: a person who advocates or tries to provoke war
chinese: 好戰者；戰爭販子
example: Kallas is a russophobic warmonger.

definition: to distort (meaning or judgment); to bend out of shape; the lengthwise threads on a loom; a distortion
chinese: v. 曲解；扭曲；（木材）翹曲；使變形；n. （織物）經紗；扭曲
example: Over time, wooden doors can warp or swell, making the door difficult to close.

definition: to justify or necessitate; to deserve; to guarantee; a legal document authorizing an action such as a search or arrest; justification
chinese: v. 使有正當理由；值得；保證；n. （法律）令狀；授權書；正當理由
example: A judge will issue a search warrant only if there is probable cause.

definition: cautious about possible dangers or problems; watchful
chinese: 謹慎的；小心的；警惕的；機警的
example: Benedito taught the kids to be wary of snakes and other dangerous animals.

definition: a person who wastes resources self-indulgently; a good-for-nothing
chinese: 揮霍者；敗家子；遊手好閒者
example: In this context, “wastrel” refers to someone who dissipates resources self-indulgently.

definition: a turning point; a ridge dividing areas drained by different rivers; a drainage basin
chinese: 分水嶺；轉捩點；（地理）流域
example: This is a watershed moment for the whole industry.

definition: to grow larger or stronger; (of the moon) to show increasing illumination; to become; to coat with wax; a soft substance used for candles
chinese: v. 增大；漸強；（月）漸圓；變得；上蠟；n. 蠟；蠟狀物
example: The flame flickered as it consumed the wax and the wick of the candle.

definition: to lie in wait for and attack; to intercept; to stop someone to talk
chinese: 埋伏；伏擊；攔截；攔住（談話）
example: The bandits hid along the forest road, ready to waylay any traveler who passed.

definition: difficult to control; following one's own wishes; erratic; unpredictable
chinese: 任性的；不服管束的；反覆無常的；難以捉摸的
example: The father had trouble communicating with his wayward son.

definition: to come safely through (a difficulty); to wear away by exposure; the state of the atmosphere
chinese: v. 安然度過；經受住；風化；n. 天氣；氣候
example: Madagascar is famous for its flora and fauna, as well as its inclement weather.

definition: a confused mass; turmoil; to roll or wallow; to be deeply involved
chinese: n. 混亂；雜亂的一團；v. 翻滾；沉溺
example: Without a word, he had disappeared into the welter of the noonday crowd.

definition: to persuade or obtain by flattery or coaxing
chinese: 哄騙；用甜言蜜語勸誘；騙取
example: I tried to wheedle him into telling me the answer.

definition: to stimulate (desire or interest); to sharpen (a blade)
chinese: 刺激；激起（食慾或興趣）；磨（刀）
example: Was the cliffhanger a downer or did it whet your appetite for more?

definition: playfully quaint or fanciful; odd; acting on whim; capricious
chinese: 古怪的；異想天開的；奇特有趣的；反覆無常的
example: She shaped the cake into a whimsical design.

definition: an odd or fanciful idea; playfully quaint humor; capriciousness
chinese: 奇想；怪念頭；古怪幽默；反覆無常
example: In this context, “whimsy” refers to an odd or fanciful or capricious idea.

definition: promoting physical health; morally good; sound and beneficial
chinese: 有益健康的；有益身心的；健全的；（道德）健康的
example: All people shall have the right to maintain the minimum standards of wholesome and cultured living.

definition: morally bad; evil; harmful or nasty; mischievous; (slang) excellent
chinese: 邪惡的；缺德的；惡劣的；淘氣的；（俚）極好的
example: The labour of the righteous tendeth to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.

definition: found or distributed over a large area or among many people
chinese: 普遍的；廣泛的；分布廣的
example: a widespread doctrine

definition: deliberate; intentional; obstinately self-willed; headstrong
chinese: 故意的；蓄意的；任性的；固執的
example: Your willful disobedience is what got you here.

definition: the trait of being headstrong and prone to disobedience; deliberateness
chinese: 任性；固執；故意
example: In this context, “willfulness” refers to the trait of being prone to disobedience and lack of discipline.

definition: haphazardly, without plan or order; whether one likes it or not
chinese: 隨意地；胡亂地；不管願不願意
example: The 'jump' action in this game is context-sensitive, so you can't jump willy-nilly.

definition: (of a plant) to droop; to become limp; to lose energy or vigor; (archaic) second-person singular of will
chinese: 枯萎；凋謝；萎靡不振；（古）將
example: Thou wilt come to the brawling stream, not falsely named.

definition: skilled at gaining advantage by deception; cunning; crafty
chinese: 狡猾的；詭計多端的；老謀深算的
example: He plays a wily detective with a penchant for disguises.

definition: to make a pained expression or flinch from pain or distress; a sudden pained grimace
chinese: v. 皺眉蹙額；畏縮；退縮；n. 皺眉；畏縮
example: Meanwhile, house parties and bar nights in college towns across the country are sparking outbreaks that make public health officials wince.

definition: a person who talks at length but says little of value
chinese: 誇誇其談的人；空談者；話匣子
example: The community pastor wasn't a fiery preacher, but rather a talkative windbag and bore.

definition: an unexpected gain or advantage; a piece of fruit blown down by the wind
chinese: 意外之財；意外收穫；被風吹落的果實
example: The unexpected windfall has put my brother and his wife on easy street.

definition: having repeated turns and bends; the act of winding; a coil of wire
chinese: adj. 蜿蜒的；曲折的；n. 纏繞；（電）線圈
example: This part of town is a veritable labyrinth of winding streets and small squares.

definition: using many words but saying little; verbose; characterized by much wind
chinese: 冗長空洞的；多話的；多風的；颳風的
example: When it's windy, the leaves of the old oak rustle and its branches creak.

definition: to sift and separate the valuable from the worthless; to narrow down; to blow chaff from grain
chinese: 篩選；過濾；精簡；揚（穀）
example: I can play well on the pipe, I can prune vines, I can dig, I can plant, I can plough, and I can winnow.

definition: attractive or appealing in a charming, innocent way
chinese: 迷人的；討人喜歡的；可愛的
example: How could you dislike that winsome smile?

definition: to tap a telephone line to secretly listen; an act or device for secret listening
chinese: v. 竊聽；搭線監聽；n. 竊聽；竊聽器
example: The wiretap was discontinued in 2016 due to a lack of evidence uncovered, but was re-started under a new warrant later that year and continued at least into early 2017.

definition: having or showing a feeling of vague or regretful longing
chinese: 惆悵的；渴望的；懷念的；若有所思的
example: Her wistful smile belied the sadness she felt at having to leave.

definition: quick, clever humor; intelligence; mental sharpness (wits); a witty person
chinese: 機智；風趣；才智；智力；才子
example: An ounce of wit that is bought is worse a pound that is taught.

definition: to remove or take back; to retreat; to stop taking part; to take money from an account; to retreat socially
chinese: 撤回；撤退；退出；提領（存款）；離群退縮
example: Participants must have the freedom to withdraw from a study at any time.

definition: to dry up and shrivel; to decline or fade; to humiliate with scorn
chinese: 枯萎；凋謝；衰退；使難堪
example: A mystery disease caused the grapes to wither on the vine.

definition: to refuse to give; to hold back; to restrain; to deduct (tax) at source
chinese: 扣留；不給予；抑制；保留；（稅）預扣
example: "Ten days the seer, as shrinking to reply / or name a victim, did the doom withhold."

definition: to become or make lean and wrinkled; shriveled and dried up
chinese: v. 使枯萎；使乾癟；adj. 乾癟的；枯萎的
example: In this context, “wizen” means lean and wrinkled by shrinkage as from age or illness.

definition: shriveled and wrinkled with age or illness
chinese: 乾癟的；滿是皺紋的；枯萎的
example: The wizened, old sorcerer took me under his wing and taught me everything he knew about magic.

definition: to move unsteadily from side to side; to waver; (of a voice) to tremble; an unsteady movement
chinese: v. 搖晃；擺動；猶豫不決；（聲音）顫抖；n. 搖晃
example: If you tighten the screws on the chair legs, it won’t wobble anymore and will be safe to sit on.

definition: great sorrow or distress; troubles (woes); misfortune
chinese: 悲痛；苦惱；災難；不幸
example: Woe to those who are obese in a society where slimness is the norm.

definition: to seek the support or favor of; to court romantically; (slang) pseudoscientific nonsense
chinese: v. 爭取；拉攏；追求；求愛；n. （俚）偽科學說法
example: Quantum physics has spawned a large amount of woo.

definition: concerned with material rather than spiritual matters; experienced and sophisticated
chinese: 世俗的；塵世的；老練的；世故的
example: There are five ways to emancipate themselves from the bond of worldly passions.

definition: to become or make worse
chinese: 惡化；變得更糟；使惡化
example: Critics say the pill could be diverted to illicit use and could worsen the country's opioid crisis.

definition: a long, complicated dispute; to argue noisily; to obtain by persistent effort; to herd livestock
chinese: n. 爭吵；爭執；糾紛；v. 爭吵；爭論；設法取得；放牧（牲畜）
example: This contract dispute turned into a legal wrangle.

definition: to pull away forcefully; to obtain with great effort; to distort the meaning of
chinese: 奪取；強奪；費力取得；曲解
example: One of the kids tried to wrest his scooter out of the officer's hands.

definition: in a very unhappy or unfortunate state; very poor in quality; contemptible; dejected
chinese: 悲慘的；可憐的；極差的；可惡的；沮喪的
example: You will never find a more wretched hive of scum and villainy.

definition: obstinately perverse in judgment or opinion; misguided
chinese: 執迷不悟的；固執錯誤的；判斷錯誤的
example: The passage describes its subject as wrongheaded, meaning obstinately perverse in judgment or opinion.

definition: using or expressing dry, mocking humor; (of a face) twisted in disgust or disappointment; bent or crooked
chinese: 苦笑的；挖苦的；冷面幽默的；扭曲的；歪斜的
example: "What an idyllic picture," he said with a wry smile.

definition: a person who fears or hates foreigners or foreign things
chinese: 仇外者；排外者；懼外者
example: I'm not a xenophobe, because I also hate my own ethnic group.

definition: a plant adapted to live with a limited water supply
chinese: 旱生植物
example: A xerophyte can survive where water is scarce for long periods.

definition: a burden or bond of oppression; a wooden crosspiece joining draft animals; a fitted part of a garment; to join or link; to harness
chinese: n. 束縛；壓迫；牛軛；（衣服）抵肩；v. 結合；連接；套上軛
example: The yoke of marriage is so heavy that it takes two people to carry it – sometimes three.

definition: an unsophisticated person from the countryside
chinese: 鄉巴佬；土包子；鄉下人
example: In this context, “yokel” refers to a person who is not very intelligent or interested in culture.

definition: great energy or enthusiasm for a cause or objective
chinese: 熱忱；熱情；熱心
example: But no disciple can be excused if he does not have zeal.

definition: a person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuit of political or religious ideals
chinese: 狂熱者；狂熱分子；極端分子
example: James was a right-wing zealot.

definition: marked by active interest and enthusiasm; fervent
chinese: 熱心的；熱誠的；狂熱的
example: The only thing worse than an idiot is a zealous idiot.

definition: the spirit or mood characteristic of an age or generation
chinese: 時代精神；時代思潮
example: In this context, “zeitgeist” refers to the spirit of the time; the spirit characteristic of an age or generation.

definition: the highest point of success or power; the point in the sky directly overhead
chinese: 頂峰；巔峰；（天文）天頂
example: His fame was at its zenith at that time.

definition: having an agreeably sharp or pungent taste; energetic and enthusiastic
chinese: 風味濃郁的；開胃的；有活力的；熱情的
example: The passage describes its subject as zesty, meaning having an agreeably pungent taste.
